type PresenceRow = typeof schema.crewPresence.$inferSelect;
function presenceDto(row: PresenceRow): z.infer<typeof presenceShape> {
  return {
    memberKey: row.memberKey, floor: row.floor, x: row.x, y: row.y,
    facing: (["down", "left", "right", "up"].includes(row.facing) ? row.facing : "down") as z.infer<typeof presenceFacing>,
    label: row.label, phase: row.phase, extra: row.extra, updatedAt: row.updatedAt.toISOString(),
  };
}

// decision, 2026-10-14). A Perfectly Paranoid story turned into a job is

// Hard caps — a quality filter, not a quota (fewer is fine): about 5 new
// stories per shelf per day, and within the Perfectly Paranoid shelf, up
// to 5 a day from declassified CIA/FBI files (inside the shelf cap, not
// on top of it).

const SVEN_STORY_DUTY = `STORY SHELVES — your second duty on every hunt run: alongside your ideas, file STORY candidates you actually found with save_sven_stories (this brief id, this job id). Stories are things you found, reported as found — never invented, never your own proposals; that is what keeps them separate from your ideas. Two shelves: "perfectly_paranoid" for stories fitting Perfectly Paranoid (UFOs, cryptids, disappearances, cold cases, weird science, strange or suppressed history) and "pulse_hq" for AI and business stories that could become Pulse HQ content or help the done-for-you offer. HARD CAP: about ${STORY_SHELF_DAILY_CAP} new stories per shelf per day across the whole day — a quality filter, not a quota; fewer is fine. DEDUPE: never file the same story twice — the same link, or the same story under another headline or from another outlet, is a duplicate, and the server checks against everything already filed, including stories Ben dismissed or already turned into jobs; dismissed stories never come back. Every story carries: its headline as found, the source name, the exact inspected HTTPS link, ONE plain line on why it fits, and a few plain topic tags. THE DECLASSIFIED BEAT: inside the Perfectly Paranoid shelf, specifically look through declassified CIA and FBI material (the CIA FOIA Reading Room / CREST releases, the FBI Vault) and file up to ${STORY_DECLASSIFIED_DAILY_CAP} story candidates a day from those files, inside the shelf's cap. For each one set isDeclassified true, name the agency (CIA or FBI), and give the document's plain title as documentTitle. A declassified document is a strong source, not a finished story — state the document plainly and never overstate what it says. Stories are CANDIDATES, never verification: filing one checks nothing, and Tom still verifies any story that becomes a job. Do not duplicate Tom's daily AI-news post — that is his finished crew post; these are raw work candidates. PLAIN LANGUAGE: every headline and fit line is written for a smart business owner who has never heard of AI agents — plain everyday words, no crew jargon, no internal document names. The server rejects any headline or fit line that uses crew jargon. In your result, report the story counts in plain words: how many stories you filed on each shelf, and how many of the Perfectly Paranoid ones came from declassified files.`;

function isRealLedgerDate(value: string): boolean {
  const [y = 0, m = 0, d = 0] = value.split("-").map(Number);
  if (!y || m < 1 || m > 12 || d < 1 || d > 31) return false;
  const probe = new Date(Date.UTC(y, m - 1, d));
  return probe.getUTCFullYear() === y && probe.getUTCMonth() === m - 1 && probe.getUTCDate() === d;
}
// The calendar day of an instant in Ben's timezone (the office runs on
// America/Vancouver, the same zone standing orders use) — a delivery made
// in the evening is recorded on the day Ben lived it, not the UTC day.
function vancouverDateString(date: Date): string {
  const parts = new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-CA", { timeZone: "America/Vancouver", year: "numeric", month: "2-digit", day: "2-digit" }).formatToParts(date);
  const part = (type: string) => parts.find((item) => item.type === type)?.value ?? "";
  return `${part("year")}-${part("month")}-${part("day")}`;
}

function presetValidationError(input: { title: string; notes: string; fillInLabel?: string | null }): string | null {
  const label = input.fillInLabel?.trim() ?? "";
  const hasToken = input.title.includes(PRESET_FILL_IN_TOKEN) || input.notes.includes(PRESET_FILL_IN_TOKEN);
  if (label && !hasToken) return `This preset asks for a fill-in (“${label}”) at start, so put the ${PRESET_FILL_IN_TOKEN} marker in the job title or the brief where that value should land.`;
  if (!label && hasToken) return `The ${PRESET_FILL_IN_TOKEN} marker needs a fill-in label — name what Ben should supply at start (for example “Source link”), or remove the marker.`;
  return null;
}

You must NOT recommend RPG Maker-related avenues in either lane — no plugins or plugin bundles, no MZ testing or ports, no tools for RPG Maker developers, no workbooks or tutorials drawn from Ben's RPG Maker work, no forums, communities, or marketplaces in the RPG Maker space, no game-dev music packs, no rescue calls or gigs in that world. const RPG_MAKER_IDEA_PATTERNS: RegExp[] = [
  /rpg[\s-]*maker/i,
  /rpgmaker/i,
  /damage[\s-]*formulas?\b/i,
  /skunk\s+(plugins|tools)\b/i,
  /\bplugins?\b[^.]{0,80}\b(rpg|maker|\bmz\b|\bmv\b|game[\s-]*dev)/i,
  /\b(mz|mv)\b[^.]{0,40}\b(testing|tests?|ports?|plugins?)\b/i,
  /\bgame[\s-]*dev(elopment)?\s+music\s+packs?\b/i,
  /\bmusic\s+packs?\b[^.]{0,60}\b(games?|rpg)\b/i,
];

function isRpgMakerRelatedIdea(idea: { title: string; rationale: string; nextStep: string }): boolean {
  const haystack = `${idea.title}\n${idea.rationale}\n${idea.nextStep}`;
  return RPG_MAKER_IDEA_PATTERNS.some((pattern) => pattern.test(haystack));
}

// Plain-language presentation rule (Ben's ruling, 2026-10-13): Sven's work
// was surfacing crew-internal language — internal document-type names like
// "Commercial Spec", raw .md filenames as labels, a bare "Work summary" —
// on the surfaces meant for Ben, and in a client office that text would be
// incomprehensible. The rule: everything a person reads from Sven (idea
// cards, and every document in the review package of a job his ideas
// launch) leads with plain human titles and a one-or-two-sentence plain
// summary, written for a smart business owner who has never heard of AI
// agents. This is a presentation rule only — the underlying files, the
// working content of documents, and verification rigor are unchanged. The
// rule lives in Sven's worker contract, in the visionary output contract,
// in the plan Remmy writes for a launched idea, and in the package
// contract every crew step of a Sven-launched job runs under — every one
// of those server-side injection points composes this one constant
// (Phase 4 consolidation). The seeded standing-order instruction carries
// the idea-card and story-card variants of the rule; those wordings now
// live in SVEN_IDEA_PLAIN_LANGUAGE_RULE and
// SVEN_STORY_CARD_PLAIN_LANGUAGE below, referenced from the order by
// token (migration 0032) and composed back in at consumption time.
// VERDICT FIRST (Ben's house rule, established 2026-10-13→18 and restated
// with force on 2026-10-18): every surface Ben decides from leads with the
// RESULT. The failure this fixes: a standard job's card face was the
// worker's descriptive summary prose ("This document settles whether…",
// "Read it to know why…") because the crew's own summary/document
// instructions told them to open by describing the document — what it is,
// what it is for, what the reader does with it — so the finding sat buried
// in a document behind the card and Ben had to hunt for it. The header
// already tells the reader what the thing is; the first sentence's job is
// the answer. This constant is the one wording of the rule: it is composed
// into Sven's plain-language rule (and through it his worker contract, the
// visionary output contract, and every Sven-package step), appended to
// every worker run in spawnWorker, and required of every step Remmy plans
// in planWork. No new face mechanism and no new checker carry it — the
// documents and results themselves are written verdict-first, and the
// existing faces (which lead with a document's own lead section / a
// result's opening) then show the verdict because that is what leads the
// text they already read.
const VERDICT_FIRST_RULE = `VERDICT FIRST — every result, summary, report, and document you produce for a person to read or decide from opens with its RESULT: the finding, verdict, decision, recommendation, or finished outcome, stated in its first sentence. The title already says what the thing is, so NEVER open by describing the document, the work, or yourself — no "This document settles…", no "This report covers…", no "Read it to know why…", no "I looked into…". State the answer first, then the one or two facts that carry it, then the supporting detail. A document whose job is to settle a question or make a call is a DECISION document: its title is followed immediately by a section headed exactly \`## Verdict\`, whose first sentence is the verdict itself, before any reasoning or evidence. If the honest result is that a question could not be settled or a thing could not be found, THAT is the verdict — state it first, plainly, and put what remains unknown after it. Finished copy that IS the deliverable (a post, a listing, an offer sheet) is exempt from describing itself at all: it simply starts, and any summary or result text around it still leads with the outcome.`;

// PLAIN SUMMARY FOR EVERY PIECE (Ben, 2026-10-19): the job-level verdict
// fix put the JOB's authored summary on the card face, but the CONTENTS
// rows under it still showed whatever a document happened to open with —
// crew metadata ("Reader: Walter, Research Department, Pulse HQ. Stage 1
// of 3…"), the research question restated as the answer's description, a
// verifier's method line cut off mid-word. Same doctrine as the stored
// job summary, one level down: every piece's plain summary is AUTHORED
// by the step that made the piece, captured onto the brief record at
// completion (set_brief_status), and served from storage — never
// manufactured by scraping the document when the card renders. This
// constant is the one wording of the rule: it is appended to every
// worker run in spawnWorker alongside VERDICT_FIRST_RULE, and the
// research stage contracts carry its document shape explicitly.
const PIECE_PLAIN_SUMMARY_RULE = `PLAIN SUMMARY FOR EVERY PIECE — every step's result, and every document a step saves, carries a short plain summary written for a person: one or two sentences, result first, saying what this piece FOUND or DID — the content, never the machinery. In a document it sits right after the plain human title heading, in a section headed exactly \`## In plain words\`. In a result that is not itself a document, it opens the result under that same heading — placed so it never breaks an exact-shape contract governing the piece (a publication-ready copy block stays verbatim and unbroken, and where a mandated opening summary already exists — a research brief's \`## SUMMARY\` short answer / verdict, a decision document's \`## Verdict\` — that opening IS the piece's plain summary and no second one is added). The office captures this summary onto the step's record when you finish and shows it on the job's card as the piece's description, so write the summary you would want a busy person to read. HARD BANS for these summaries: no role, department, or stage narration — never "Reader: Walter", "Verifier: Peter", "Stage 1 of 3", "Research Department", "Pulse HQ Method:", or anything like them; never restate the job's question or title as the description of the answer (state the answer); never describe the document or the work itself ("this document settles…", "this check lists…") — state what it found instead. Who did the work, which stage it was, and how it was checked belong in the working content below the summary, never in the summary itself. Finished copy that IS the deliverable (a post, a letter) is exempt inside its own text — its plain summary lives in the result around it, never inside the copy.`;

const SVEN_PLAIN_LANGUAGE_RULE = `PLAIN-LANGUAGE RULE — everything you write will be read by a smart business owner who has never heard of AI agents, and possibly by a client. Write every title, summary, and explanation in plain everyday words. Banned in anything a person will read: the word "agentic", talk of pipelines, briefs, steps, or deliverables as crew machinery, internal document-type names (no "spec", "brief", or "sheet" used as a codename), shortened or cut-off auto-titles, and file names used as titles. Every document you produce starts with a plain human title as its first heading — a short description of what the document is, like "The offer sheet (one page, ready to send)" — followed immediately by a section headed exactly \`## In plain words\` holding one or two plain sentences whose FIRST sentence states the document's result — its finding, verdict, recommendation, or finished outcome (verdict first: the title already says what the document is, so never describe the document itself, what it is for, or what the reader should read it to learn) — followed, only if needed, by the one fact that carries that result or what the reader does with it. ${VERDICT_FIRST_RULE} The working content after that section keeps its full rigor; only the titles, summaries, and reader-facing wording change.`;

const SVEN_PACKAGE_CONTRACT = `PLAIN-LANGUAGE PACKAGE RULE — this job came from one of Sven's ideas, so the finished package will be read by a person, possibly a client, who has never heard of AI agents. ${SVEN_PLAIN_LANGUAGE_RULE} This applies to every document and result you produce for this job, whatever your role: files keep their working names on disk, but inside each document the first heading is the plain human title, the \`## In plain words\` summary comes next, and your result text opens with the result itself — the finding, verdict, or finished outcome in its first sentence — before any detail about what was made.`;

// Standing-order fragment references (Phase 4 consolidation): the seeded
// sven-visionary-daily order stores these tokens in place of the rule
// texts above and of SVEN_RPG_MAKER_EXCLUSION, so each rule has exactly
// one source of truth — the server constant — while the order's stored
// text stays short. Every consumption point (the order DTO the UI reads,
// the dispatcher, and the on-demand hunt) expands the tokens through this
// one helper, so the effective instruction a worker receives, and the
// order text Ben reads, are byte-identical to the pre-consolidation text.
// Instructions without tokens pass through unchanged.
const STANDING_ORDER_FRAGMENTS: Array<readonly [string, string]> = [
  ["[[SVEN_RPG_MAKER_EXCLUSION]]", SVEN_RPG_MAKER_EXCLUSION],
  ["[[SVEN_IDEA_PLAIN_LANGUAGE_RULE]]", SVEN_IDEA_PLAIN_LANGUAGE_RULE],
  ["[[SVEN_STORY_CARD_PLAIN_LANGUAGE]]", SVEN_STORY_CARD_PLAIN_LANGUAGE],
];

export function expandStandingOrderInstruction(instruction: string): string {
  let expanded = instruction;
  for (const [token, text] of STANDING_ORDER_FRAGMENTS) expanded = expanded.split(token).join(text);
  return expanded;
}

const READER_JARGON_PATTERN = /\bagentic\b|\bpipeline\b|\bdeliverables?\b|\bbriefs?\b/i;

function readerJargonIn(text: string): boolean {
  return READER_JARGON_PATTERN.test(text);
}

// Clean a chunk of worker prose down to the plain text a summary card can
// show: strip Markdown decoration, drop metadata and file-path lines, and
// swap the worst crew jargon for everyday words (older documents predate
// the plain-language contract, so their extracted summaries get this light
// cleanup at presentation time; the stored files themselves are untouched).
function plainProse(value: string): string {
  return value
    .replace(/!\[[^\]]*\]\([^)]*\)/g, " ")
    .replace(/\[([^\]]+)\]\([^)]*\)/g, "$1")
    .replace(/`{1,3}([^`]*)`{1,3}/g, "$1")
    .replace(/[*_]{1,2}([^*_]+)[*_]{1,2}/g, "$1")
    .replace(/\bagentic\b/gi, "AI")
    .replace(/\bpipeline\b/gi, "process")
    .replace(/\bdeliverables?\b/gi, "finished work")
    .replace(/\s+/g, " ")
    .trim();
}

function firstSentences(value: string, maxSentences = 2, maxChars = 300): string | null {
  const cleaned = plainProse(value);
  if (!cleaned) return null;
  // Sentence boundaries are a terminator followed by a capitalized next
  // sentence or the end of the text — a naive split on "." mangles domain
  // names ("itch.io") and decimals ("$3.99") into fake sentence ends.
  const sentences = cleaned.match(/.+?[.!?]+(?:["')\]]+)?(?=\s+[A-Z0-9"'(]|\s*$)/g) ?? [cleaned];
  let out = "";
  let count = 0;
  for (const sentence of sentences) {
    const piece = sentence.trim();
    if (!piece) continue;
    if (count >= maxSentences) break;
    if (out && out.length + piece.length + 1 > maxChars) break;
    out = out ? `${out} ${piece}` : piece;
    count += 1;
    if (out.length >= maxChars) break;
  }
  out = out.trim();
  if (out.length > maxChars) out = `${out.slice(0, maxChars - 1).trimEnd()}…`;
  return out || null;
}

const PLAIN_SUMMARY_HEADING = /^#{1,6}\s*(?:in plain words|plain(?:[- ]language)? summary|summary|overview|the short version|tl;?dr)\b.*$/im;
const VERDICT_HEADING = /^#{1,6}\s*verdict\b.*$/im;
// A paragraph that opens with a verdict label ("Short answer: …",
// "**Short answer / verdict:** …") — the label itself is machinery, the
// prose after its colon is the finding the card face needs. The label may
// pair the two words with a slash, so validate everything before the
// first colon is label material only, then strip through the colon.
function stripVerdictLabel(paragraph: string): string | null {
  const para = paragraph.trim();
  if (!/^\*{0,2}(?:short answer|verdict)\b/i.test(para)) return null;
  const colon = para.indexOf(":");
  if (colon === -1 || colon > 48) return null;
  const labelPart = para.slice(0, colon).replace(/[*_]/g, "").trim();
  if (!/^(?:short answer|verdict)(?:\s*\/\s*(?:short answer|verdict))?$/i.test(labelPart)) return null;
  // When the bold markers wrap the label AND its colon ("**Verdict:** …"),
  // the colon just consumed was a bolded one — drop a bold closer left
  // sitting at the start of the remainder.
  return para.slice(colon + 1).trim().replace(/^\*\*\s*/, "") || null;
}

function sectionAfterHeading(normalized: string, heading: RegExpExecArray): string {
  const after = normalized.slice(heading.index + heading[0].length);
  const boundary = /\n#{1,6}\s+/.exec(after);
  return (boundary ? after.slice(0, boundary.index) : after).trim();
}

// Read the summary a finishing step AUTHORED in its own result, under the
// contract every job type now carries: a section headed "## SUMMARY"
// whose "Short answer / verdict" paragraph states the result in one or
// two plain sentences, verdict first (a "## Verdict" section's first prose
// paragraph serves the same purpose on question-settling documents). This
// is NOT a display-time scrape: it runs at completion, captures exactly
// the labelled paragraph the worker wrote as the job's summary, and the
// caller stores it on the task record — the card renders the stored
// value. Returns null when the result carries no authored summary, which
// the outcome check treats as a contract violation on bound jobs.
function extractAuthoredSummary(text: string | null | undefined): string | null {
  if (!text) return null;
  const normalized = text.replace(/\r\n/g, "\n");
  const verdictHeading = VERDICT_HEADING.exec(normalized);
  if (verdictHeading && verdictHeading.index !== undefined) {
    const section = sectionAfterHeading(normalized, verdictHeading);
    for (const part of section.split(/\n\s*\n/)) {
      const summary = firstSentences(part);
      if (summary) return summary;
    }
  }
  const summaryHeading = PLAIN_SUMMARY_HEADING.exec(normalized);
  if (summaryHeading && summaryHeading.index !== undefined) {
    const section = sectionAfterHeading(normalized, summaryHeading);
    const paragraphs = section.split(/\n\s*\n/).map((part) => part.trim()).filter(Boolean);
    for (const part of paragraphs) {
      const rest = stripVerdictLabel(part);
      if (rest) {
        const summary = firstSentences(rest);
        if (summary) return summary;
      }
    }
    // Unlabelled shape (the other job types' contracts): the section's
    // first prose paragraph IS the authored summary. A "Research
    // question:" lead is the question, not the answer — and bullet lists
    // (top facts, failed checking) are supporting detail, not the summary
    // — so neither counts as one.
    const first = paragraphs[0];
    if (first && !first.startsWith("-") && !first.startsWith("* ") && !/^research question\s*:/i.test(plainProse(first).replace(/^[-*+]\s+/, ""))) {
      const summary = firstSentences(first);
      if (summary) return summary;
    }
  }
  return null;
}

function isClaimTallySummary(value: string | null | undefined): boolean {
  if (!value) return false;
  const clean = plainProse(value);
  if (!clean) return false;
  return /^all\s+\d+\s+claims\s+held up\b/i.test(clean)
    || /^\d+\s+of\s+\d+\s+claims\s+(?:held up|documented)\b/i.test(clean)
    || /\bclaims held up as DOCUMENTED\b/i.test(clean)
    || /\b\d+\s+claims held up\b/i.test(clean);
}

// A raw deliverable dump is not an answer: a block of label:value
// metadata lines ("Business: … Town: … Contact route: … Mockup: …
// Screenshot: …") or a file-path listing extracted from a document's
// opening metadata must never displace the job's stored/package
// summary on the face.
function isRawMetadataDump(value: string | null | undefined): boolean {
  if (!value) return false;
  const clean = plainProse(value);
  if (!clean) return false;
  if (/^(?:business|town|contact route|status|mockup|screenshot)\s*:/i.test(clean)) return true;
  const labelCount = (clean.match(/\b(?:business|town|contact route|mockup|screenshot)\s*:/gi) ?? []).length;
  if (labelCount >= 2) return true;
  return false;
}

function isUsableAnswerCandidate(value: string | null | undefined): value is string {
  return Boolean(value) && !isClaimTallySummary(value) && !isRawMetadataDump(value) && !/^research question\s*:/i.test(value ?? "");
}

function primaryDeliverableScore(fileName: string): number {
  const lower = fileName.toLowerCase();
  if (lower.includes("brief")) return 0;
  if (lower.includes("report")) return 1;
  if (lower.includes("findings")) return 2;
  return 3;
}

// The answer's verdict paragraph, wherever it sits inside its section.
// In the research brief shape the "Short answer / verdict:" label shares
// a block with the preceding "Research question:" line (no blank line
// between them), so the paragraph-based extraction in
// extractAuthoredSummary cannot see it — this finder locates the label
// itself, then takes the prose that follows it up to the next section
// boundary (a blank line, a heading, a "Top …:" / "Failed checking:"
// label line, or a bullet list).
function extractShortAnswerVerdict(text: string | null | undefined): string | null {
  if (!text) return null;
  const normalized = text.replace(/\r\n/g, "\n");
  const verdictHeading = VERDICT_HEADING.exec(normalized);
  if (verdictHeading && verdictHeading.index !== undefined) {
    const section = sectionAfterHeading(normalized, verdictHeading);
    for (const part of section.split(/\n\s*\n/)) {
      const summary = firstSentences(part);
      if (summary) return summary;
    }
  }
  const labelRe = /(?:^|\n)[ \t]*(?:\*\*)?(?:short answer(?:\s*\/\s*verdict)?|verdict)(?:\*\*)?[ \t]*:[ \t]*(?:\*\*)?[ \t]*/i;
  const match = labelRe.exec(normalized);
  if (!match) return null;
  const rest = normalized.slice(match.index + match[0].length);
  const collected: string[] = [];
  for (const line of rest.split("\n")) {
    const trimmed = line.trim();
    if (collected.length > 0) {
      if (!trimmed) break;
      if (/^#{1,6}\s+/.test(trimmed)) break;
      if (/^(?:top\s+\d|top facts|failed checking|key facts)\b[^:]*:\s*$/i.test(trimmed)) break;
      if (/^[-*]\s+/.test(trimmed)) break;
    }
    collected.push(line);
  }
  const paragraph = collected.join(" ").trim();
  if (!paragraph) return null;
  return firstSentences(paragraph);
}

function extractAnswerCandidate(text: string | null | undefined): string | null {
  return extractShortAnswerVerdict(text) ?? extractAuthoredSummary(text);
}

// A piece summary a person can actually read (Ben, 2026-10-19): the hard
// bans of PIECE_PLAIN_SUMMARY_RULE, enforced at capture time. A summary
// that opens with role/department/stage narration ("Reader: Walter…",
// "Verifier: Peter…", "Stage 1 of 3…", a "Research Department" byline, a
// "Pulse HQ Method:" line), that restates the job's question instead of
// stating its answer, or that describes the document itself instead of
// its finding is NOT a plain summary — capture stores nothing for it and
// the read path falls back rather than serving machinery as a
// description.
function isReaderFacingSummary(summary: string): boolean {
  const clean = plainProse(summary);
  if (!clean) return false;
  if (/^(?:reader|verifier|researcher|author|worker|head of research)\s*:/i.test(clean)) return false;
  if (/\bstage\s+\d+\s+of\s+\d+\b/i.test(clean)) return false;
  if (/^(?:research question|the research question|question)\s*:/i.test(clean)) return false;
  if (/\bpulse hq method\s*:/i.test(clean)) return false;
  const firstSentence = clean.split(/(?<=[.!?])\s+/)[0] ?? clean;
  if (/\bresearch department\b/i.test(firstSentence)) return false;
  if (/^this (?:document|brief|report|extraction|check|summary|piece|gathering)\b[^.]*\b(?:settles|covers|describes|lists|presents|contains|explains|gathers|records|compiles)\b/i.test(clean)) return false;
  return true;
}

// Read the plain summary a step AUTHORED for its piece, under
// PIECE_PLAIN_SUMMARY_RULE: the prose under its "## In plain words" lead,
// or the mandated opening summary of an exact-shape piece (a research
// brief's "## SUMMARY" short answer / verdict, a "## Verdict" section) —
// both are the same extraction the job-level summary uses. This is NOT a
// display-time scrape: it runs at completion, captures exactly the lead
// the worker wrote as the piece's summary, and the caller stores it on
// the brief record — the card renders the stored value. Returns null
// when the result carries no authored plain summary, or the lead it
// carries breaks the hard bans above.
function extractPiecePlainSummary(text: string | null | undefined): string | null {
  const authored = extractAuthoredSummary(text);
  if (!authored) return null;
  return isReaderFacingSummary(authored) ? authored : null;
}

// LEGACY-ONLY summaries for pieces finished before stored piece
// summaries existed (Ben, 2026-10-19): the two research stage documents
// whose old extractions surfaced crew metadata on the card. These read
// the document's own STRUCTURE — the reader's stated claim count and
// topic headings, the verifier's own claim-by-claim labels — and state
// the content in plain words. They run only when a piece has neither a
// stored summary nor an authored lead of its own; no new piece ever
// reaches them.
function legacyReaderSummary(text: string): string | null {
  const count = /claims extracted\s*:\s*(\d+)/i.exec(text)?.[1] ?? null;
  const topics = Array.from(text.matchAll(/^###\s+(.+)$/gm))
    .map((match) => (match[1] ?? "").trim())
    .filter((topic) => topic.length > 0 && !/sources i could not read/i.test(topic))
    .slice(0, 6)
    .map((topic) => topic.charAt(0).toLowerCase() + topic.slice(1));
  if (!count && topics.length === 0) return null;
  const lead = count ? `${count} claims gathered from the sources, each with the evidence offered for it and its source link` : "The claims gathered from the sources, each with the evidence offered for it and its source link";
  return topics.length > 0 ? `${lead} — covering ${topics.join(", ")}.` : `${lead}.`;
}

function legacyVerifierSummary(text: string): string | null {
  const labeledList = text.split(/^#{1,6}\s*DO[-\s]?NOT[-\s]?PUBLISH/im)[0] ?? text;
  const counts = { documented: 0, mainstream: 0, fringe: 0, notVerified: 0 };
  for (const match of labeledList.matchAll(/(?:\*\*)?Claim\s+\d+\s*[—–-]\s*(DOCUMENTED|MAINSTREAM INTERPRETATION|FRINGE CLAIM|NOT VERIFIED)(?:\*\*)?/g)) {
    const label = match[1] ?? "";
    if (label === "DOCUMENTED") counts.documented += 1;
    else if (label === "MAINSTREAM INTERPRETATION") counts.mainstream += 1;
    else if (label === "FRINGE CLAIM") counts.fringe += 1;
    else if (label === "NOT VERIFIED") counts.notVerified += 1;
  }
  const total = counts.documented + counts.mainstream + counts.fringe + counts.notVerified;
  if (total === 0) return null;
  if (counts.documented === total) return `All ${total} claims held up — every claim was found in the source it cited and labelled DOCUMENTED. Nothing failed checking.`;
  const parts = [`${counts.documented} of ${total} claims held up as DOCUMENTED`];
  if (counts.mainstream > 0) parts.push(`${counts.mainstream} labelled mainstream interpretation`);
  if (counts.fringe > 0) parts.push(`${counts.fringe} labelled fringe claims`);
  if (counts.notVerified > 0) parts.push(`${counts.notVerified} could not be verified and sit on the do-not-publish list`);
  return `${parts.join("; ")}.`;
}

// The legacy fallback for ONE piece, chosen by what the piece is: a
// brief knows its worker, a file knows its name. Anything else gets the
// general extraction with the metadata filter (extractPlainSummary).
function legacyPieceSummary(text: string | null | undefined, hint: string): string | null {
  if (!text) return null;
  if (/reader[- ]extraction/i.test(hint) || hint === "walter") return legacyReaderSummary(text) ?? extractPlainSummary(text);
  if (/verifier[- ]check/i.test(hint) || hint === "peter") return legacyVerifierSummary(text) ?? extractPlainSummary(text);
  return extractPlainSummary(text);
}

// Extract the one-or-two-sentence plain summary a document leads with: the
// section under an "In plain words" / summary heading when the document has
// one (the shape the plain-language contract mandates), otherwise the first
// real paragraph of the document, skipping headings, metadata lines, rules,
// and file paths.
function extractPlainSummary(text: string | null | undefined): string | null {
  if (!text) return null;
  const normalized = text.replace(/\r\n/g, "\n");
  // A document's own authored summary lead (its "## In plain words"
  // section, a research brief's "## SUMMARY" short answer, a "## Verdict"
  // section) IS its plain summary — it wins over any first-paragraph
  // extraction, which is what used to surface a brief's "Research
  // question:" line as the description of its answer.
  const authored = extractAuthoredSummary(normalized);
  if (authored && isReaderFacingSummary(authored)) return authored;
  const heading = PLAIN_SUMMARY_HEADING.exec(normalized);
  if (heading && heading.index !== undefined) {
    const after = normalized.slice(heading.index + heading[0].length);
    const boundary = /\n#{1,6}\s+/.exec(after);
    const section = (boundary ? after.slice(0, boundary.index) : after).trim();
    const summary = firstSentences(section.split(/\n\s*\n/).find((part) => part.trim()) ?? "");
    if (summary) return summary;
  }
  for (const block of normalized.split(/\n\s*\n/)) {
    const lines = block.split("\n").map((line) => line.trim()).filter(Boolean);
    const prose = lines.filter((line) => {
      // Test the line with bullet markers and bold stripped, so metadata
      // bullets like "- Brief id: …" / "- Job id: …" are recognized as the
      // internal bookkeeping they are and never lead a plain summary.
      const stripped = line.replace(/^[-*+]\s+/, "").replace(/\*\*/g, "");
      return !line.startsWith("#") && !line.startsWith("---") && !line.startsWith("|") && !line.startsWith(">")
        && !/^(?:prepared|written|author|date|file|source|status|job|step|worker|brief id|job id|reader|verifier|method|stage|head of research|inputs synthesised|inputs synthesized)\s*:/i.test(stripped)
        && !/\bstage\s+\d+\s+of\s+\d+\b/i.test(stripped)
        && !stripped.endsWith(":")
        && !/^(?:IMAGE PROVENANCE|Sources?|https?:\/\/)/i.test(stripped)
        && !/^[-\w./ ]+\.(?:md|txt|png|jpe?g|webp)$/i.test(stripped);
    }).join(" ");
    if (!prose || prose.replace(/[^a-zA-Z]/g, "").length < 24) continue;
    const summary = firstSentences(prose.replace(/^[-*]\s+/, ""));
    if (summary) return summary;
  }
  return null;
}

function cleanedFileTitle(fileName: string): string {
  const stem = fileName.replace(/\.[^.]+$/, "").replace(/[-_]+/g, " ").trim();
  return stem.replace(/\b\w/g, (character) => character.toUpperCase());
}

// Map an internal deliverable filename to the plain human title a reader
// sees. Keyword rules cover the document kinds Sven-launched jobs actually
// produce; the fallback drops the repeated job-title tail workers append to
// filenames (that tail is what produced titles like "Commercial Spec 5 Tool
// Stack Cleanup Audit") and keeps the cleaned name in sentence form.
function humanTitleForDeliverable(fileName: string, kind: "image" | "markdown" | "text" | "document" | "video", taskTitle: string): string {
  const normalized = fileName.toLowerCase().replace(/\.[^.]+$/, "").replace(/[-_]+/g, " ").trim();
  if (kind !== "image") {
    if (/\boffer\b/.test(normalized)) return "The offer sheet (one page, ready to send)";
    if (/\bcommercial\b|\bdeal terms\b|\bpricing\b|\bprice list\b/.test(normalized)) return "The deal terms in plain words";
    if (/\bverified\b|\bfact/.test(normalized)) return "What we checked and what turned out to be true";
    if (/\bproposal\b/.test(normalized)) return "The proposal (ready to send)";
    if (/\baudit\b|\breview of\b/.test(normalized)) return "What we looked at, and what we found";
    if (/\blisting\b/.test(normalized)) return "The listing words (ready to copy)";
    if (/\bresearch\b|\bfindings\b|\breport\b/.test(normalized)) return "What we found, and how we know";
    if (/\bpost\b|\bcopy\b|\bcaption\b/.test(normalized)) return "The finished writing (ready to use)";
    if (/\bsummary\b|\boverview\b/.test(normalized)) return "A short summary of the work";
    if (/\bplan\b/.test(normalized)) return "The plan, in plain words";
    if (/\bcontract\b|\bagreement\b|\bterms\b/.test(normalized)) return "The agreement in plain words";
  }
  let title = cleanedFileTitle(fileName);
  const taskWords = taskTitle.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, " ").trim().split(" ").filter(Boolean);
  const titleWords = title.toLowerCase().split(" ").filter(Boolean);
  if (taskWords.length >= 2 && titleWords.length > taskWords.length) {
    const tail = titleWords.slice(titleWords.length - taskWords.length);
    if (tail.join(" ") === taskWords.join(" ")) {
      title = title.split(" ").slice(0, titleWords.length - taskWords.length).join(" ").trim() || title;
    }
  }
  return title || "A document from this job";
}

// Plain human label for a crew member's finished-work entry in a review
// package — replaces the bare internal "Work summary" label on packages a
// person reads.
function humanTitleForBrief(assignee: string, status: string): string {
  if (status === "failed") return "A note about what went wrong";
  switch (assignee) {
    case "scout": return "What was checked and what turned out to be true";
    case "quill": return "The finished writing";
    case "forge": return "What was made for you";
    case "ledger": return "Sven's summary, in plain words";
    case "walter": return "The sources that were gathered";
    case "peter": return "What held up under checking";
    case "olivia": return "The drafted posts";
    default: return "What was done, in plain words";
  }
}

// The lead summary for an idea card: the stored plain summary when Sven
// supplied one, otherwise the first sentences of the rationale, lightly
// cleaned — older ideas predate the column but still lead with plain words.
function plainSummaryForIdea(row: typeof schema.visionaryIdeas.$inferSelect): string {
  const stored = row.plainSummary?.trim();
  if (stored) return stored;
  return firstSentences(row.rationale) ?? "One of Sven's ideas — the reasoning below explains what it is and why it is worth doing.";
}

];

const workPlanShape = z.object({
  reason: z.string().trim().min(1).max(240),
  steps: z.array(z.object({
    assignee: crewMemberId,
    title: z.string().trim().min(1).max(120),
    instructions: z.string().trim().min(1).max(5000),
  })).min(1).max(5),
});

type PlanStep = z.infer<typeof workPlanShape>["steps"][number];

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// OUTCOME CONTRACTS PER JOB TYPE (Ben, 2026-10-15).
//
// The failure this fixes: a Standard job (an outreach pack of contact-form
// letters) was routed through the social-post pipeline and inherited a
// Perfectly Paranoid voice template the writer had to overrule by judgment,
// a hashtag finisher block on a document, and an image step that generated
// an unneeded stock photo. Judgment saved it; the system must not depend on
// judgment — least of all on deliverables people pay for.
//
// So every job created from now on is BOUND AT CREATION to the outcome
// contract of its job type. A contract declares: which crew steps may run,
// the deliverable's shape, the voice, which finishers are allowed or
// forbidden, and how the job exits. Triage plans only the steps the
// contract declares, every worker brief carries the contract text, and
// before a finished deliverable can surface in Ready for You it is checked
// against the contract (validateDeliverableAgainstContract): a violation
// bounces it back for rework with the reason recorded, before Ben sees it.
// Client-tagged jobs get the strictest enforcement — a deliverable still
// carrying a violation cannot be approved into a client's delivery package.
//
// SCOPE GUARD: contracts bind only jobs created after this build. Tasks
// with job_type NULL (everything already in flight, standing orders, lab
// sub-cases, delivery-package jobs) keep their current plans and are never
// checked — the validators below all return "no contract" for them.
type JobTypeValue = z.infer<typeof jobType>;

export interface OutcomeContract {
  jobType: JobTypeValue;
  label: string;
  stepsSummary: string;
  deliverableShape: string;
  voice: string;
  // "none": no image step and no attached image, ever. "brief": an image
  // step only when the job's own brief explicitly asks for one (computed
  // per job into imageAllowed). "post": the post package's one image is
  // part of the deliverable. "image_or_link": Olivia's per-post rule.
  // "designed": designed visuals are the product.
  imageRule: "none" | "brief" | "post" | "image_or_link" | "designed";
  // "forbidden_except_posts" is the Standard carve-out (Ben, 2026-10-15):
  // documents, letters, and reports get NO hashtag finisher, but finished
  // social posts DO end with their strongest topic hashtags — and a post
  // deliverable without them is a violation. Which side applies is
  // computed per job into postsRequested.
  hashtagRule: "forbidden" | "required" | "inside_copy_only" | "forbidden_except_posts";
  ppVoiceRule: "required" | "forbidden" | "brief";
  exitRule: string;
  requiredElements: string[];
  forbiddenElements: string[];
  strict: boolean;
  // Per-job computed allowances (standard jobs only): whether THIS job's
  // brief explicitly asked for an image, and whether it explicitly asked
  // for the Perfectly Paranoid voice/template.
  imageAllowed: boolean;
  ppVoiceAllowed: boolean;
  // Per-job computed (standard jobs): whether THIS job's brief asks for
  // finished social posts — the hashtag carve-out's post side.
  postsRequested: boolean;
}

// Does this job's own brief explicitly ask for an image? Standard jobs get
// an image step ONLY on an explicit ask — a verb of making/asking tied to
// an image-like deliverable, an explicit "image step", or a mockup (a
// visual deliverable the brief itself names). Mere mentions of images, or
// a social platform's name, do not count: the outreach pack that motivated
// outcome contracts mentioned Facebook pages throughout and asked for no
// image at all.
export function briefExplicitlyRequestsImage(text: string): boolean {
  return /\bimage step\b/i.test(text)
    || /\bmock\s?up\b/i.test(text)
    || /\b(?:include|add|create|make|generate|produce|design|attach|supply|provide|need|want|request|including|adds?|creates?|makes?|generates?|produces?|designs?|attaches?|supplies?|provides?|needs?|wants?|requests?)\b[^.!?\n]{0,60}\b(?:an?|the|one|some|each)?\s*(?:image|picture|photo|photograph|illustration|graphic|visual)s?\b/i.test(text)
    || /\bwith (?:an?|the) (?:image|picture|photo|photograph|illustration|graphic|visual)\b/i.test(text);
}

// Does this job's own brief explicitly request the Perfectly Paranoid
// voice or template? Only a direct naming of Perfectly Paranoid as the
// wanted voice/template counts — a Standard job ABOUT Perfectly Paranoid
// (a report on the page, say) does not inherit its voice.
export function briefExplicitlyRequestsPpVoice(text: string): boolean {
  return /perfectly paranoid[^.!?\n]{0,60}\b(?:voice|template|style|tone)\b/i.test(text)
    || /\b(?:voice|template|style|tone)\b[^.!?\n]{0,60}perfectly paranoid/i.test(text)
    || /\bin the (?:locked )?perfectly paranoid\b/i.test(text);
}

// Does this job's own brief ask for finished social posts? The Standard
// hashtag carve-out turns on exactly this: a brief that asks for posts
// (a count of posts, posts for a named platform, or a write/draft/posts
// instruction) gets posts that END with hashtags; a brief that asks for a
// document, letter, or report — even one that merely mentions a Facebook
// page or the word "post" in passing — does not.
export function briefExplicitlyRequestsPosts(text: string): boolean {
  return /\bsocial(?:\s+media)?\s+posts?\b/i.test(text)
    || /\bfinished posts?\b/i.test(text)
    || /\b\d+\s+(?:finished\s+)?(?:facebook\s+|social\s+|instagram\s+)?posts?\b/i.test(text)
    || /\b(?:facebook|instagram|threads|linkedin)\s+posts?\b/i.test(text)
    || /\bposts?\s+for\s+(?:facebook|instagram|threads|linkedin|social)\b/i.test(text)
    || /\b(?:write|draft|create|produce|make|deliver|prepare|compose)\b[^.!?\n]{0,60}\b(?:\d+\s+)?posts?\b/i.test(text)
    || /\bposts?\s+(?:pack|batch|set|series)\b/i.test(text);
}

// Does a client-tagged job require its client report deliverable? Every
// client_report job does, and so does any other client job whose own
// brief (title + notes, as created) includes a report.
export function briefIncludesReport(title: string, notes: string): boolean {
  return /\breport\b/i.test(`${title}\n${notes}`);
}

export function outcomeContractFor(type: JobTypeValue, briefText: string, clientTagged: boolean): OutcomeContract {
  const base = OUTCOME_CONTRACTS[type];
  return {
    ...base,
    jobType: type,
    imageAllowed: base.imageRule === "brief" ? briefExplicitlyRequestsImage(briefText) : base.imageRule !== "none",
    ppVoiceAllowed: base.ppVoiceRule === "required" ? true : base.ppVoiceRule === "brief" ? briefExplicitlyRequestsPpVoice(briefText) : false,
    postsRequested: type === "standard" ? briefExplicitlyRequestsPosts(briefText) : false,
    strict: base.strict || clientTagged,
  };
}

export function parseOutcomeContract(raw: string | null | undefined): OutcomeContract | null {
  if (!raw) return null;
  try {
    const parsed = JSON.parse(raw) as OutcomeContract;
    if (!parsed || typeof parsed !== "object" || !parsed.jobType || !OUTCOME_CONTRACTS[parsed.jobType]) return null;
    return { ...outcomeContractFor(parsed.jobType, "", false), ...parsed };
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}

export function contractForTask(task: Pick<typeof schema.tasks.$inferSelect, "jobType" | "outcomeContract"> | null | undefined): OutcomeContract | null {
  if (!task?.jobType) return null;
  return parseOutcomeContract(task.outcomeContract) ?? outcomeContractFor(task.jobType, "", Boolean((task as { clientId?: string | null }).clientId));
}

// The contract text every worker brief of a contract-bound job carries, so
// a worker starting fresh knows this job's shape, voice, and finishers —
// and knows the finished deliverable is checked against it before it
// surfaces. For non-PP types it states the exclusions plainly (the PP
// template/voice itself is never included — only the locked PP contract
// carries it).
// Handoffs append the completed-work context to the next brief's notes and
// cap the result at 20,000 characters — a long upstream result can push the
// contract block (stamped at creation, mid-notes) out of the kept tail.
// This re-stamps the block at the very END whenever a handoff rewrites a
// contract-bound brief's notes, so the contract survives every handoff and
// always sits where truncation cannot reach it.
export function ensureContractBlock(task: Pick<typeof schema.tasks.$inferSelect, "jobType" | "outcomeContract"> | null | undefined, notes: string): string {
  const contract = contractForTask(task);
  if (!contract || notes.includes("OUTCOME CONTRACT —")) return notes;
  return `${notes}\n\n${contractBriefBlock(contract)}`;
}

export function contractBriefBlock(contract: OutcomeContract): string {
  const imageLine = contract.imageRule === "none"
    ? "Images: NO image step runs on this job and no image is attached to the deliverable — ever."
    : contract.imageRule === "brief"
      ? contract.imageAllowed
        ? "Images: this job's brief explicitly asks for an image, so image work the brief calls for may run — and nothing beyond it."
        : "Images: NO image step runs on this job — the brief does not ask for an image, so none is created, sourced, or attached."
      : contract.imageRule === "post"
        ? "Images: exactly one image is part of the deliverable — a real photograph preferred, provenance recorded."
        : contract.imageRule === "image_or_link"
          ? "Images: every post carries a link in its text or an attached generated image — never neither."
          : "Images: the designed visuals ARE this job's product — build them to the concept; never invent a client brand asset (a missing one stays a marked PLACEHOLDER).";
  const hashtagLine = contract.hashtagRule === "forbidden"
    ? "Finishers: NO hashtag finisher and no hashtag block anywhere in the deliverable."
    : contract.hashtagRule === "required"
      ? "Finishers: the finished post ENDS with its hashtag block — top topic-specific tags only, no filler tags, nothing after the block."
      : contract.hashtagRule === "forbidden_except_posts"
        ? contract.postsRequested
          ? "Finishers — HASHTAG CARVE-OUT: this job's brief asks for finished social posts, so EACH post ENDS with its strongest topic hashtags — top topic-specific tags only, no filler, nothing after the block — and a post without that ending block breaks this contract. The no-hashtag rule still applies in full to documents, letters, and reports: if this job also produces one of those, it gets NO hashtag finisher."
          : "Finishers — HASHTAG CARVE-OUT: NO hashtag finisher and no hashtag block anywhere in this deliverable. The no-hashtag rule applies to documents, letters, and reports (this job's shapes). Carve-out, for the record: finished social posts would end with their strongest topic hashtags — but this job's brief does not ask for posts, so no hashtags appear here."
        : "Finishers: hashtags appear only inside copy items that are themselves social posts — never as a pack-level finisher block.";
  const voiceLine = contract.ppVoiceRule === "required"
    ? "Voice: the locked Perfectly Paranoid voice in this brief governs the copy — it applies to this job only."
    : contract.ppVoiceAllowed
      ? "Voice: this job's brief explicitly requests the Perfectly Paranoid voice, so that voice may be used for this job's copy — nothing else from the post pipeline (no automatic image step) comes with it; finishers still follow this contract's hashtag carve-out below."
      : "Voice: the Perfectly Paranoid template and voice do NOT apply to this job — never use them, even if the subject touches Perfectly Paranoid.";
  return [
    `OUTCOME CONTRACT — ${contract.label.toUpperCase()} (bound at creation from this job's type; it governs every step of this job, and the finished deliverable is checked against it before it can surface${contract.strict ? " — this is a client deliverable, so enforcement is strictest: any violation blocks it" : ""}):`,
    `- Steps that may run: ${contract.stepsSummary}`,
    `- Deliverable: ${contract.deliverableShape}`,
    `- Voice: ${contract.voice} ${voiceLine}`,
    `- ${imageLine}`,
    `- ${hashtagLine}`,
    `- Required: ${contract.requiredElements.join("; ")}.`,
    `- Finishing summary: the job's FINAL step ends its result with a section headed "## SUMMARY" whose "Short answer / verdict" paragraph states the result in one or two plain sentences, verdict first. The office stores that paragraph on the job record as the summary Ben reads on the card — a final finish without it is bounced by the outcome check (the finished work carries no summary).`,
    `- Forbidden: ${contract.forbiddenElements.join("; ")}.`,
    `- Exit: ${contract.exitRule}`,
    "Anything outside this contract is out of scope for this job, even if another job type would normally include it. If the brief and this contract ever conflict, the contract wins and you note the conflict in your result.",
  ].join("\n");
}

// A step whose whole job is producing an image for something else (a post
// image, an illustration) — as opposed to a step that builds the briefed
// deliverable itself (a website, a mockup, a document, a tool). Used by
// triage (a contract that forbids image steps never spawns one) and by the
// contract check (receipts name image steps plainly).
export function isImageProductionStep(step: { assignee: string; title: string; instructions?: string }): boolean {
  // Judge the step by its OWN text: the outcome-contract block stamped onto
  // every brief of a contract-bound job talks about image steps ("NO image
  // step runs on this job"), and that stamped text must never make an
  // ordinary research or writing step look like an image step.
  const ownInstructions = (step.instructions ?? "").split("OUTCOME CONTRACT —")[0];
  const text = `${step.title}\n${ownInstructions}`;
  if (/\b(?:website|web site|webpage|web page|site|app|tool|code|coding|document|spreadsheet|deck|presentation|mockup|mock-up|prototype|build the|develop)\b/i.test(text) && !/\bpost image\b|\bimage step\b/i.test(step.title)) return false;
  return step.assignee === "forge" && /\b(?:image|picture|photo|photograph|illustration|graphic|visual)s?\b/i.test(text) && /\b(?:create|make|generate|produce|design|find|source|prepare)\b/i.test(text)
    || /\bpost image\b|\bimage step\b|create the (?:post )?image/i.test(step.title);
}

export function isFinisherStep(step: { title: string; instructions?: string }): boolean {
  return /\bhashtag(?:s| block| finisher)?\b[^.]{0,30}\bstep\b/i.test(step.title) || /^\s*(?:add|write|finish with)\b[^.]{0,30}\bhashtag/i.test(step.title) || /\bfinisher step\b/i.test(step.title);
}

// Hashtag detection — ONE shared implementation (Phase 4 consolidation).
// Three verdicts used to be computed by three separate regex/logic
// copies: findHashtagBlock (a block anywhere in a document),
// trailingHashtagBlock (a closing block), and hashtagBlockError's own
// trailing-line scan (the save/completion gate). They now share the two
// primitives below — the labelled-heading test and the trailing
// hashtag-only line run — so a wording or pattern fix lands in exactly
// one place and every checker agrees. Each verdict keeps its own
// semantics on top of the primitives: findHashtagBlock also accepts a
// bulleted or comma-separated block line anywhere in the text,
// trailingHashtagBlock requires at least two tags in the closing run,
// and hashtagBlockError applies the per-platform tag counts.
const HASHTAG_HEADING_PATTERN = /^#{1,6}\s*hashtags?\b/im;
const HASHTAG_ONLY_LINE_PATTERN = /^#[\p{L}\p{N}_]+(?:\s+#[\p{L}\p{N}_]+)*$/u;

export function hasHashtagHeading(text: string): boolean {
  return HASHTAG_HEADING_PATTERN.test(text);
}

// The closing run of hashtag-only lines at the end of a text (each line
// trimmed, empty lines ignored), in reading order. Empty when the text
// does not end on hashtags.
export function trailingHashtagLines(text: string): string[] {
  const lines = text.replace(/\r\n/g, "\n").split("\n").map((line) => line.trim()).filter((line) => line.length > 0);
  const trailing: string[] = [];
  for (let i = lines.length - 1; i >= 0; i -= 1) {
    const line = lines[i] ?? "";
    if (HASHTAG_ONLY_LINE_PATTERN.test(line)) trailing.unshift(line);
    else break;
  }
  return trailing;
}

// A hashtag block: a line (or closing run of lines) containing only
// hashtags — two or more tags as a block, or a labelled hashtag section.
// A single inline hashtag inside prose is not a finisher and never flags.
export function findHashtagBlock(text: string): boolean {
  const normalized = text.replace(/\r\n/g, "\n");
  if (hasHashtagHeading(normalized)) return true;
  for (const rawLine of normalized.split("\n")) {
    const line = rawLine.trim().replace(/^[-*]\s+/, "");
    if (/^(?:#[\p{L}\p{N}_]+[\s,]+){1,}#[\p{L}\p{N}_]+$/u.test(line)) return true;
  }
  return false;
}

// Distinctive markers of the Perfectly Paranoid template in a deliverable:
// its mandated stakes-beat opener and its voice heading. (The phrase is
// the PP structure's signature — a non-PP deliverable carrying it is
// wearing the template, whatever its subject.)
const PP_TEMPLATE_MARKERS: RegExp[] = [
  /why is this a big deal\?/i,
  /PERFECTLY PARANOID VOICE — LOCKED/i,
  /publication-ready post copy/i,
];

export function findPpTemplateMarkers(text: string): boolean {
  return PP_TEMPLATE_MARKERS.some((pattern) => pattern.test(text));
}

// Ben's source-first image ruling (office-wide default): agents use real-world
// photographs of real things whenever one exists; AI generation is the fallback
// only. Provenance is mandatory either way, recorded in image-provenance.md in
// the job folder AND as an IMAGE PROVENANCE line in the worker's result, so Ben
// can see which happened on the approval card. Out of scope by Ben's ruling:
// print-on-demand artwork (original art by definition) and Olivia's X-post
// office art.
// Aspect control — one-off override (Ben, 2026-10-14): when the approver's
// special instructions for an IMAGE rework explicitly say to generate the
// image directly, that instruction wins for that run only — it must not be
// silently overridden by the source-first default appended to worker runs.
// send_back_task stamps this marker into the rework brief when it detects
// the instruction; mediaProcessingPolicy reads the same marker and returns
// a policy that agrees with the brief. The marker never appears in ordinary
// briefs, so the standing default is unchanged for every other run, and
// provenance stays mandatory either way (a generated image is recorded as
// AI-generated; a found photo keeps its source record).
const REWORK_GENERATE_DIRECT_MARKER = "ONE-OFF OVERRIDE — GENERATE DIRECTLY (this run only)";

function hasExplicitGenerateDirective(feedback: string): boolean {
  const text = feedback.toLowerCase();
  return /\b(generate|create|make|draw|produce|render)\b[^.!?\n]{0,50}\b(image|picture|photo|photograph|illustration|artwork|visual|one|it)\b/.test(text)
    || /\bjust generate\b/.test(text)
    || /\bgenerate (it|one|directly)\b/.test(text)
    || (/\b(skip|don't|do not|no need to|instead of)\b[^.!?\n]{0,40}\b(search|searching|find|finding|look for|sourcing)\b/.test(text) && /\b(image|picture|photo|generate)\b/.test(text));
}

const SOURCE_FIRST_IMAGE_RULE = `SOURCE-FIRST IMAGE RULE — office-wide default: when this job needs an image of a real thing (a real place, event, object, artifact, animal, person, or phenomenon), do NOT generate one first. First search the web for a suitable real-world photograph of the actual thing, preferring public-domain and freely licensed sources — NASA imagery, Wikimedia Commons, and other Creative Commons material. Download the chosen photograph into this job's folder, open it, and inspect it before using it: it must genuinely depict the thing the work is about and be clean enough to publish (no watermark, no misleading crop). AI image generation is the FALLBACK, used only when no suitable real photograph can be found. PROVENANCE IS MANDATORY either way, recorded in BOTH of these places: (1) a file named image-provenance.md in this job's folder, with one block per delivered image in exactly this shape — a line "Image: <exact image file name>", a line "Kind: real" or "Kind: generated", and for a real photograph also a line "Source: <exact source URL, copied character-for-character>" and a line "License: <license basis, e.g. NASA / public domain, or Wikimedia Commons CC BY-SA>"; a generated fallback block has only the Image and Kind lines. (2) Your result, as one line per image: "IMAGE PROVENANCE: Real photograph — <file name> — Source: <source URL> — License: <license basis>" for a real photograph, or "IMAGE PROVENANCE: AI-generated (no suitable real image found) — <file name>" for a generated fallback. Ben sees this provenance on the approval card; an image without recorded provenance is not done. This rule never applies to print-on-demand artwork, which is original art by definition.`;

// Hashtag block rule — Ben's rule (2026-10-14): EVERY finished post ends
// with a hashtag block, no exceptions — Perfectly Paranoid posts, standard
// social posts, and Olivia's X drafts. The tags are the TOP hashtags for
// that post's specific topic: the strongest, most-searched niche tags for
// the subject, chosen from the post's own content — never a fixed generic
// set pasted onto everything, and never filler / reach-bait tags. A post
// without its hashtag block is UNFINISHED, with the same standing as
// Olivia's image-or-link requirement: it lives in each writer's contract
// (Johnny for Facebook/social, Olivia for X), in their Definition of Done
// checklists, in the run-time output contracts, and in server-side
// completion gates (save_x_posts rejects X drafts; set_brief_status
// rejects a Perfectly Paranoid / social copy step). Applies to new work
// only — posts already approved or queued are not retroactively rewritten.
export const HASHTAG_FILLER_TAGS = new Set([
  "fyp", "foryou", "foryoupage", "foryourpage", "viral", "goviral", "trending", "trendingnow",
  "explore", "explorepage", "blowup", "follow", "followme", "follow4follow", "followforfollow",
  "likeforlike", "like4like", "instagood", "photooftheday", "repost", "share", "spam",
]);
export const HASHTAG_RULE_FACEBOOK = `HASHTAG BLOCK — REQUIRED ON EVERY FINISHED POST, NO EXCEPTIONS (Ben's rule, 2026-10-14): the post ENDS with a hashtag block — a final line (or lines) containing ONLY hashtags, placed after the closing hook / call to action, with nothing after it. A post without that ending block is UNFINISHED and must not be marked done. Use 3–5 hashtags that are the TOP, strongest, most-searched niche tags for THIS post's specific topic — chosen from the post's actual subject, names, places, and themes, never a fixed generic set pasted onto every post. NO filler or reach-bait tags: never #fyp, #foryou, #foryoupage, #viral, #trending, #explore, #explorepage, or any tag that does not name this post's topic. Tight and strong beats long and generic.`;
export const HASHTAG_RULE_X = `HASHTAG BLOCK — REQUIRED ON EVERY FINISHED X POST, NO EXCEPTIONS (Ben's rule, 2026-10-14): the post ENDS with a hashtag block — a final line containing ONLY hashtags, placed after the call to action, with nothing after it. The hashtags count inside the 280-character limit, so keep them few and strong: 1–3 hashtags that are the TOP, strongest, most-searched niche tags for THIS post's specific topic — chosen from the post's actual content, never a fixed generic set pasted onto every post. NO filler or reach-bait tags: never #fyp, #foryou, #foryoupage, #viral, #trending, #explore, #explorepage, or any tag that does not name this post's topic. A post without that ending block is UNFINISHED and the server rejects the save.`;
export function extractHashtags(text: string): string[] {
  return Array.from(text.matchAll(/#[\p{L}\p{N}_]+/gu), (match) => match[0]);
}
export function hashtagBlockError(text: string, platform: "facebook" | "x"): string | null {
  const trimmed = text.trim();
  if (!trimmed) return "the post is empty — it has no hashtag block";
  const all = extractHashtags(trimmed);
  if (all.length === 0) return "the post has no hashtags — every finished post must end with a hashtag block of topic-strong tags";
  const filler = all.find((tag) => HASHTAG_FILLER_TAGS.has(tag.slice(1).toLowerCase()));
  if (filler) return `the post uses the filler / reach-bait tag ${filler} — remove filler tags and use only the top topic-specific tags for this post's subject`;
  const trailing = trailingHashtagLines(trimmed);
  if (trailing.length === 0) return "the post does not END with a hashtag block — put the hashtags together as the final line(s), after the closing hook / call to action, with nothing after them";
  const blockTags = extractHashtags(trailing.join(" "));
  if (platform === "x") {
    if (blockTags.length < 1 || blockTags.length > 3) return `the ending hashtag block has ${blockTags.length} tag${blockTags.length === 1 ? "" : "s"} — on X keep it few and strong: 1–3 top topic tags, counted inside the 280-character limit`;
  } else {
    if (blockTags.length < 3 || blockTags.length > 5) return `the ending hashtag block has ${blockTags.length} tag${blockTags.length === 1 ? "" : "s"} — on Facebook use a tight set of 3–5 top topic-specific tags`;
  }
  return null;
}

const PERFECTLY_PARANOID_VOICE = `PERFECTLY PARANOID VOICE — LOCKED (Ben approved, 2026-10-13). This voice governs ONLY this Perfectly Paranoid copy step; it replaces any casual, curious, or playful tone instruction for this step.

// Escalation rule (Ben, 2026-10-14 — "double duty on the tricky claims"):

// high, there is exactly ONE escalation per job, and the sub-case is
// internal — it never appears in Ready for You and needs no approval.
export const ESCALATION_HEADING = "ESCALATED TO RESEARCH DEPT";
export const ESCALATION_RULE = `ESCALATION TO THE RESEARCH DEPARTMENT — high bar, use sparingly:
You may send specific claims upstairs to the Research Department (Walter gathers, Peter verifies claim by claim, the Claim-checker grades, Tom synthesizes) for a second, deeper check — but ONLY claims that meet at least one of these tests:
- contested (credible sources disagree), OR
- extraordinary (surprising, viral, or hard to believe on its face), OR
- high-stakes if wrong (the job would publish or act on it and being wrong would mislead people), OR
- your downstairs pass could not verify it against a source you opened and read.
Ordinary claims NEVER escalate. If a claim is routine and you verified it, it stays downstairs — do not send everything upstairs, and do not escalate a whole topic, only the specific claims that clear the bar above.
HOW TO ESCALATE: in your result, add a section headed exactly "${ESCALATION_HEADING}" and list each escalated claim as one bullet, in this shape: "- <the claim, stated exactly> — <one-line reason it clears the bar>". List nothing else under that heading. The office reads that heading mechanically: listing claims there spawns ONE lab sub-case for exactly those claims, your step then waits for the lab, and the lab's labels are attached to your output for the steps that follow. Claims the lab labels NOT VERIFIED go on the do-not-publish footing for this job — later steps (Johnny's copy above all) must not use them, exactly as with your own unverified list.
ONE ESCALATION PER JOB, hard cap: escalate once, in this step's result, with the full list. There is no second escalation on this job.
If no claim clears the bar, do not include the heading at all — the job simply continues as usual.`;

// Social links check (Ben, 2026-10-15 — prompted by a real miss: Tom's

// facebook.com/flourishbakerybc — in seconds). Whenever a research step's

export const SOCIAL_LINKS_CHECK = `SOCIAL LINKS CHECK — MANDATORY whenever the subject of this research is a business or a public page:
Before you report anything about the subject's social media presence — and before any verdict on whether a page exists or is verified — open the subject's OWN website and look for its social media links. Check the header and footer icons first, then the contact page and the about page. Businesses link their real profiles from their own site; that link is the authoritative pointer to the correct page.

- If a social link IS present on their own site but you cannot open or resolve it with your tools, report it exactly as: "social link found on their own site — needs a live look", together with the site URL and the link as found. NEVER report that as a flat "not verified", "no page found", or "no citable URL found" — a link on their own site IS a finding, even when your tools cannot follow it.

export function parseEscalatedClaims(result: string): string[] | null {
  const lines = result.replace(/\r\n/g, "\n").split("\n");
  let start = -1;
  for (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i += 1) {
    if (/ESCALATED TO RESEARCH DEPT/i.test(lines[i] ?? "")) { start = i; break; }
  }
  if (start < 0) return null;
  const claims: string[] = [];
  for (let i = start + 1; i < lines.length; i += 1) {
    const raw = (lines[i] ?? "").trim();
    if (/^#{1,6}\s+/.test(raw)) break;
    if (/^[A-Z][A-Z ]{3,}:\s*$/.test(raw)) break;
    const bulletText = raw.match(/^[-*]\s+(.+)$/)?.[1] ?? raw.match(/^\d+[.)]\s+(.+)$/)?.[1];
    if (bulletText?.trim()) claims.push(bulletText.trim().slice(0, 600));
    else if (raw && claims.length === 0) continue;
    else if (!raw) continue;
  }
  return claims.length ? claims : null;
}

export function countLabLabels(text: string): { documented: number; notVerified: number } {
  // Peter lists NOT VERIFIED claims a second time under a DO-NOT-PUBLISH
  // heading — count only the labeled list itself, before that repeat.
  const labeledList = text.split(/DO[-\s]?NOT[-\s]?PUBLISH/i)[0] ?? text;
  const documented = (labeledList.match(/\bDOCUMENTED\b/g) ?? []).length;
  const notVerified = (labeledList.match(/\bNOT VERIFIED\b/g) ?? []).length;
  return { documented, notVerified };
}

export function isEscalationEligibleTask(task: Pick<typeof schema.tasks.$inferSelect, "pipeline"> | null | undefined): boolean {
  if (!task) return false;
  // Research cases are already in the lab; Olivia/X work has no Tom step;
  // Front Office package/report jobs are not research steps. Market
  // briefings and creative packages are product pipelines with their own
  // fixed steps — Tom's briefing step synthesizes Sven's gathering and is
  // not a downstairs verification pass, so it never escalates either.
  return task.pipeline !== "research_case" && task.pipeline !== "x_posts" && task.pipeline !== "client_delivery" && task.pipeline !== "client_report" && task.pipeline !== "market_briefing" && task.pipeline !== "creative_package";
}

function isSocialPostRequest(title: string, notes: string): boolean {
  const context = `${title}\n${notes}`;
  const explicitlySocial = /\b(?:facebook|perfectly paranoid|social (?:media|post|content|story)|instagram post|threads post)\b/i.test(context);
  const storyPackage = /\b(?:story|post)\b/i.test(context)
    && /\b(?:research|find|verify|source)\b/i.test(context)
    && /\b(?:image|visual|art|graphic)\b/i.test(context);
  return explicitlySocial || storyPackage;
}

Re-saving a chunk with the same grades is harmless and never duplicates; NEVER try to change a grade already recorded — a conflicting overwrite is rejected as a reconciliation failure and marks the job GRADING INCOMPLETE.
4. RECONCILE BEFORE YOU FINISH: call reconcile_claim_grades. If it does not come back complete, your claim-check.md and your result must state GRADING INCOMPLETE in plain words and list the unaccounted claim IDs — never present a partial grading as a complete one.

SOURCE PROVENANCE (Change 2 — recorded and reported, never a grading shortcut): Walter recorded a structured provenance record for every gathered source (publisher, document type, publication date or vintage, primary-vs-secondary, independence). get_claim_grading_state returns those records with the manifest, and every manifest claim's source references resolve to them, so what stands behind a claim is visible. Provenance informs the provenance test below exactly as it always has — by you opening and judging the source — and nothing else: no source family is automatically demoted, penalised, or preferred at grading time because of its provenance record, in either gathering mode.

TASK: Grade EVERY claim in Walter's extraction on four tests:
(a) Provenance — who published the underlying figure, and why: official statistics or a primary record, trade coverage, a vendor selling a related product, or a roundup citing another roundup.
(b) Triangulation — an independent second witness exists for the claim, or the claim rests on a single source.
(c) Definition fit — the source measured what the claim says: the same population, the same size band, the same definitions, measured behaviour rather than survey-reported behaviour (or the reverse, where the claim blurs them).
(d) Vintage/scope — the year, country, and population behind the figure match how the claim is used.

GRADE RUBRIC — assign each claim exactly one grade, spelled exactly like this:
- STRONG — passes all four tests.
- SUPPORTED — a real, traceable source behind it; usable with its label attached, even if one test is merely adequate rather than clean.
- SHAKY — a vendor self-report without a visible method, a second-hand report of a primary source nobody opened, stale for the use it is put to, or soft definitions presented flat.
- MISFRAMED — the figure does not measure what the claim says, or a narrow population is presented as a general one.
A claim Peter labeled NOT VERIFIED has no traceable source to grade: its disposition is UNTRACEABLE, with the reason "not verified at verification — no traceable source to grade", so every claim still ends with exactly one disposition and the count reconciles claim by claim.

DEFINITION OF DONE — all six are true:
- The claim manifest was recorded first (save_claim_manifest), the grades were saved in chunks of at most 15 (save_claim_grade_chunk), and reconcile_claim_grades was called at the end.
- Every claim in the manifest appears in your output exactly once, under its CC ID, with exactly one disposition (STRONG / SUPPORTED / SHAKY / MISFRAMED / UNTRACEABLE / UNGRADED).
- Each grade carries a one-line reason that names the deciding test(s) — provenance, triangulation, definition fit, or vintage/scope — never just "weak source"; every UNGRADED claim carries its specific recorded reason instead.

- A demoted list names every SHAKY and every MISFRAMED claim again, each with its reason, so Tom cannot miss what was demoted.
- No grade is raised because a claim would help the verdict, and none is lowered because it would hurt it — the tests are the whole call.

OUTPUT FORMAT: save the full grading as a Markdown file named claim-check.md in this job's folder, and return the identical grading as your result so Tom can synthesize under it. Every claim line carries its manifest ID in this shape: "CC-001 — STRONG — <one-line reason>". The grading opens with its plain human title heading, then a section headed exactly \`## In plain words\` holding one or two plain sentences that state the outcome of the grading — the tallies in plain words (how many claims checked, and how many came out strong, supported, shaky, and misframed) and what that leaves standing; if the reconciliation is not complete, that lead states GRADING INCOMPLETE and names the unaccounted claim IDs instead. That lead is written for a person, not the crew: no byline, no department name, no stage narration — who graded it and how belongs in the working content below, never in the lead. IF A GRADE TURNS ON METHODOLOGY YOU CANNOT SEE: say so in that claim's reason and grade it no higher than SHAKY — an unseen method is never given the benefit of the doubt.`,
    },
    {
