// Olivia — X Drafter, Research Department. She drafts posts for
// @PulseHQOffice into the Post Queue and nothing else: she never logs into
// X, never uses an API, and never publishes. Ben copies a queued post,
// pastes it into X himself, and marks it posted. The queue is the review
// surface, so X-post jobs finish straight to Done — no approval step.
export const OLIVIA_X_ORDER_ID = "olivia-x-posts-weekly";
export const X_POST_MAX_CHARS = 280;
export const X_SHOWCASE_LINK = "https://tinyurl.com/ms54rvz7";

export const X_POST_FORBIDDEN_NAMES = /\b(?:ben|benjamin|skunk)\b/i;
export function xPostHasLink(text: string): boolean { return /https?:\/\/\S+/i.test(text); }
export function normalizeXImagePath(raw: string): string | null {
  const cleaned = raw.trim().replace(/^~\/+/, "").replace(/^\/home\/hatch\//, "");
  const marker = "workspace/ai-office/";
  const at = cleaned.indexOf(marker);
  const relative = (at >= 0 ? cleaned.slice(at + marker.length) : cleaned).replace(/^\/+/, "");
  if (!relative || relative.split("/").includes("..")) return null;
  if (!/\.(?:png|jpe?g|webp)$/i.test(relative)) return null;
  return relative;
}

// Olivia's drafting rules live in exactly ONE place: her standing order
// (OLIVIA_X_ORDER_ID) in the database. The order's text was reconciled to
// carry the complete ruleset (migration 0033) — scope, never-mention-the-
// owner, attraction grammar, the hashtag-block rule, truth rules, format,
// the image-or-link rule, the Definition of Done, and the shortfall clause,
// plus the order's own administrative content (weekly Monday 9:00 AM
// America/Vancouver schedule, scheduled batch of 3). Every brief path —
// manual X Posts jobs (xPostsPlan below) and the scheduled Monday batch
// (createOliviaMondayBatch) — composes her drafting instructions FROM that
// order text through oliviaRulesFromOrderText, so editing her standing
// order changes what she drafts. There is no server-side copy of the rules
// anymore: do not reintroduce one. The only per-job substitutions are the
// {{count}} / {{plural}} tokens, set from the count the running job asked
// for (3 for the scheduled batch).
export function oliviaRulesFromOrderText(orderText: string, count: number): string {
  return expandStandingOrderInstruction(orderText)
    .split("{{count}}").join(String(count))
    .split("{{plural}}").join(count === 1 ? "" : "s");
}

async function oliviaRulesForCount(ctx: Ctx, count: number): Promise<string | null> {
  const db = ctx.db<typeof schema>();
  const rows = await db.select().from(schema.standingOrders).where(eq(schema.standingOrders.id, OLIVIA_X_ORDER_ID)).limit(1);
  const order = rows[0];
  if (!order) return null;
  return oliviaRulesFromOrderText(order.instruction, count);
}

async function xPostsPlan(ctx: Ctx, topic: string, notes: string, count: number): Promise<PlanStep[] | null> {
  const rules = await oliviaRulesForCount(ctx, count);
  if (!rules) return null;
  const material = `${topic}${notes ? `\n\nSupplied angle / details:\n${notes}` : ""}`;
  return [{
    assignee: "olivia",
    title: `Draft ${count} X post${count === 1 ? "" : "s"}: ${topic}`.slice(0, 120),
    instructions: `You are Olivia, the X Drafter in Pulse HQ's Research Department. You start this run fresh: the material below is everything you know about this batch, and it is the source of truth for every claim you make — if an event or number is not in it, it does not go in a post.\n\nTopic / angle supplied for this batch:\n${material}\n\n${rules}\n\nAny link in the material above may be used as a post's link branch.`,
  }];
}

const blockerClassificationShape = z.object({
  kind: blockerKind,
  gateKey: z.string().regex(/^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$/).max(80),
  verificationInstructions: z.string().trim().min(1).max(1000).nullable(),
});
const answerAssessmentShape = z.object({ addressed: z.boolean(), isQuestion: z.boolean(), reason: z.string().trim().min(1).max(240) });

function fallbackGateKey(question: string): string {
  const service = ["redbubble", "cloudflare", "facebook", "meta", "instagram", "teepublic", "etsy", "login", "consent", "captcha"].find((word) => question.toLowerCase().includes(word));
  const cause = /cloudflare|captcha|verify (?:you are|you're) human|checkbox/i.test(question) ? "human-check" : /consent|approve/i.test(question) ? "consent" : /log[ -]?in|sign[ -]?in|session/i.test(question) ? "login" : "decision";
  return `${service ?? "external"}-${cause}`;
}

async function classifyBlocker(ctx: Ctx, question: string, suppliedKind?: z.infer<typeof blockerKind>, suppliedGateKey?: string, suppliedVerification?: string): Promise<z.infer<typeof blockerClassificationShape>> {
  const cleanedKey = suppliedGateKey?.trim().toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, "-").replace(/^-|-$/g, "").slice(0, 80);
  if (suppliedKind && cleanedKey) {
    return { kind: suppliedKind, gateKey: cleanedKey, verificationInstructions: suppliedKind === "browser_action" ? suppliedVerification?.trim() || `Re-check the external gate described here without repeating the blocked work: ${question}` : null };
  }
  try {
    return await ctx.inference.complete(
      `Classify this one work blocker into exactly one kind. DEFINITIONS: "decision" means Ben's words alone resolve it — a choice between named options, a missing detail only he holds, or an approval. "browser_action" means Ben must physically do something in a browser: sign in, click a human-check checkbox, approve a consent prompt, or clear an access wall. If both could apply, choose browser_action only when a browser step must happen before any decision matters. GATE KEY: build a stable lowercase kebab-case key from the service and the underlying cause only — never from this question's wording — so repeat reports of the same gate reuse the same key (example: redbubble-cloudflare-human-check). VERIFICATION INSTRUCTIONS: for browser_action blockers only, write one lightweight check that confirms whether the gate cleared and nothing more; it must not redo or describe redoing the blocked work. For decision blockers, return null.\n\nBlocker: ${question}`,
      { schema: blockerClassificationShape },
    );
  } catch {
    const browserAction = /browser|click|checkbox|cloudflare|captcha|verify (?:you are|you're) human|sign[ -]?in|log[ -]?in|consent|access wall/i.test(question);
    return { kind: browserAction ? "browser_action" : "decision", gateKey: fallbackGateKey(question), verificationInstructions: browserAction ? `Re-check only whether this gate is now clear: ${question}` : null };
  }
}

// Ben's decision is judged by rule, never by a model. The sheet's own copy
// promises exactly this contract — "Give a direct choice or instruction.
// A question keeps the blocker open" — so the ONLY reply that stays open
// is one that is itself a question back to the crew. Anything else is a
// decision the worker acts on; if it is genuinely unclear, the worker's
// own tool is to report the blocker again with a sharper question.
//
// This used to call ctx.inference to grade the reply "conservatively";
// that gate looped on Ben's phone (2026-10-15, Founding Test Run hunt):
// a plain instruction that didn't literally pick the offered (a)/(b)/(c)
// letter could be graded "not addressed", the rejection surfaced only in
// a toast rendered BEHIND the sheet, and every resubmission re-ran the
// slow model check and came back to the same open sheet — "Checking
// answer…" forever, with the decision never landing. No model call also
// means the tap-to-resume path is a fast database write, so the button
// can no longer hang on inference latency or schema retries.
function assessDecisionAnswer(answer: string): z.infer<typeof answerAssessmentShape> {
  const trimmed = answer.trim();
  const endsAsQuestion = /\?\s*$/.test(trimmed);
  const opensAsQuestion = /^(?:how|what|why|where|when|who|which|whose|can|could|would|should|shall|do|does|did|is|are|was|were|am)\b/i.test(trimmed);
  const carriesDirective = /\b(?:deliver|send|close|choose|pick|go with|use|make|reroute|supply|publish|post|skip|stop|continue|proceed|approve|option\s*\(?[abc]\)?|\(?[abc]\)\s*[—–-])/i.test(trimmed);
  const isQuestion = endsAsQuestion || (opensAsQuestion && !carriesDirective);
  if (isQuestion) {
    return { addressed: false, isQuestion: true, reason: "That reads as a question, so this request stays open. Give a direct choice or instruction and the step resumes right away." };
  }
  return { addressed: true, isQuestion: false, reason: "Decision received." };
}

function taskDto(row: typeof schema.tasks.$inferSelect, compact = false): z.infer<typeof taskShape> {
  const parsed = taskStatus.safeParse(row.status);
  const parsedType = jobType.safeParse(row.jobType);
  const contract = parsedType.success ? contractForTask(row) : null;
  const { outcomeContract: _snapshot, gradingDetail: _gradingDetailRaw, gradingUpdatedAt: _gradingUpdatedAt, gatheringMode: _gatheringModeRaw, labMeasurements: _labMeasurementsRaw, ...rest } = row;
  // Compact mode (get_state only, done tasks only — Phase 2): the notes
  // tail of finished history is truncated exactly the way briefDto's
  // compact mode truncates brief notes (900 chars). Every other caller
  // (single-task returns, job creation, rework, …) keeps the full notes.
  const notes = compact && row.notes.length > 900 ? `${row.notes.slice(0, 899)}…` : row.notes;
  // Claim completeness gate: the persisted reconciliation detail carries
  // the unaccounted IDs and counts the job surfaces show.
  let gradingIncompleteIds: string[] = [];
  let gradingManifestCount = 0;
  let gradingGradedCount = 0;
  if (_gradingDetailRaw) {
    try {
      const detail = JSON.parse(_gradingDetailRaw) as Partial<ClaimReconciliation>;
      if (Array.isArray(detail.incompleteIds)) gradingIncompleteIds = detail.incompleteIds.filter((value): value is string => typeof value === "string");
      if (typeof detail.manifestCount === "number") gradingManifestCount = detail.manifestCount;
      if (typeof detail.gradedCount === "number") gradingGradedCount = detail.gradedCount;
    } catch { /* A malformed detail serves empty gate counts, never a crash. */ }
  }
  return {
    ...rest,
    notes,
    gradingStatus: row.gradingStatus ?? null,
    gradingIncompleteIds,
    gradingManifestCount,
    gradingGradedCount,
    gatheringMode: (_gatheringModeRaw === "tiered" ? "tiered" : "standard") as z.infer<typeof gatheringMode>,
    jobType: parsedType.success ? parsedType.data : null,
    contractLabel: contract?.label ?? null,
    contractDeliverable: contract?.deliverableShape ?? null,
    contractVoice: contract?.voice ?? null,
    contractStatus: row.contractStatus ?? null,
    contractViolation: row.contractViolation ?? null,
    contractBounces: row.contractBounces ?? 0,
    status: parsed.success ? parsed.data : "working", created: row.created.toISOString(), approvedAt: row.approvedAt?.toISOString() ?? null, postedAt: row.postedAt?.toISOString() ?? null, deliverableReviewFinalizedAt: row.deliverableReviewFinalizedAt?.toISOString() ?? null,
  };
}

  return { ...row, notes: shorten(row.notes, 900) ?? "", result: shorten(row.result, 1200), createdAt: row.createdAt.toISOString(), updatedAt: row.updatedAt.toISOString(), lastHeartbeatAt: row.lastHeartbeatAt?.toISOString() ?? null };

// Internal clients (Ben's rule, 2026-10-16): Perfectly Paranoid is
// Client #1 — Ben's own proving client — and Pulse HQ's own house posts
// are not revenue. Their packages NEVER create ledger rows: PP posts and
// Pulse posts don't go into the owed-money queue. The auto-row rule
// applies to EXTERNAL clients only. Manual rows stay unrestricted —
// if Ben hand-adds a row for anything, it stays.
function isInternalLedgerClientName(name: string): boolean {
  const normalized = name.trim().toLowerCase();
  return normalized.includes("perfectly paranoid") || normalized.includes("pulse hq");
}

// Shipped & Revenue AUTO-ROW: the moment an EXTERNAL client's delivery
// package becomes Delivered, exactly one ledger row is created from it —
// the client, the package's plain title as what shipped, the delivery
// date, amount left empty (Ben records money; the crew never invents a
// figure), status owed. Idempotent by construction: the existence check
// here plus the unique index on package_id make a second row for the
// same package impossible.
async function ensureLedgerRowForDeliveredPackage(ctx: Ctx, pkg: typeof schema.deliveryPackages.$inferSelect, deliveredAt: Date): Promise<void> {
  const db = ctx.db<typeof schema>();
  const existing = await db.select({ id: schema.ledgerEntries.id }).from(schema.ledgerEntries).where(eq(schema.ledgerEntries.packageId, pkg.id)).limit(1);
  if (existing[0]) return;
  const clientRows = await db.select().from(schema.clients).where(eq(schema.clients.id, pkg.clientId)).limit(1);
  if (clientRows[0] && isInternalLedgerClientName(clientRows[0].businessName)) return;
  const now = new Date();
  await db.insert(schema.ledgerEntries).values({
    id: `ledger-${crypto.randomUUID()}`,
    shippedDate: vancouverDateString(deliveredAt),
    clientId: pkg.clientId,
    clientLabel: clientRows[0]?.businessName ?? "",
    whatShipped: pkg.title,
    amountCents: null,
    status: "owed",
    method: "",
    note: "",
    source: "package",
    packageId: pkg.id,
    createdAt: now,
    updatedAt: now,
  });
}

// Dedupe identity for a story: the normalized source link AND the
// normalized headline are each identities on their own — the same link
// under a new headline, or the same story from another outlet under the
// same headline, is the same story. The stored dedupeKey covers the
// combined pair (unique index as a backstop); save_sven_stories compares
// both halves against every row ever filed, dismissed and used included.
function normalizeStoryUrl(value: string): string {
  try {
    const url = new URL(value.trim());
    url.hash = "";
    url.hostname = url.hostname.toLowerCase();
    const path = url.pathname.replace(/\/+$/, "") || "/";
    return `${url.protocol}//${url.host}${path}${url.search}`;
  } catch {
    return value.trim().toLowerCase().replace(/\/+$/, "");
  }
}
function normalizeStoryHeadline(value: string): string {
  return value.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, " ").trim().replace(/\s+/g, " ");
}
function storyDedupeKey(headline: string, sourceUrl: string): string {
  return `${normalizeStoryUrl(sourceUrl)}::${normalizeStoryHeadline(headline)}`;
}
function isStoryExpired(row: Pick<typeof schema.svenStories.$inferSelect, "status" | "expiresAt">, now: Date): boolean {
  return row.status === "new" && row.expiresAt.getTime() <= now.getTime();
}
// Story expiry (Phase 2): stories untouched past their expiry leave the
// shelves quietly — flipped to 'expired', with no notification. The row
// stays in the table, so an expired story still counts for dedupe. This
// write used to run inside get_state on every screen load; it now runs
// from poll_dispatch, which already runs periodically, so get_state is a
// pure read. get_state still hides past-expiry 'new' rows at read time
// (isStoryExpired), so a story never shows past its expiry even between
// dispatcher runs.
async function expireSvenStories(ctx: Ctx): Promise<number> {
  const db = ctx.db<typeof schema>();
  const expiryNow = new Date();
  const expirable = await db.select({ id: schema.svenStories.id, expiresAt: schema.svenStories.expiresAt }).from(schema.svenStories).where(eq(schema.svenStories.status, "new"));
  let expired = 0;
  for (const row of expirable) {
    if (row.expiresAt.getTime() <= expiryNow.getTime()) {
      await db.update(schema.svenStories).set({ status: "expired" }).where(eq(schema.svenStories.id, row.id));
      expired += 1;
    }
  }
  return expired;
}
// "Today" for the daily caps is Sven's hunt day in the office timezone.
function sameStoryDay(left: Date, right: Date): boolean {
  const a = localDateParts(left, "America/Vancouver");
  const b = localDateParts(right, "America/Vancouver");
  return a.year === b.year && a.month === b.month && a.day === b.day;
}

async function remmyBriefingDto(ctx: Ctx, session: typeof schema.remmyBriefingSessions.$inferSelect): Promise<z.infer<typeof remmyBriefingShape>> {
  const db = ctx.db<typeof schema>();
  const [messageRows, attachmentRows, taskRows] = await Promise.all([
    db.select().from(schema.remmyBriefingMessages).where(eq(schema.remmyBriefingMessages.sessionId, session.id)).orderBy(schema.remmyBriefingMessages.createdAt),
    db.select().from(schema.remmyBriefingAttachments).where(eq(schema.remmyBriefingAttachments.sessionId, session.id)).orderBy(schema.remmyBriefingAttachments.createdAt),
    session.taskId ? db.select().from(schema.tasks).where(eq(schema.tasks.id, session.taskId)).limit(1) : Promise.resolve([] as Array<typeof schema.tasks.$inferSelect>),
  ]);
  const attachmentsByMessage = new Map<string, Array<z.infer<typeof remmyAttachmentShape>>>();
  const unattached: Array<z.infer<typeof remmyAttachmentShape>> = [];
  for (const row of attachmentRows) {
    let imageUrl: string | null = null;
    if (row.previewBlobKey) {
      try { imageUrl = await ctx.blobs.getUrl(row.previewBlobKey, { expiresInSeconds: 3600 }); } catch { imageUrl = null; }
    }
    const dto: z.infer<typeof remmyAttachmentShape> = {
      id: row.id, fileName: row.fileName, contentType: row.contentType, size: row.size,
      kind: REMMY_ATTACHMENT_TYPES[row.contentType]?.kind ?? "text", imageUrl,
      stagingRelativePath: row.stagingRelativePath, jobRelativePath: row.jobRelativePath ?? null,
    };
    if (row.messageId) {
      const list = attachmentsByMessage.get(row.messageId) ?? [];
      list.push(dto);
      attachmentsByMessage.set(row.messageId, list);
    } else {
      unattached.push(dto);
    }
  }
  const messages: Array<z.infer<typeof remmyMessageShape>> = messageRows.map((row) => ({
    id: row.id, role: row.role === "remmy" ? "remmy" as const : "user" as const, text: row.text,
    createdAt: row.createdAt.toISOString(), attachments: attachmentsByMessage.get(row.id) ?? [],
  }));
  if (unattached.length && messages.length) {
    const first = messages[0];
    if (first) first.attachments = [...first.attachments, ...unattached];
  }
  const shaped: z.infer<typeof remmyShapedShape> | null = session.shapedTitle && session.shapedJobType && session.shapedSummary && session.shapedBrief
    ? { title: session.shapedTitle, jobType: session.shapedJobType, summary: session.shapedSummary, brief: session.shapedBrief, postCount: session.shapedPostCount ?? null }
    : null;
  return {
    id: session.id, status: session.status, createdAt: session.createdAt.toISOString(), updatedAt: session.updatedAt.toISOString(),
    messages, shaped, taskId: session.taskId ?? null, taskTitle: taskRows[0]?.title ?? null,
  };
}
