type LocalDateParts = { year: number; month: number; day: number };

function localDateParts(value: Date, timezone: string): LocalDateParts {
  const parts = new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-CA", { timeZone: timezone, year: "numeric", month: "2-digit", day: "2-digit" }).formatToParts(value);
  const numberPart = (type: "year" | "month" | "day") => Number(parts.find((part) => part.type === type)?.value ?? 0);
  return { year: numberPart("year"), month: numberPart("month"), day: numberPart("day") };
}

function shiftLocalDate(parts: LocalDateParts, days: number): LocalDateParts {
  const shifted = new Date(Date.UTC(parts.year, parts.month - 1, parts.day + days));
  return { year: shifted.getUTCFullYear(), month: shifted.getUTCMonth() + 1, day: shifted.getUTCDate() };
}

function localWeekday(parts: LocalDateParts): number { return new Date(Date.UTC(parts.year, parts.month - 1, parts.day)).getUTCDay(); }

function localWallTimeToInstant(parts: LocalDateParts, hour: number, minute: number, timezone: string): Date {
  const target = Date.UTC(parts.year, parts.month - 1, parts.day, hour, minute, 0, 0);
  let guess = target;
  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 4; attempt += 1) {
    const rendered = new Date(guess);
    const dateParts = new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-CA", {
      timeZone: timezone, year: "numeric", month: "2-digit", day: "2-digit", hour: "2-digit", minute: "2-digit", second: "2-digit", hourCycle: "h23",
    }).formatToParts(rendered);
    const value = (type: "year" | "month" | "day" | "hour" | "minute" | "second") => Number(dateParts.find((part) => part.type === type)?.value ?? 0);
    const renderedAsUtc = Date.UTC(value("year"), value("month") - 1, value("day"), value("hour"), value("minute"), value("second"));
    const correction = target - renderedAsUtc;
    if (correction === 0) break;
    guess += correction;
  }
  return new Date(guess);
}

function scheduledRunAround(now: Date, selectedCadence: "daily" | "weekly", weekday: number | null, hour: number, minute: number, timezone: string, direction: "latest" | "next"): Date {
  const today = localDateParts(now, timezone);
  const targetWeekday = weekday ?? 1;
  for (let delta = direction === "latest" ? 0 : 0; direction === "latest" ? delta >= -8 : delta <= 8; delta += direction === "latest" ? -1 : 1) {
    const date = shiftLocalDate(today, delta);
    if (selectedCadence === "weekly" && localWeekday(date) !== targetWeekday) continue;
    const candidate = localWallTimeToInstant(date, hour, minute, timezone);
    if (direction === "latest" ? candidate.getTime() <= now.getTime() : candidate.getTime() > now.getTime()) return candidate;
  }
  return new Date(now.getTime() + (direction === "latest" ? -86_400_000 : 86_400_000));
}

function latestScheduledRun(now: Date, selectedCadence: "daily" | "weekly", weekday: number | null, hour: number, minute: number, timezone: string): Date {
  return scheduledRunAround(now, selectedCadence, weekday, hour, minute, timezone, "latest");
}

function nextScheduledRun(now: Date, selectedCadence: "daily" | "weekly", weekday: number | null, hour: number, minute: number, timezone: string): Date {
  return scheduledRunAround(now, selectedCadence, weekday, hour, minute, timezone, "next");
}

function decodeBase64(value: string): Uint8Array {
  const binary = atob(value); const bytes = new Uint8Array(binary.length);
  for (let index = 0; index < binary.length; index += 1) bytes[index] = binary.charCodeAt(index);
  return bytes;
}
function deliverableHints(results: string[]): string[] {
  const hints = new Set<string>();
  for (const result of results) {
    for (const match of result.matchAll(/(?:~\/|\/home\/hatch\/)?workspace\/ai-office\/[^\s"'`<>\]]+/g)) {
      const value = match[0]?.replace(/^(?:~\/|\/home\/hatch\/)?workspace\/ai-office\//, "").replace(/[),.;:]+$/g, "");
      if (value && value.length <= 500 && !value.split("/").includes("..")) hints.add(value);
      if (hints.size >= 30) return Array.from(hints);
    }
  }
  return Array.from(hints);
}
function deliverableBlobKey(relativePath: string): string { return `brief-deliverables/${relativePath.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9._/-]/g, "_")}`; }

type ImageProvenance = z.infer<typeof imageProvenanceShape>;

function provenanceFromParts(kind: "real" | "generated", sourceUrl: string | null, license: string | null): ImageProvenance {
  const cleanLicense = license?.trim() ? license.trim().slice(0, 200) : null;
  const cleanSource = sourceUrl && /^https?:\/\/\S+$/i.test(sourceUrl.trim()) ? sourceUrl.trim() : null;
  return kind === "real"
    ? { kind, sourceUrl: cleanSource, license: cleanLicense, label: `Real photograph${cleanLicense ? ` · ${cleanLicense}` : ""}` }
    : { kind, sourceUrl: null, license: null, label: "AI-generated (no suitable real image found)" };
}

// Provenance reaches the server in two worker-written shapes, both mandated by
// the source-first contract: blocks in image-provenance.md ("Image:" / "Kind:"
// / "Source:" / "License:" lines) and one-line IMAGE PROVENANCE statements in a
// step result. Keys are lowercased image file basenames.
function parseImageProvenance(text: string): Map<string, ImageProvenance> {
  const entries = new Map<string, ImageProvenance>();
  let pendingFile: string | null = null;
  let pendingKind: "real" | "generated" | null = null;
  let pendingSource: string | null = null;
  let pendingLicense: string | null = null;
  const flush = () => {
    if (pendingFile && pendingKind) entries.set(pendingFile, provenanceFromParts(pendingKind, pendingSource, pendingLicense));
    pendingFile = null; pendingKind = null; pendingSource = null; pendingLicense = null;
  };
  for (const rawLine of text.replace(/\r\n/g, "\n").split("\n")) {
    const line = rawLine.trim();
    const imageLine = /^(?:#{1,6}\s*)?(?:[-*]\s*)?Image\s*:\s*(.+)$/i.exec(line);
    if (imageLine?.[1]) { flush(); pendingFile = imageLine[1].trim().split("/").at(-1)?.toLowerCase() ?? null; continue; }
    const kindLine = /^Kind\s*:\s*(real|generated)\b/i.exec(line);
    if (kindLine?.[1]) { pendingKind = kindLine[1].toLowerCase() as "real" | "generated"; continue; }
    const sourceLine = /^Source\s*:\s*(\S+)\s*$/i.exec(line);
    if (sourceLine?.[1]) { pendingSource = sourceLine[1]; continue; }
    const licenseLine = /^License\s*:\s*(.+)$/i.exec(line);
    if (licenseLine?.[1]) { pendingLicense = licenseLine[1].trim(); continue; }
    const resultLine = /IMAGE PROVENANCE\s*:\s*(.+)$/i.exec(line);
    if (resultLine?.[1]) {
      const body = resultLine[1];
      const generated = /AI-generated/i.test(body);
      const url = /https?:\/\/\S+/.exec(body)?.[0]?.replace(/[),.;]+$/, "") ?? null;
      const licenseMatch = /License\s*:\s*([^—–\n]+)/i.exec(body);
      const nameMatch = /(?:Real photograph|AI-generated \(no suitable real image found\))\s*[—–-]\s*([^\s—–]+)/i.exec(body);
      const fileName = nameMatch?.[1]?.trim().split("/").at(-1)?.toLowerCase();
      if (fileName) entries.set(fileName, provenanceFromParts(generated ? "generated" : "real", url, licenseMatch?.[1]?.trim() ?? null));
    }
  }
  flush();
  return entries;
}
function taskDeliverableFolder(taskId: string): string { return `jobs/${taskId.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]/g, "_")}`; }

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// EXCLUDED DELIVERABLES (Ben's ruling, enforced mechanically 2026-10-18).
// A job's own finished documents can declare a piece EXCLUDED from the
// pack — the outreach pack's manifest does exactly this for Pb47 Blendz:
// "EXCLUDED from this pack … Its rebuilt mockup file
// (mockups/06-pb47-blendz.html / .png) may remain in the folder unused;
// it is not part of the pack." The declaration is read from the job's own
// texts: any line that says "excluded" and names a file excludes that
// file, and — by stem — its sibling renditions (the .png of an excluded
// .html). An excluded piece is not part of the decision: never a
// keep/delete choice, never deleted by the batch review, never a blocker
// on approval. Before this, the excluded mockup sat in the review grid
// as a keep/delete chore and an undecided excluded image could hold the
// whole pack's approval hostage.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
function exclusionStemsFromTexts(texts: string[]): Set<string> {
  const stems = new Set<string>();
  const fileToken = /[\w./-]+\.(?:html?|png|jpe?g|webp|pdf|mp4|md|txt)/gi;
  for (const text of texts) {
    for (const line of text.replace(/\r\n/g, "\n").split("\n")) {
      const keywords = [...line.matchAll(/exclud\w*/gi)].map((match) => ({ start: match.index, end: match.index + match[0].length }));
      if (keywords.length === 0) continue;
      for (const token of line.matchAll(fileToken)) {
        const tokenStart = token.index;
        const tokenEnd = tokenStart + token[0].length;
        // The exclusion word must actually govern this file: the file is
        // named after it on the same line ("EXCLUDED from this pack —
        // mockups/06-pb47-blendz.html may remain…"), or directly before
        // it with only punctuation between ("06-pb47-blendz.html —
        // EXCLUDED"). A line that merely mentions a file and the word
        // "excluded" in passing ("…present in mockups/manifest.md (plus
        // a Pb47 excluded note)") excludes nothing.
        const governed = keywords.some((keyword) => tokenStart >= keyword.end)
          || keywords.some((keyword) => tokenEnd <= keyword.start && !/[a-z0-9]/i.test(line.slice(tokenEnd, keyword.start)));
        if (!governed) continue;
        const base = (token[0].split("/").pop() ?? "").toLowerCase();
        if (!base) continue;
        stems.add(base);
        stems.add(base.replace(/\.[^.]+$/, ""));
      }
    }
  }
  return stems;
}

function isExcludedFileName(fileName: string, stems: ReadonlySet<string>): boolean {
  if (stems.size === 0) return false;
  const base = fileName.toLowerCase();
  return stems.has(base) || stems.has(base.replace(/\.[^.]+$/, ""));
}

async function excludedPathsForTask(ctx: Ctx, task: Pick<typeof schema.tasks.$inferSelect, "id">): Promise<Set<string>> {
  const folder = taskDeliverableFolder(task.id);
  try {
    const db = ctx.db<typeof schema>();
    const [scanned, briefRows] = await Promise.all([
      ctx.executePrivileged(privileged.scanDeliverables, { relativeHints: [folder] }),
      db.select().from(schema.briefs).where(eq(schema.briefs.taskId, task.id)),
    ]);
    const owned = scanned.files.filter((file) => file.relativePath.startsWith(`${folder}/`) && !file.relativePath.includes("/.superseded/"));
    const texts: string[] = [];
    for (const brief of briefRows) if (brief.result) texts.push(brief.result);
    for (const file of owned) {
      if (file.kind !== "markdown" && file.kind !== "text") continue;
      try {
        const content = await ctx.executePrivileged(privileged.readDeliverable, { relativePath: file.relativePath });
        if (content.text) texts.push(content.text);
      } catch { /* one unreadable file never blocks a review */ }
    }
    const stems = exclusionStemsFromTexts(texts);
    if (stems.size === 0) return new Set();
    return new Set(owned.filter((file) => isExcludedFileName(file.fileName, stems)).map((file) => file.relativePath));
  } catch {
    return new Set();
  }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// DO-NOT-PUBLISH → OFFICE POT (Ben, 2026-10-18). The pipeline sweep found
// the failure: a research case killed a claim while a parallel one-pager
// and campaign asserted it, because the lab's do-not-publish list never
// travelled sideways. The rule now lives in the lifecycle, not in worker
// instructions: when ANY research job closes — a manual Research
// Department case, a client-tagged case, a standing-order run, or a lab
// sub-case — the office extracts the case's do-not-publish list (the
// brief's own do-not-publish section, or its SUMMARY "Failed checking"
// list) and posts it to the office pot's Department notes, where every
// floor reads it. Extraction is mechanical and best-effort: a case whose
// brief names no failed claims posts nothing.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
function extractDoNotPublishItems(texts: string[]): string[] {
  const items: string[] = [];
  const seen = new Set<string>();
  const push = (raw: string) => {
    const clean = raw.replace(/\*\*([^*]+)\*\*/g, "$1").replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim().replace(/^[-–—:]\s*/, "");
    if (clean.length < 8 || clean.length > 400) return;
    if (/^none\.?$/i.test(clean)) return;
    const key = clean.toLowerCase();
    if (seen.has(key)) return;
    seen.add(key);
    items.push(clean);
  };
  for (const text of texts) {
    let collecting = false;
    for (const line of text.replace(/\r\n/g, "\n").split("\n")) {
      const trimmed = line.trim();
      if (/^#{1,4}\s/.test(trimmed)) {
        collecting = /do[- ]not[- ]publish/i.test(trimmed);
        continue;
      }
      if (/do[- ]not[- ]publish/i.test(trimmed) && trimmed.length < 140) { collecting = true; continue; }
      if (/failed checking/i.test(trimmed) && trimmed.length < 140) {
        collecting = true;
        const afterColon = trimmed.split(/failed checking\s*:?\s*/i)[1];
        if (afterColon) push(afterColon);
        continue;
      }
      if (!collecting) continue;
      const bullet = trimmed.match(/^(?:[-*]|\d+[.)])\s+(.+)$/);
      if (bullet?.[1]) push(bullet[1]);
    }
  }
  return items.slice(0, 20);
}

async function postDoNotPublishToPot(ctx: Ctx, task: Pick<typeof schema.tasks.$inferSelect, "id" | "title" | "revision">, texts: string[]): Promise<void> {
  const items = extractDoNotPublishItems(texts);
  if (items.length === 0) return;
  const date = new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10);
  const entry = [
    `- **DO NOT PUBLISH — ${task.title}** (research job ${task.id}, closed ${date}): this case's do-not-publish list, posted by the office at close so it binds every floor's copy:`,
    ...items.map((item) => `  - ${item}`),
    `  — Research Department (posted automatically at close), ${date}`,
  ].join("\n");
  try {
    await ctx.executePrivileged(privileged.appendOfficePotNote, { marker: `dnp:${task.id}:r${task.revision}`, entry });
  } catch {
    // The list still lives in the case brief itself; a failed pot post
    // never blocks the job's own close.
  }
}

const PUBLICATION_COPY_HEADING = /^#{1,6}\s*(?:publication[- ]ready\s+)?(?:(?:facebook|social(?: media)?)\s+)?post\s+copy(?:\s*\(final\)|\s*[-—:]\s*final)?\s*$/im;

function extractPublicationReadyPost(value: string): string | null {
  const normalized = value.replace(/\r\n/g, "\n").trim();
  if (!normalized) return null;
  const heading = normalized.match(PUBLICATION_COPY_HEADING);
  if (!heading || heading.index === undefined) return null;
  const afterHeading = normalized.slice(heading.index + heading[0].length).replace(/^\s+/, "");
  const boundary = afterHeading.match(/\n(?:---\s*$|#{1,6}\s+)/m);
  const copy = (boundary ? afterHeading.slice(0, boundary.index) : afterHeading).trim();
  return copy || null;
}

async function captureSocialPostCopy(ctx: Ctx, taskId: string, resultText: string): Promise<string | null> {
  const fromResult = extractPublicationReadyPost(resultText);
  if (fromResult) return fromResult;
  try {
    const folder = taskDeliverableFolder(taskId);
    const scanned = await ctx.executePrivileged(privileged.scanDeliverables, { relativeHints: [folder, ...deliverableHints([resultText])] });
    const candidates = scanned.files
      .filter((file) => file.kind === "markdown" || file.kind === "text")
      .sort((left, right) => {
        const score = (name: string) => /(?:facebook|social)[-_ ]*post|post[-_ ]*copy|caption/i.test(name) ? 1 : 0;
        return score(right.fileName) - score(left.fileName) || new Date(right.modifiedAt).getTime() - new Date(left.modifiedAt).getTime();
      });
    for (const file of candidates) {
      const content = await ctx.executePrivileged(privileged.readDeliverable, { relativePath: file.relativePath });
      const copy = content.text ? extractPublicationReadyPost(content.text) : null;
      if (copy) return copy;
    }
  } catch {
    // The preview can still fall back to a publication-ready section in the stored result.
  }
  return null;
}
// Publishable post packages (Perfectly Paranoid / social posts) follow Ben's
// combined Deliverables flow: Ready for You is only the decision queue, and
// once Ben approves, the package waits in Deliverables under "To post"
// (task status stays "approval" with publicationStatus
// "awaiting_manual_publish") until he marks it posted, which closes the
// job to Done and moves the package into the Deliverables Library with a
// Posted badge. Every other job keeps the single approve-and-done
// behavior, and its finished outputs land in the same Library.
function isPublishablePostTask(task: Pick<typeof schema.tasks.$inferSelect, "pipeline">): boolean {
  return task.pipeline === "perfectly_paranoid";
}
function isApprovedPostPackage(task: Pick<typeof schema.tasks.$inferSelect, "pipeline" | "publicationStatus" | "clientId">): boolean {
  // EXIT RULE (Ben, 2026-10-14; PP routing change 2026-10-16): a post job
  // tagged to an EXTERNAL client never waits in Deliverables → To post —
  // it exits ONLY through its client's delivery package. Untagged post
  // jobs take the To post state — and so do jobs tagged to Perfectly
  // Paranoid (Client #1): PP posts are house content, not client
  // deliveries, so they approve and post exactly like untagged posts.
  return isPublishablePostTask(task)
    && (!task.clientId || task.clientId === PERFECTLY_PARANOID_CLIENT_ID)
    && (task.publicationStatus === "awaiting_manual_publish" || task.publicationStatus === "approved_posting" || task.publicationStatus === "preparing_upload");
}
function isMerchTask(task: Pick<typeof schema.tasks.$inferSelect, "title" | "notes" | "pipeline">): boolean {
  // One shared definition lives in ./shared (isMerchTaskLike) — the
  // client classifies with the same function, not a copy.
  return isMerchTaskLike(task);
}
type ScannedDeliverable = { relativePath: string; fileName: string; kind: "image" | "markdown" | "text" | "document" | "video"; contentType: string; size: number; modifiedAt: string; hasAlphaChannel: boolean | null };
function merchDesignKey(fileName: string): string {
  const numbered = fileName.match(/(?:design|artwork)[-_ ]*0*(\d+)/i)?.[1];
  if (numbered) return `design-${Number(numbered)}`;
  return fileName
    .replace(/\.[^.]+$/, "")
    .replace(/(?:^|[-_ ])(?:transparent|transparency|print[-_ ]?ready|final|rework|revision|rev|version|v)[-_ ]*\d*/gi, " ")
    .replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/gi, "-")
    .replace(/^-|-$/g, "")
    .toLowerCase();
}
function merchVersionScore(fileName: string): number {
  const scores = Array.from(fileName.matchAll(/(?:^|[-_ ])(?:rework|revision|rev|version|v)[-_ ]*(\d+)/gi), (match) => Number(match[1] ?? 0));
  return scores.length ? Math.max(...scores) : 0;
}
function readyImageFiles(task: Pick<typeof schema.tasks.$inferSelect, "title" | "notes" | "pipeline">, files: ScannedDeliverable[]): ScannedDeliverable[] {
  const images = files.filter((file) => file.kind === "image");
  if (task.pipeline === "perfectly_paranoid") return [...images].sort((left, right) => new Date(right.modifiedAt).getTime() - new Date(left.modifiedAt).getTime()).slice(0, 1);
  if (!isMerchTask(task)) return images;
  const transparentPngs = images.filter((file) =>
    file.contentType === "image/png"
    && file.hasAlphaChannel === true
    && !/(?:^|[-_ ])(?:preview|mockup|proof|zoom|source|original)(?:[-_ .]|$)/i.test(file.fileName),
  );
  const latestByDesign = new Map<string, ScannedDeliverable>();
  for (const file of transparentPngs) {
    const key = merchDesignKey(file.fileName) || file.fileName.toLowerCase();
    const previous = latestByDesign.get(key);
    const fileScore = merchVersionScore(file.fileName);
    const previousScore = previous ? merchVersionScore(previous.fileName) : -1;
    if (!previous || fileScore > previousScore || (fileScore === previousScore && new Date(file.modifiedAt).getTime() > new Date(previous.modifiedAt).getTime())) latestByDesign.set(key, file);
  }
  return Array.from(latestByDesign.values()).sort((left, right) => left.fileName.localeCompare(right.fileName));
}
async function taskImageFiles(ctx: Ctx, task: Pick<typeof schema.tasks.$inferSelect, "id" | "title" | "notes" | "pipeline">): Promise<ScannedDeliverable[]> {
  const folder = taskDeliverableFolder(task.id);
  const scanned = await ctx.executePrivileged(privileged.scanDeliverables, { relativeHints: [folder] });
  const owned = scanned.files.filter((file) => file.relativePath.startsWith(`${folder}/`));
  return readyImageFiles(task, owned);
}
async function taskImagePaths(ctx: Ctx, task: Pick<typeof schema.tasks.$inferSelect, "id" | "title" | "notes" | "pipeline">): Promise<string[]> {
  return (await taskImageFiles(ctx, task)).map((file) => file.relativePath);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// PACKAGE DELIVERY — customer ZIP assembly (Ben, 2026-10-16).
//
// The ZIP a customer receives is built from exactly the deliverable set the
// package view lists for the package's source job: the same scan, the same
// superseded-file fallbacks, the same per-image review filtering, and the
// same exclusions (image-provenance files are metadata, never documents;
// files the scan hides never appear). Nothing outside the source job's
// listed deliverables can enter the ZIP, and no internal file (briefs,
// handoffs, drafts, provenance) is ever a listed deliverable.
type PackageFile = {
  relativePath: string; fileName: string;
  kind: "image" | "markdown" | "text" | "document" | "video";
  contentType: string; size: number; modifiedAt: string;
  text: string | null; bytes: Uint8Array | null;
  humanTitle: string;
};

async function collectPackageFiles(ctx: Ctx, task: typeof schema.tasks.$inferSelect): Promise<{ files: PackageFile[]; postCopy: string | null }> {
  const db = ctx.db<typeof schema>();
  const [briefRows, reviewRows] = await Promise.all([
    db.select().from(schema.briefs).where(eq(schema.briefs.taskId, task.id)).orderBy(desc(schema.briefs.updatedAt)),
    db.select().from(schema.deliverableReviews).where(eq(schema.deliverableReviews.taskId, task.id)),
  ]);
  const reviews = new Map(reviewRows.map((row) => [row.relativePath, row.decision]));
  const revisionBriefs = briefRows.filter((item) => item.revision === task.revision);
  const briefs = revisionBriefs.filter((item) => (item.status === "done" || item.status === "failed") && item.result)
    .map((item) => ({ id: item.id, result: item.result ?? "" }));
  const hints = [taskDeliverableFolder(task.id), ...deliverableHints(briefs.map((item) => item.result))];
  const scanned = await ctx.executePrivileged(privileged.scanDeliverables, { relativeHints: hints });
  const folder = taskDeliverableFolder(task.id);
  const taskFiles = scanned.files.filter((file) => file.relativePath.startsWith(`${folder}/`));
  const liveFiles = taskFiles.filter((file) => !file.relativePath.includes("/.superseded/"));
  const archivedFiles = taskFiles
    .filter((file) => file.relativePath.includes("/.superseded/"))
    .sort((left, right) => new Date(right.modifiedAt).getTime() - new Date(left.modifiedAt).getTime());
  const currentFiles: ScannedDeliverable[] = [...liveFiles];
  const addLatestArchived = (matches: (file: ScannedDeliverable) => boolean) => {
    const fallback = archivedFiles.find(matches);
    if (fallback) currentFiles.push(fallback);
  };
  if (!liveFiles.some((file) => file.kind === "image")) addLatestArchived((file) => file.kind === "image");
  const postFilePattern = /(?:facebook|social)[-_ ]*post|post[-_ ]*copy|caption/i;
  if (!liveFiles.some((file) => file.kind !== "image" && postFilePattern.test(file.fileName))) {
    addLatestArchived((file) => file.kind !== "image" && postFilePattern.test(file.fileName));
  }
  const researchFilePattern = /research|source|notes/i;
  if (!liveFiles.some((file) => file.kind !== "image" && researchFilePattern.test(file.fileName))) {
    addLatestArchived((file) => file.kind !== "image" && researchFilePattern.test(file.fileName));
  }
  const isProvenanceFile = (file: ScannedDeliverable) => file.kind !== "image" && /^image-provenance\.(?:md|txt)$/i.test(file.fileName);
  if (!liveFiles.some(isProvenanceFile)) addLatestArchived(isProvenanceFile);
  const readyImages = readyImageFiles(task, currentFiles);
  const isFinalPackage = task.status === "done" || isApprovedPostPackage(task);
  const anyImageDecided = readyImages.some((file) => reviews.has(file.relativePath));
  const visibleImagePaths = new Set(readyImages.filter((file) => {
    if (isFinalPackage) return anyImageDecided ? reviews.get(file.relativePath) === "approved" : true;
    return !task.deliverableReviewFinalizedAt || reviews.get(file.relativePath) === "approved";
  }).map((file) => file.relativePath));
  const files: PackageFile[] = [];
  for (const file of currentFiles) {
    if (isProvenanceFile(file)) continue;
    if (file.kind === "image" && !visibleImagePaths.has(file.relativePath)) continue;
    try {
      const content = await ctx.executePrivileged(privileged.readDeliverable, { relativePath: file.relativePath });
      if ((content.kind === "image" || content.kind === "document" || content.kind === "video") && content.dataBase64) {
        files.push({ relativePath: file.relativePath, fileName: file.fileName, kind: file.kind, contentType: file.contentType, size: file.size, modifiedAt: file.modifiedAt, text: null, bytes: decodeBase64(content.dataBase64), humanTitle: humanTitleForDeliverable(file.fileName, file.kind, task.title) });
      } else if (content.text !== null) {
        files.push({ relativePath: file.relativePath, fileName: file.fileName, kind: file.kind, contentType: file.contentType, size: file.size, modifiedAt: file.modifiedAt, text: content.text, bytes: null, humanTitle: humanTitleForDeliverable(file.fileName, file.kind, task.title) });
      }
    } catch { /* A file that cannot be read is not listed by the package view either. */ }
  }
  const documentPostCopy = files
    .filter((item) => item.text)
    .sort((left, right) => {
      const score = (name: string) => postFilePattern.test(name) ? 1 : 0;
      return score(right.fileName) - score(left.fileName) || new Date(right.modifiedAt).getTime() - new Date(left.modifiedAt).getTime();
    })
    .map((item) => extractPublicationReadyPost(item.text ?? ""))
    .find((copy): copy is string => Boolean(copy));
  const resultPostCopy = briefRows
    .filter((item) => item.status === "done" && item.assignee === "quill" && item.result)
    .map((item) => extractPublicationReadyPost(item.result ?? ""))
    .find((copy): copy is string => Boolean(copy));
  const postCopy = task.pipeline === "perfectly_paranoid" ? task.postCopy ?? documentPostCopy ?? resultPostCopy ?? null : null;
  return { files, postCopy };
}

// A file or folder name a non-technical customer can read: plain words,
// no job ids, no characters Windows or macOS object to.
function sanitizeCustomerName(value: string, fallback: string, maxLength = 64): string {
  const cleaned = value
    .replace(/[\\/:*?"<>|]/g, " ")
    .replace(/[\u0000-\u001f]/g, " ")
    .replace(/\s+/g, " ")
    .replace(/[. ]+$/g, "")
    .trim();
  const out = cleaned.slice(0, maxLength).replace(/[. ]+$/g, "").trim();
  return out || fallback;
}

function firstWordsStem(text: string, fallback: string): string {
  const line = text.replace(/\r\n/g, "\n").split("\n").map((part) => part.replace(/^#+\s*/, "").trim()).find((part) => part.length >= 3) ?? "";
  const words = line.replace(/[*_`>]/g, "").split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean).slice(0, 7).join(" ");
  return sanitizeCustomerName(words, fallback, 56);
}

const CRC32_TABLE = (() => {
  const table = new Uint32Array(256);
  for (let n = 0; n < 256; n += 1) {
    let c = n;
    for (let k = 0; k < 8; k += 1) c = c & 1 ? 0xedb88320 ^ (c >>> 1) : c >>> 1;
    table[n] = c >>> 0;
  }
  return table;
})();

function crc32(bytes: Uint8Array): number {
  let crc = 0xffffffff;
  for (let i = 0; i < bytes.length; i += 1) crc = (CRC32_TABLE[(crc ^ (bytes[i] ?? 0)) & 0xff] ?? 0) ^ (crc >>> 8);
  return (crc ^ 0xffffffff) >>> 0;
}

// Minimal ZIP writer (STORE method — no compression). Images and PDFs are
// already compressed formats, and post/report text is small, so a stored
// ZIP stays honest and every stock extractor opens it.
function buildZipArchive(entries: Array<{ name: string; bytes: Uint8Array }>): Uint8Array {
  const encoder = new TextEncoder();
  const now = new Date();
  const dosTime = ((now.getHours() & 0x1f) << 11) | ((now.getMinutes() & 0x3f) << 5) | ((Math.floor(now.getSeconds() / 2)) & 0x1f);
  const dosDate = (((Math.max(0, now.getFullYear() - 1980)) & 0x7f) << 9) | (((now.getMonth() + 1) & 0xf) << 5) | (now.getDate() & 0x1f);
  const chunks: Uint8Array[] = [];
  const central: Uint8Array[] = [];
  let offset = 0;
  for (const entry of entries) {
    const nameBytes = encoder.encode(entry.name);
    const crc = crc32(entry.bytes);
    const local = new DataView(new ArrayBuffer(30));
    local.setUint32(0, 0x04034b50, true);
    local.setUint16(4, 20, true);
    local.setUint16(6, 0x0800, true); // UTF-8 file names
    local.setUint16(8, 0, true); // STORE
    local.setUint16(10, dosTime, true);
    local.setUint16(12, dosDate, true);
    local.setUint32(14, crc, true);
    local.setUint32(18, entry.bytes.length, true);
    local.setUint32(22, entry.bytes.length, true);
    local.setUint16(26, nameBytes.length, true);
    local.setUint16(28, 0, true);
    chunks.push(new Uint8Array(local.buffer), nameBytes, entry.bytes);
    const centralHeader = new DataView(new ArrayBuffer(46));
    centralHeader.setUint32(0, 0x02014b50, true);
    centralHeader.setUint16(4, 20, true);
    centralHeader.setUint16(6, 20, true);
    centralHeader.setUint16(8, 0x0800, true);
    centralHeader.setUint16(10, 0, true);
    centralHeader.setUint16(12, dosTime, true);
    centralHeader.setUint16(14, dosDate, true);
    centralHeader.setUint32(16, crc, true);
    centralHeader.setUint32(20, entry.bytes.length, true);
    centralHeader.setUint32(24, entry.bytes.length, true);
    centralHeader.setUint16(28, nameBytes.length, true);
    centralHeader.setUint32(42, offset, true);
    central.push(new Uint8Array(centralHeader.buffer), nameBytes);
    offset += 30 + nameBytes.length + entry.bytes.length;
  }
  const centralStart = offset;
  let centralSize = 0;
  for (const chunk of central) centralSize += chunk.length;
  const end = new DataView(new ArrayBuffer(22));
  end.setUint32(0, 0x06054b50, true);
  end.setUint16(8, entries.length, true);
  end.setUint16(10, entries.length, true);
  end.setUint32(12, centralSize, true);
  end.setUint32(16, centralStart, true);
  const total = centralStart + centralSize + 22;
  const out = new Uint8Array(total);
  let cursor = 0;
  for (const chunk of [...chunks, ...central, new Uint8Array(end.buffer)]) {
    out.set(chunk, cursor);
    cursor += chunk.length;
  }
  return out;
}

type BatchImageDecisionOutcome =
  | { ok: true; kept: string[]; discarded: string[] }
  | { ok: false; error: string };

// Batch image approval (Ben's design, 2026-10-16): ONE Accept on the
// review grid commits every image decision for an item at once — the
// step-by-step per-image wizard is gone. The images Ben selected are
// recorded "approved" in deliverable_reviews; every NON-selected image
// is recorded "rejected" there AND its file is deleted from the job
// folder, so it leaves the item's deliverables entirely. The review
// record is what History and provenance read, and it stays — only the
// file goes. onlyPaths narrows the decision to a subset (a delivery
// package decides only its still-undecided images; an image that
// already carries a decision keeps it).
async function applyBatchImageDecisions(ctx: Ctx, taskId: string, imagePaths: string[], keepPaths: string[], onlyPaths?: string[]): Promise<BatchImageDecisionOutcome> {
  const db = ctx.db<typeof schema>();
  const targets = onlyPaths ?? imagePaths;
  const keepSet = new Set(keepPaths);
  if (keepPaths.some((path) => !imagePaths.includes(path))) return { ok: false, error: "One of the selected images is not part of this item anymore. Reopen it and try again." };
  const kept = targets.filter((path) => keepSet.has(path));
  const discarded = targets.filter((path) => !keepSet.has(path));
  if (discarded.length) {
    try {
      await ctx.executePrivileged(privileged.deleteDeliverableFiles, { relativePaths: discarded });
    } catch {
      return { ok: false, error: "The images you did not select could not be deleted. Nothing was changed — try again." };
    }
  }
  const now = new Date();
  const existing = await db.select().from(schema.deliverableReviews).where(eq(schema.deliverableReviews.taskId, taskId));
  const existingPaths = new Set(existing.map((row) => row.relativePath));
  for (const path of targets) {
    const decision = keepSet.has(path) ? "approved" as const : "rejected" as const;
    if (existingPaths.has(path)) {
      await db.update(schema.deliverableReviews).set({ decision, updatedAt: now }).where(and(eq(schema.deliverableReviews.taskId, taskId), eq(schema.deliverableReviews.relativePath, path)));
    } else {
      await db.insert(schema.deliverableReviews).values({ taskId, relativePath: path, decision, updatedAt: now });
    }
  }
  return { ok: true, kept, discarded };
}

async function planWork(ctx: Ctx, title: string, notes: string, options?: { svenOriginated?: boolean; standardContract?: boolean }): Promise<z.infer<typeof workPlanShape>> {
  // STANDARD OUTCOME CONTRACT: a job created as type "standard" is never
  // auto-routed into the social-post pipeline, however social its subject
  // sounds — that routing is what put a Perfectly Paranoid template, a
  // hashtag finisher, and an image step onto a document job. The fixed
  // social plan below serves only unbound legacy callers; a standard job's
  // plan is written under its contract (see the note in the prompt).
  if (!options?.standardContract && isSocialPostRequest(title, notes)) return socialPostPlan(`${title}${notes ? ` — ${notes}` : ""}`);
  const standardContractNote = options?.standardContract
    ? `\n10. STANDARD OUTCOME CONTRACT — this job was created as a STANDARD job and its contract OVERRIDES rules 5, 5b, and 6 wherever they conflict: (a) the deliverable follows the job's own brief — a document, pack, list, or finished social posts as briefed; plan only the research and drafting steps the brief itself needs. (b) Do NOT plan the fixed Perfectly Paranoid social-post pipeline and do NOT use the Perfectly Paranoid template or voice in any step, unless the brief itself explicitly requests the Perfectly Paranoid voice. (c) HASHTAG CARVE-OUT: the no-hashtag rule applies to documents, letters, and reports — for those shapes, add NO hashtag finisher, hashtag block, or finisher step. BUT when the brief itself asks for finished social posts, the copy step you plan for Johnny MUST require each post to END with its strongest topic hashtags (3–5 top topic-specific tags, no filler, nothing after the block, per rule 5b) — hashtags live inside the post copy itself, never as a separate finisher step — and a post without that ending block is unfinished. So: posts get hashtags, documents don't; never apply one shape's rule to the other. (d) Do NOT add an image step (a step whose job is producing an image) unless the brief itself explicitly asks for an image or a visual deliverable; a step that builds the briefed deliverable itself (a document, a site, a mockup the brief names) is a build step, not an image step. (e) The source-first image rule in rule 6 applies only inside an image step the brief explicitly called for — it never creates one.`
    : "";
  const plainLanguageRule = options?.svenOriginated
    ? `\n7. Plain-language rule (this job came from one of Sven's ideas, so its finished package will be read by a person — possibly a client — who has never heard of AI agents): write every step so its documents come out readable by a smart business owner. Each step that produces a document must instruct the worker to (a) give the document a plain human title as its first heading — a short description of what it is, like "The offer sheet (one page, ready to send)", never an internal document-type name like "Commercial Spec" and never a file name; (b) begin the document with a section headed exactly "## In plain words" holding one or two plain sentences whose first sentence states the document's result — its finding, verdict, recommendation, or finished outcome — never a description of the document itself, what it is for, or what the reader should read it to learn (the title already says what it is); and (c) keep reader-facing wording free of crew jargon — no "agentic", no pipeline/brief/step/deliverable language. Working content and checking rigor stay exactly as demanding as usual; only titles, summaries, and reader-facing wording change.`
    : "";
  return ctx.inference.complete(
    `Act as Remmy, Ben's chief of staff. Break this job into the smallest ordered set of crew steps that produces one final result Ben can judge.

CREW — assign only these people, only for this work:
- Tom (scout): web research and verification of factual claims.
- Nik (forge): coding, building, design, and visual production.
- Johnny (quill): writing and copy.
- Sven (ledger): opportunity scouting, practical ideation, prioritization, tracking, and reconciliation.
Never assign Olivia (olivia): she drafts X posts only, through dedicated X Posts jobs and her Monday standing order.
Never assign Maria (maria): she heads the Front Office and handles client intake, delivery packages, and client reports through steps the office attaches itself — she is never part of a plan you write.

RULES FOR THE PLAN:
1. Steps run automatically in the order you list them, and each step's worker sees the completed results of the steps before it. Write every instruction so a worker starting fresh — with no memory of any earlier job — can execute it from the instruction plus those prior results alone.
2. One step when one specialist can do the whole job. Add a step only when the work genuinely crosses into another specialty listed above.
3. Never add approval, review, coordination, handoff, or status-reporting steps. Ben sees the combined result once, after the final step, and decides then.
4. Every instruction names its deliverable concretely: what is produced, in what form, and what it must contain or satisfy. Ban vague directives ("make it good", "handle appropriately") — if a requirement cannot be checked, rewrite it until it can.
5. Social-content rule: any Facebook or social-content job must include Johnny for the copy and must run in exactly this order — Tom researches and verifies, Johnny writes the finished post, Nik creates the image. Never omit the writer from a social-post job. Perfectly Paranoid copy uses its locked voice (dark and cynical, delivered dry; flat factual opening, dry aside, an explicit "Why is this a big deal?" stakes paragraph, quiet-hook close; verified facts only) — that voice applies to the Perfectly Paranoid copy step only, never to Johnny's other work.
5b. Hashtag-block rule (Ben, 2026-10-14 — applies to EVERY social copy step you write, Perfectly Paranoid and standard social alike): the step's instructions must require the finished post to END with a hashtag block — 3–5 top, topic-specific, most-searched niche tags chosen from that post's own subject, as the final line(s) containing only hashtags, after the closing hook, with nothing after them; no filler / reach-bait tags (#fyp, #viral, #trending, #explore, or similar) and no fixed generic set. State in the step that a post without that ending block is unfinished. For any non-social copy step, do not add this requirement.
6. Source-first image rule: any step that produces an image of a real thing must be written source-first — the worker searches for a suitable real-world photograph first (public-domain and freely licensed sources such as NASA and Wikimedia Commons preferred), downloads it into the job folder, inspects it, and records its provenance (source URL + license basis) in an image-provenance.md file and in the step result; AI generation is only the fallback when no suitable real photograph exists, and a generated fallback must be labeled "AI-generated (no suitable real image found)" in both places. Print-on-demand artwork is exempt — it is original art by definition.
7. Escalation rule for Tom steps: any step you assign to Tom (scout) for research or verification on a main-floor job must carry this clause, in plain words: Tom may escalate specific claims to the Research Department — contested, extraordinary, high-stakes-if-wrong, or unverifiable-downstairs claims only, ordinary claims never — by listing them in his result under the exact heading "${ESCALATION_HEADING}", one bullet per claim with a one-line reason; one escalation per job. Do not add a separate escalation, lab, or approval step to the plan — the office spawns the lab sub-case itself when Tom lists claims under that heading.
8. Social links check rule for research steps: whenever a step you assign to Tom (scout) researches or verifies a job whose subject is a business or a public page, that step's instructions must carry a mandatory SOCIAL LINKS CHECK clause with all of this content, in plain words: before reporting anything about the subject's social media presence — and before any verdict on whether a page exists or is verified — Tom must open the subject's OWN website and look for its social media links (header/footer icons first, then the contact and about pages); record every social profile URL found there exactly as linked, character-for-character, in the result under a "Social links found on their own site" heading with the website URL named; follow at least the Facebook link and record what it resolves to; if a social link is present on their own site but cannot be opened or resolved with his tools, report it exactly as "social link found on their own site — needs a live look" with the site URL, NEVER as a flat "not verified"; a "not verified" verdict for a business's or public page's social presence is acceptable only after the business's own website has been checked for social links and none were found there; if the subject has no website of its own that can be found, the step says exactly that. Do not add a separate social-links step to the plan — the check belongs inside the research step itself.
9. Verdict-first rule (house rule, every job, every step): write every step's instructions so its result text and every document it produces OPEN WITH THE RESULT — the first sentence states the finding, verdict, decision, recommendation, or finished outcome. A step whose document settles a question or makes a call must instruct the worker to put a section headed exactly "## Verdict" immediately after the document's title, whose first sentence is the verdict itself, before any reasoning or evidence. Never write, require, or allow an opening that describes the document or the work ("this document settles…", "this report covers…", "read it to know…") — the title already tells the reader what the thing is, and supporting detail always follows the verdict, never precedes it.${plainLanguageRule}${standardContractNote}

Job: ${title}

Details:
${notes || "No additional details."}`,
    { schema: workPlanShape },
  );
}

async function createPlannedWork(ctx: Ctx, values: {
  title: string; notes: string; steps: Array<PlanStep & { stage?: z.infer<typeof pipelineStage> }>; standingOrderId?: string | null; pipeline?: z.infer<typeof pipelineType> | null; clientId?: string | null; parentTaskId?: string | null;
  // Outcome contract binding: callers that create a job THROUGH one of the
  // seven job types pass that type, and the job is bound to its contract
  // here — snapshot stored on the task, contract text stamped into every
  // brief, and any planned step the contract forbids (an image step or a
  // finisher step on a type that forbids them) is dropped before it can
  // ever spawn. Callers that omit jobType (standing orders, lab sub-cases,
  // delivery packages, merch and other legacy flows) create unbound jobs
  // that finish under their current plans, untouched.
  jobType?: JobTypeValue | null;
  // Gathering mode (Change 2): research callers pass the mode chosen at
  // creation; every other caller leaves it unset and the job is standard.
  gatheringMode?: "standard" | "tiered" | null;
}): Promise<{ task: typeof schema.tasks.$inferSelect; briefs: Array<typeof schema.briefs.$inferSelect> } | null> {
  const db = ctx.db<typeof schema>(); const now = new Date(); const taskId = `task-${crypto.randomUUID()}`;
  const contract = values.jobType ? outcomeContractFor(values.jobType, `${values.title}\n${values.notes}`, Boolean(values.clientId)) : null;
  let steps = values.steps;
  if (contract) {
    const kept = steps.filter((step) => {
      if (isFinisherStep(step) && contract.hashtagRule !== "required") return false;
      if (isImageProductionStep(step) && (contract.imageRule === "none" || (contract.imageRule === "brief" && !contract.imageAllowed))) return false;
      return true;
    });
    // A plan reduced to nothing by its contract keeps its first step — the
    // deliverable follows the brief, and the contract block below tells the
    // worker exactly what shape it must take.
    if (kept.length > 0) steps = kept;
  }
  const first = steps[0];
  if (!first) return null;
  const contractBlock = contract ? contractBriefBlock(contract) : null;
  const taskRows = await db.insert(schema.tasks).values({
    id: taskId, title: values.title, assignee: first.assignee, notes: values.notes, status: "working", created: now,
    parentTaskId: values.parentTaskId ?? null, standingOrderId: values.standingOrderId ?? null, clientId: values.clientId ?? null,
    jobType: contract?.jobType ?? null, outcomeContract: contract ? JSON.stringify(contract) : null, contractStatus: null, contractViolation: null, contractBounces: 0,
    gatheringMode: values.gatheringMode ?? "standard",
    pipeline: values.pipeline ?? null, pipelineStage: null,
    publicationStatus: null, postCopy: null, postImagePath: null, postedUrl: null, approvedAt: null, postedAt: null, revision: 0,
  }).returning();
  const task = taskRows[0]; if (!task) return null;
  const briefs: Array<typeof schema.briefs.$inferSelect> = [];
  for (let index = 0; index < steps.length; index += 1) {
    const step = steps[index]; if (!step) continue;
    const rows = await db.insert(schema.briefs).values({
      id: `brief-${crypto.randomUUID()}`, taskId, title: step.title, assignee: step.assignee, notes: contractBlock ? `${step.instructions}\n\n${contractBlock}` : step.instructions,
      status: "new", result: null, createdAt: new Date(now.getTime() + index), updatedAt: now,
      pipeline: values.pipeline ?? null, pipelineStage: step.stage ?? null, runTaskId: null, progressText: "Queued by Remmy", lastHeartbeatAt: null, attempt: 0, stepIndex: index, revision: 0,
    }).returning();
    const brief = rows[0]; if (brief) briefs.push(brief);
  }
  return { task, briefs };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Front Office — Maria's department (clients & delivery).
//
// Intake: a client-tagged job gets ONE Maria step in front of its normal
// steps. She shapes the request into a job brief with the client's registry
// voice and constraints attached; the shaped brief rides into the pipeline
// through the usual completed-work handoff, so the floors execute exactly
// as they do for untagged work. Untagged jobs never see any of this.
//
// Delivery: approving a client-tagged job creates a delivery package and a
// small package job whose only step is Maria assembling the cover note.
// When she finishes, the package waits in Deliverables for Ben's one
// decision (approve → Delivered, or rework → back to Maria).
//
// Reporting: a per-client standing order (weekly / monthly, off by
// default). When it fires, Maria assembles the activity record from office
// data ONLY — the server builds that record from real rows before she ever
// sees it — and Johnny drafts the plain-language summary. Ben approves it
// as a normal job, and approval produces a delivery package as usual.
type FrontOfficeStep = PlanStep & { stage: z.infer<typeof pipelineStage> };

export function clientPhotoLibraryLine(client: Pick<typeof schema.clients.$inferSelect, "photoLibraryStatus" | "photoLibraryLocation">): string {
  if (client.photoLibraryStatus === "provided") {
    return client.photoLibraryLocation?.trim()
      ? `Provided — the client's own photos live at: ${client.photoLibraryLocation.trim()}`
      : "Provided — the client gave Pulse HQ their own photos (ask Maria where they live if the location is not recorded)";
  }
  if (client.photoLibraryStatus === "none") return "None provided — the client has no photo library to use; the shaped brief must say so explicitly";
  return "Not recorded yet — Maria asks for the client's own photos at intake and records the answer here";
}

function clientRegistryBlock(client: typeof schema.clients.$inferSelect): string {
  return [
    `Business: ${client.businessName}`,
    `The person who approves their work: ${client.approverName || "not recorded"}`,
    `Platforms they publish on: ${client.platforms || "not recorded"}`,
    `How they like to sound (their voice notes): ${client.voiceNotes || "none recorded"}`,
    `Photo library (client's own photos of their business, place, and products): ${clientPhotoLibraryLine(client)}`,
    `Relationship status: ${client.status}`,
    `Showcase permission: ${client.showcasePermission ? "YES — Pulse HQ may showcase this client's finished work" : "NO — Pulse HQ may not showcase this client's work"}`,
  ].join("\n");
}

// The standing downstream rule for client photos: when a client provided
// their own photos, every image step on their jobs uses those first —
// real photos of the real business beat a generated stand-in every time.
// Generated imagery stays available only as the labelled fallback.
export function clientPhotoPreferenceBlock(client: Pick<typeof schema.clients.$inferSelect, "businessName" | "photoLibraryStatus" | "photoLibraryLocation">): string | null {
  if (client.photoLibraryStatus !== "provided") return null;
  const where = client.photoLibraryLocation?.trim() ? ` They live at: ${client.photoLibraryLocation.trim()}.` : "";
  return `CLIENT PHOTO LIBRARY — USE THE CLIENT'S OWN PHOTOS FIRST: ${client.businessName} provided their own photo library at onboarding — real photos of their business, place, and products.${where} Any image step on this job MUST prefer those provided photos when one fits: use the client's real photo, not a generated stand-in for their real place or products. Generated imagery is the labelled fallback only, used only when no provided photo fits, and recorded as AI-generated in the provenance exactly as the source-first rule requires. A provided client photo is recorded in image-provenance.md as a real photograph with its source noted as the client's own photo library.`;
}

function mariaIntakeStep(client: typeof schema.clients.$inferSelect, title: string, notes: string): FrontOfficeStep {
  return {
    assignee: "maria",
    stage: "intake",
    title: `Client intake — shape the brief: ${title}`.slice(0, 120),
    instructions: `You are Maria, head of the Front Office at Pulse HQ. This is the intake step of a client job: it runs FIRST, before any other crew step, and the brief you shape here is what the rest of the crew works from.

THE CLIENT, from the registry (this is the source of truth for anything about the client — if a detail is not here, it is not known):
${clientRegistryBlock(client)}

THE REQUEST, exactly as it came in:
Title: ${title}
${notes ? `Details:\n${notes}` : "No extra details supplied."}

DEFINITIONS:
- "The shaped brief" is a working brief for the crew steps that follow: the original request restated completely, with the client's voice and constraints from the registry applied to it — tone, platforms, anything their notes say to always do or never do.
- A "constraint" is anything in the registry that limits or directs the work (a platform the work must fit, a phrase or topic to avoid, an approval habit). Voice notes are constraints, not decoration.
- The "photo library" is the client's OWN photos — real photos of their business, their place, and their products that the client handed over. It is not stock photography and it is not generated imagery.

WHAT TO DO:
1. Restate the request in full — nothing from the original request is dropped, shortened away, or replaced with your summary of it.
2. Apply the client's registry voice and constraints to it: name each constraint and say exactly how it changes this job (for example: posts must fit the platforms listed; wording follows the voice notes).
3. PHOTO LIBRARY — a standing onboarding step, on every intake, the same standing as the voice and platform items above: ask for and record the client's own photo library — real photos of their business, place, and products. Carry the registry's photo-library line into the shaped brief exactly as it stands, under a plain heading "Photo library": if photos were provided, say so and say where they live, exactly as recorded; if none were provided, the shaped brief says explicitly, in plain words, that no client photos were provided. If the status is "not recorded yet", the shaped brief says the photo library still needs to be asked for at onboarding — never leave the item out and never guess an answer. Then state what it means for THIS job: when photos were provided, every image step on this job prefers the client's provided photos when one fits, and generated imagery is the labelled fallback only; when none were provided, image work follows the office's normal source-first rule with generated imagery as its labelled fallback.
4. End with what "done" looks like for this client: the finished pieces the crew must produce, in plain words.

DEFINITION OF DONE — all four are true:
- The shaped brief contains the complete original request AND every applicable registry constraint, each with how it applies to this job.
- The shaped brief contains the "Photo library" item exactly as the WHAT TO DO step requires: provided-and-where, explicitly none, or explicitly still-to-ask — never omitted, never invented.
- The shaped brief is saved as a file named client-brief.md in this job's folder, and your result is that same shaped brief, word for word.
- Nothing about the client appears in the brief that is not in the registry block above — no invented preferences, history, photos, or promises.

IF THE REGISTRY AND THE REQUEST CONFLICT (the request asks for something the client's notes rule out): keep both visible in the shaped brief, flag the conflict in plain words at the top, and let the crew and Ben see it — never silently pick a side, and never invent a client detail to fill a gap.`,
  };
}

function mariaAssemblyStep(client: typeof schema.clients.$inferSelect, sourceTask: typeof schema.tasks.$inferSelect): FrontOfficeStep {
  const isPost = sourceTask.pipeline === "perfectly_paranoid";
  return {
    assignee: "maria",
    stage: "assembly",
    title: `Assemble the delivery package: ${sourceTask.title}`.slice(0, 120),
    instructions: `You are Maria, head of the Front Office at Pulse HQ. The job below is finished and approved. Your step assembles its DELIVERY PACKAGE — the client-ready bundle Ben will approve once in Deliverables.

THE CLIENT, from the registry:
${clientRegistryBlock(client)}

THE FINISHED JOB:
Title: ${sourceTask.title}
Its finished files live in its job folder: ~/workspace/ai-office/jobs/${sourceTask.id}/ — read the folder and the finished pieces in it before writing anything, so the cover note describes the work that actually exists, never the work that was planned.
${isPost ? "This job is a social post package: the finished post copy is part of the package, and its posting status matters — it is approved and waiting to be posted; the package's cover note should say so in plain words." : ""}

WHAT TO DO:
1. Write the package's COVER NOTE in plain language a client understands with no explanation: what was made, what it is for, and what the client does with it next. One short page at most. No crew language — no pipelines, briefs, steps, or deliverables-as-machinery; say "the finished work" or name the pieces themselves.
2. Save a file named delivery-package.md in THIS package job's folder listing: the cover note, then the exact file names of the finished pieces from the source job's folder that the package contains.
3. Your result is the cover note itself, word for word — the office stores it on the package Ben reads.

REVISING A FINISHED PIECE (when Ben's feedback changes a finished piece itself — the words of the post, for example, like adding hashtags): the package Ben reads is built from the finished pieces themselves, so the revision has to BE in a piece — a cover note saying the change was made does not change anything Ben sees. Save the revised piece in THIS package job's folder under the same file name as the original, with the complete revised text: for a post, the full revised copy under its \`## PUBLICATION-READY POST COPY\` heading, ending with its hashtag block and followed by the \`---\` line, exactly as the original file is shaped. When you finish, the office carries that saved revision into the package automatically.

DEFINITION OF DONE — all three are true:
- The cover note describes only finished work you actually found in the source job's folder.
- delivery-package.md exists in this job's folder and names the real finished files.
- The cover note is plain client language throughout and states, where it applies, the posting status in plain words.

IF THE FINISHED WORK CANNOT BE FOUND in the source job's folder: say exactly that in your result instead of writing a cover note for work you could not see — a package must never describe work that is not there.`,
  };
}

// The activity record for a client report is built HERE, from real office
// rows only: jobs for this client and their states, packages delivered,
// post packages marked posted. If it did not happen in the office data, it
// is not in the record, and no worker downstream may add to it.
async function clientActivityRecord(ctx: Ctx, client: typeof schema.clients.$inferSelect): Promise<string> {
  const db = ctx.db<typeof schema>();
  const [clientTasks, clientPackages] = await Promise.all([
    db.select().from(schema.tasks).where(eq(schema.tasks.clientId, client.id)).orderBy(desc(schema.tasks.created)),
    db.select().from(schema.deliveryPackages).where(eq(schema.deliveryPackages.clientId, client.id)).orderBy(desc(schema.deliveryPackages.createdAt)),
  ]);
  const workTasks = clientTasks.filter((task) => task.pipeline !== "client_delivery" && task.pipeline !== "client_report");
  const completed = workTasks.filter((task) => task.status === "done");
  const inProgress = workTasks.filter((task) => task.status === "working");
  const delivered = clientPackages.filter((pkg) => pkg.status === "delivered");
  const posted = workTasks.filter((task) => task.postedAt);
  const fmt = (value: Date) => value.toISOString().slice(0, 10);
  const lines = [
    `Activity record for ${client.businessName} — built from Pulse HQ office records only. Every line below is a real office record; anything not listed here did not happen in the office data.`,
    "",
    `Jobs completed for this client: ${completed.length}`,
    ...completed.map((task) => `- ${task.title} (finished; approved ${task.approvedAt ? fmt(task.approvedAt) : "date not recorded"})`),
    `Jobs currently being worked: ${inProgress.length}`,
    ...inProgress.map((task) => `- ${task.title}`),
    `Delivery packages delivered: ${delivered.length}`,
    ...delivered.map((pkg) => `- ${pkg.title} (delivered ${pkg.deliveredAt ? fmt(pkg.deliveredAt) : "date not recorded"})`),
    `Post packages marked posted: ${posted.length}`,
    ...posted.map((task) => `- ${task.title} (marked posted ${task.postedAt ? fmt(task.postedAt) : "date not recorded"})`),
  ];
  return lines.join("\n");
}

function mariaReportStep(client: typeof schema.clients.$inferSelect, record: string): FrontOfficeStep {
  return {
    assignee: "maria",
    stage: "report",
    title: `Assemble the activity record: ${client.businessName}`.slice(0, 120),
    instructions: `You are Maria, head of the Front Office at Pulse HQ. This is step 1 of a client report for ${client.businessName}: you assemble the activity record; Johnny drafts the client's summary from it next.

THE ACTIVITY RECORD, built from office data only:
${record}

WHAT TO DO:
1. Check the record over: every line must be one of the office facts above, restated cleanly — same jobs, same counts, same dates.
2. Save it as client-activity-record.md in this job's folder and return the identical record as your result.

DEFINITION OF DONE — both are true:
- Your result and the saved file contain exactly the office facts above: no added job, count, date, result, or outcome of any kind.
- The record is readable by a person: one fact per line, plain words.

IF THE RECORD IS EMPTY of completed work: return it as it stands, saying plainly that there is nothing completed to report yet. An honest empty record is a finished step; an invented achievement is a failed one.`,
  };
}

function johnnyReportStep(client: typeof schema.clients.$inferSelect): FrontOfficeStep {
  return {
    assignee: "quill",
    stage: "report",
    title: `Draft the client summary: ${client.businessName}`.slice(0, 120),
    instructions: `You are Johnny, Pulse HQ's writer. This is step 2 of a client report for ${client.businessName}: Maria's assembled activity record is in the completed work above, and it is the ONLY source of facts for this summary.

THE CLIENT, from the registry:
${clientRegistryBlock(client)}

TASK: Draft the client's report summary in plain, warm, everyday language — a short note the client reads in one sitting: what Pulse HQ finished for them in this period, what was delivered, what was posted, and what is still being worked on. Write to the client (second person, their business named naturally), in the voice their registry notes describe where they give one. VERDICT FIRST: the summary's first sentence states the period's headline result — what Pulse HQ finished and delivered for them — and never opens by describing the report itself; the heading already says what it is.

DEFINITION OF DONE — all three are true:
- Every fact, count, and date in the summary appears in Maria's activity record. Nothing is rounded up, combined into a bigger number, or added — no results, reach, sales, or praise the record does not contain.
- The summary is finished and sendable as-is: no placeholders, no notes to the office inside it.
- The summary is saved as client-report.md in this job's folder and your result is that same summary, word for word.

IF THE RECORD SHOWS NOTHING COMPLETED: write the honest short version — what is under way and that the first finished pieces are still to come. Never pad a quiet period into a busy one.`,
  };
}

function nextClientReportAt(cadence: "weekly" | "monthly", from: Date): Date {
  if (cadence === "weekly") return nextScheduledRun(from, "weekly", 1, 9, 0, "America/Vancouver");
  const parts = localDateParts(from, "America/Vancouver");
  const nextMonth = parts.month === 12 ? { year: parts.year + 1, month: 1, day: 1 } : { year: parts.year, month: parts.month + 1, day: 1 };
  return localWallTimeToInstant(nextMonth, 9, 0, "America/Vancouver");
}

async function createClientReportJob(ctx: Ctx, client: typeof schema.clients.$inferSelect, origin: "schedule" | "manual"): Promise<boolean> {
  const db = ctx.db<typeof schema>();
  const openReports = await db.select({ id: schema.tasks.id }).from(schema.tasks)
    .where(and(eq(schema.tasks.clientId, client.id), eq(schema.tasks.pipeline, "client_report"), eq(schema.tasks.status, "working")));
  if (openReports.length > 0) return false;
  const record = await clientActivityRecord(ctx, client);
  const title = `Client report — ${client.businessName}`.slice(0, 120);
  const notes = `Recurring client report for ${client.businessName} (${origin === "manual" ? "started by hand" : "from the client's reporting order"}). Maria assembles the activity record from office data only; Johnny drafts the plain-language summary; the finished report is approved like any other job and then becomes a delivery package for the client.`;
  const created = await createPlannedWork(ctx, {
    title, notes, clientId: client.id, pipeline: "client_report", jobType: "client_report",
    steps: [mariaReportStep(client, record), johnnyReportStep(client)],
  });
  if (!created) return false;
  await db.insert(schema.activityLog).values({ t: new Date(), text: origin === "manual"
    ? `A client report for ${client.businessName} was started by hand — Maria is assembling the activity record from office data.`
    : `The reporting order for ${client.businessName} fired — Maria is assembling the activity record from office data.` });
  await startNextForTask(ctx, created.task.id);
  return true;
}

// Approving a client-tagged job (the one place that event is known) spawns
// its delivery package: a package row in Deliverables plus a small
// package job whose only step is Maria's assembly. Idempotent per source
// job — a job produces at most one package, ever.
async function createDeliveryPackageForTask(ctx: Ctx, task: typeof schema.tasks.$inferSelect): Promise<void> {
  if (!task.clientId) return;
  // PERFECTLY PARANOID IS HOUSE CONTENT (Ben's routing ruling,
  // 2026-10-16): jobs tagged to Client #1 NEVER assemble a delivery
  // package — PP posts exit through To post like untagged posts and PP
  // reports exit as plain report deliverables. This backstop sits at the
  // one place every package is born, so no approval path can package a
  // PP job. External clients are untouched.
  if (task.clientId === PERFECTLY_PARANOID_CLIENT_ID) return;
  // CLIENT REPORT GUARANTEE — defence in depth: a client job carrying a
  // "client report missing" violation never gets a delivery package, even
  // if an approval path other than set_task_status reaches here.
  if (task.contractStatus === "bounced" && task.contractViolation?.includes("client report missing")) return;
  const db = ctx.db<typeof schema>();
  const existing = await db.select({ id: schema.deliveryPackages.id }).from(schema.deliveryPackages).where(eq(schema.deliveryPackages.taskId, task.id)).limit(1);
  if (existing[0]) return;
  const clientRows = await db.select().from(schema.clients).where(eq(schema.clients.id, task.clientId)).limit(1);
  const client = clientRows[0];
  if (!client) return;
  const now = new Date();
  const packageRows = await db.insert(schema.deliveryPackages).values({
    id: `pkg-${crypto.randomUUID()}`, clientId: client.id, taskId: task.id, packageTaskId: null,
    title: task.title, coverNote: null,
    postingStatus: task.pipeline === "perfectly_paranoid" ? "Approved — waiting to be posted" : null,
    status: "assembling", createdAt: now, updatedAt: now, deliveredAt: null,
  }).returning();
  const pkg = packageRows[0];
  if (!pkg) return;
  const created = await createPlannedWork(ctx, {
    title: `Delivery package — ${task.title}`.slice(0, 120),
    notes: `Maria assembles the delivery package for ${client.businessName} from the approved job “${task.title}”.`,
    clientId: client.id, pipeline: "client_delivery", parentTaskId: task.id,
    steps: [mariaAssemblyStep(client, task)],
  });
  if (created) {
    await db.update(schema.deliveryPackages).set({ packageTaskId: created.task.id, updatedAt: new Date() }).where(eq(schema.deliveryPackages.id, pkg.id));
    await db.insert(schema.activityLog).values({ t: now, text: `Maria is assembling a delivery package for ${client.businessName}: “${task.title}”. It will wait in Deliverables for your one decision.` });
    await startNextForTask(ctx, created.task.id);
  }
  ctx.invalidateQueries();
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------
// THE PIPELINE ROUTES (Ben, 2026-10-18): every job type has exactly
// ONE route to Ben, and arrival in Ready for You happens only by
// passing the final gate of that route — never by default, never by
// falling through.
//   · Manual jobs (untagged, or tagged to Perfectly Paranoid — house
//     content whose client IS Ben): steps complete → outcome-contract
//     check passes → surface ONCE in Ready for You for his decision.
//   · Standing orders: complete → Done/activity. The approval state
//     is unreachable for a standing-order run (enforced on every
//     finish path, plus the poll_dispatch sweep).
//   · Client-tagged jobs (external clients): finish → the client's
//     delivery package. The package in Deliverables is the decision
//     item; the individual job NEVER surfaces loose in Ready for You.
//     This helper is that route: it closes the job to Done and hands
//     it to Maria's package assembly (createDeliveryPackageForTask).
//     The one exception is a job STUCK on its outcome-contract check
//     (bounce budget spent): it cannot be packaged, so it surfaces in
//     Ready for You as a stuck item — a problem addressed to Ben, like
//     a blocker — where he can rework or delete it.
//   · Blockers reach Ready for You only when genuinely addressed to
//     Ben (an open blocker on a manual or client job; standing-order
//     blockers are recorded in history instead, at report time).
// Returns true when the job took the client route (caller is done).
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------
function isExternalClientJob(task: { clientId: string | null }): boolean {
  return Boolean(task.clientId) && task.clientId !== PERFECTLY_PARANOID_CLIENT_ID;
}

function isStuckOnContract(task: { contractStatus: string | null; contractBounces: number }): boolean {
  return isBounceExhausted(task.contractStatus, task.contractBounces);
}

async function routeFinishedClientJob(ctx: Ctx, task: typeof schema.tasks.$inferSelect, assignee: string): Promise<void> {
  const db = ctx.db<typeof schema>();
  const now = new Date();
  const clientRows = task.clientId ? await db.select({ businessName: schema.clients.businessName }).from(schema.clients).where(eq(schema.clients.id, task.clientId)).limit(1) : [];
  const clientName = clientRows[0]?.businessName ?? "the client";
  await db.batch([
    db.update(schema.tasks).set({ status: "done", assignee }).where(eq(schema.tasks.id, task.id)),
    db.insert(schema.activityLog).values({ t: now, text: `${memberByAssignee(assignee)} finished “${task.title}” for ${clientName}. Client work never waits loose in Ready for You — Maria is assembling its delivery package, and the package in Deliverables is the one decision.` }),
  ]);
  await createDeliveryPackageForTask(ctx, task);
  ctx.invalidateQueries();
}

// Package post-copy sync — the package Ben reads in Deliverables is
// rendered from the SOURCE job's stored post copy, never from files in the
// package job's own folder. When a package rework changes the post itself
// (adding a hashtag block, say), Maria saves the revised copy in the
// package job's folder; without this sync her revision — and her cover
// note saying it was made — never reaches the package Ben sees (the
// Dyatlov Day 3 rework, 2026-10-14: tags saved in her folder, package
// still showed the tag-less copy). So whenever Maria's package step
// finishes, any publication-ready copy staged in the package job's folder
// that differs from the source job's stored copy is validated against the
// hashtag gate and written back onto the source job, where the package
// card, Deliverables, and the copy Ben pastes all read it from.
async function syncPackagePostCopy(ctx: Ctx, packageTaskId: string, resultText: string): Promise<{ outcome: "synced" | "unchanged" } | { outcome: "invalid"; error: string }> {
  const db = ctx.db<typeof schema>();
  const pkgRows = await db.select().from(schema.deliveryPackages).where(eq(schema.deliveryPackages.packageTaskId, packageTaskId)).limit(1);
  const pkg = pkgRows[0];
  if (!pkg) return { outcome: "unchanged" };
  const sourceRows = await db.select().from(schema.tasks).where(eq(schema.tasks.id, pkg.taskId)).limit(1);
  const sourceTask = sourceRows[0];
  if (!sourceTask || sourceTask.pipeline !== "perfectly_paranoid") return { outcome: "unchanged" };
  const staged = await captureSocialPostCopy(ctx, packageTaskId, resultText);
  if (!staged || staged === sourceTask.postCopy) return { outcome: "unchanged" };
  const hashtagError = hashtagBlockError(staged, "facebook");
  if (hashtagError) return { outcome: "invalid", error: hashtagError };
  await db.update(schema.tasks).set({ postCopy: staged }).where(eq(schema.tasks.id, sourceTask.id));
  await db.insert(schema.activityLog).values({ t: new Date(), text: `Maria's package work revised the finished post copy on “${sourceTask.title}” — the package in Deliverables now carries the revised copy.` });
  return { outcome: "synced" };
}
