function mediaProcessingPolicy(brief: typeof schema.briefs.$inferSelect, task: typeof schema.tasks.$inferSelect | undefined, clientPhotoBlock?: string | null): string {
  const pipeline = brief.pipeline ?? task?.pipeline ?? null;
  const context = `${task?.title ?? ""}\n${task?.notes ?? ""}\n${brief.title}\n${brief.notes}`;
  const isSocialPost = pipeline === "perfectly_paranoid" || /\b(?:facebook|perfectly paranoid|social (?:post|image|story))\b/i.test(context);
  const isPodDesign = pipeline === "merch_upload" || /\b(?:pod|print[ -]?on[ -]?demand|merch(?:andise)?|t[ -]?shirts?|tees?|redbubble|teepublic)\b/i.test(context);
  const withClientPhotos = (policy: string): string => clientPhotoBlock ? `${clientPhotoBlock}\n\n${policy}` : policy;
  // Outcome contract: a contract-bound job whose contract forbids images
  // gets NO image machinery at run time at all — not the source-first rule,
  // not a fallback, nothing. The deliverable is words; an attached image is
  // a contract violation that bounces it before it can surface.
  const boundContract = contractForTask(task);
  if (boundContract && (boundContract.imageRule === "none" || (boundContract.imageRule === "brief" && !boundContract.imageAllowed))) {
    return `MEDIA PIPELINE — OUTCOME CONTRACT (${boundContract.label}): this job's contract FORBIDS image steps and attached images. Do NOT create, generate, source, download, or attach any image for this job, and do not record image provenance — there is no image in this deliverable, by contract. If some habit or generic workflow suggests adding one, the contract wins: the finished deliverable is checked against it before it can surface, and an attached image bounces it back. Do the work in words, exactly as the brief asks.`;
  }
  // Aspect control: a rework brief carrying the generate-direct marker gets
  // a policy that AGREES with the approver's one-off instruction instead of
  // silently re-imposing the source-first default below. This branch is the
  // only place the default is lifted, it lifts it for this brief's run
  // only, and provenance stays mandatory: the generated image is recorded
  // in image-provenance.md with "Kind: generated" and in the result with
  // the standard AI-generated IMAGE PROVENANCE line, so the approval card
  // labels it AI-generated.
  if (brief.notes.includes(REWORK_GENERATE_DIRECT_MARKER)) {
    const overridePolicy = `MEDIA PIPELINE — ${REWORK_GENERATE_DIRECT_MARKER}: the approver's special instructions for the image on this rework explicitly say to generate the image directly. That instruction OVERRIDES the source-first image rule for THIS RUN ONLY — do NOT search for a real photograph first, and do not let any source-first wording in your worker contract or elsewhere change that. Generate the image directly, based on the finished post and the approver's instructions, inspect it before delivering, and save it exactly as produced, with its full background kept. PROVENANCE IS STILL MANDATORY: record the image in image-provenance.md in this job's folder with a block naming the exact file ("Image: <file name>") and "Kind: generated", and put the standard line in your result: "IMAGE PROVENANCE: AI-generated (no suitable real image found) — <file name>", so the approval card labels it AI-generated. The standing source-first default is unchanged for every other run — this override never becomes a setting.`;
    if (isPodDesign) return overridePolicy;
    return withClientPhotos(`${overridePolicy}\n\nTransparency processing is forbidden on this job — no transparency tool, no background removal, no alpha masks, no cutouts. The deliverable is a normal opaque image with its full background.`);
  }
  if (pipeline === "creative_package") {
    return withClientPhotos("MEDIA PIPELINE — CREATIVE PACKAGE: These are DESIGNED visuals for a campaign package, created as original designs — the office's source-first real-photograph rule does NOT apply to this job, and no image provenance record is required for them. Build the visuals to match the campaign concept and copy in the completed work. NEVER invent a client logo, product shot, or brand mark: use only brand assets supplied with this job, and where a needed asset was not supplied, leave a clearly marked placeholder box labelled exactly \"PLACEHOLDER — [the asset] to be supplied by the client\" in its place. Where the client provided their own photos (see the client photo library note above, when present), use those real photos for anything that should show the client's real place or products instead of inventing them. Do not use transparency or background-removal processing unless a visual's design genuinely calls for it; deliver each visual exactly as designed, with its full background kept where it has one.");
  }
  if (isSocialPost) {
    return withClientPhotos(`MEDIA PIPELINE — SOCIAL POST: ${SOURCE_FIRST_IMAGE_RULE}\n\nSave the delivered image (real photograph or generated fallback) exactly as sourced or produced, with the full background kept. Transparency processing is forbidden on this job — that means no transparency tool, no background removal, no alpha masks, no cutouts. The deliverable is a normal opaque editorial image suitable for Facebook. This rule overrides any generic design workflow that suggests otherwise.`);
  }
  if (isPodDesign) {
    return "MEDIA PIPELINE — PRINT-ON-DEMAND: This is the one pipeline where transparency processing is allowed: you may use transparency or background-removal tools when they help produce print-ready artwork. Done requires inspecting the processed output before delivering it — check the edges and that no part of the design was eaten away. Print-on-demand designs are original art by definition, so the office's source-first image rule does not apply here: never substitute a found photograph for an original design.";
  }
  return withClientPhotos(`MEDIA PIPELINE — STANDARD: ${SOURCE_FIRST_IMAGE_RULE}\n\nDo not use transparency or background-removal processing on this job. Those tools are reserved for print-on-demand artwork only; deliver images exactly as sourced or produced, with their full backgrounds.`);
}

// Skill pool (~/workspace/ai-office/skill-pool/<skill-name>/SKILL.md):
// plain files Ben owns, one folder per skill. The index is rebuilt fresh
// from the pool folders every time a worker is spawned, so dropping a new
// folder into the pool is enough for it to appear in the next brief's
// wrapper — no code change. Only the one-line index (name + "Use when:"
// trigger + path) rides along in every run; a worker reads a SKILL.md in
// full only when its trigger matches the job. The pool is read-only for
// workers: they may read any skill file but never write to the pool.
const SKILL_POOL_RULE = "Before starting, check the skill index. If a skill's trigger matches your job, read that SKILL.md in full and follow it. If a skill conflicts with your contract, the contract wins and note the conflict in your result.";

async function skillPoolSection(ctx: Ctx): Promise<string> {
  let entries: Array<{ name: string; trigger: string; relativePath: string }> = [];
  try {
    const listed = await ctx.executePrivileged(privileged.listSkillPool, {});
    entries = listed.entries;
  } catch {
    entries = [];
  }
  if (!entries.length) {
    return `SKILL POOL:\n${SKILL_POOL_RULE}\nThe skill pool is currently empty, so no skill applies to this job. The pool is read-only: never write, edit, move, or delete any file under ~/workspace/ai-office/skill-pool/.`;
  }
  const lines = entries.map((entry) => `- ${entry.name} — Use when: ${entry.trigger} — File: ~/workspace/ai-office/${entry.relativePath}`);
  return `SKILL POOL — index (one line per skill; full text is NOT included):\n${SKILL_POOL_RULE}\nRead a skill file only when its trigger matches this job; if no trigger matches, proceed without reading any skill file. The pool is read-only: you may read any skill file, but never write, edit, move, or delete any file under ~/workspace/ai-office/skill-pool/.\n${lines.join("\n")}`;
}

async function spawnWorker(ctx: Ctx, brief: typeof schema.briefs.$inferSelect): Promise<{ ok: boolean; taskId?: string }> {
  const parsed = memberId.safeParse(brief.assignee); const worker = parsed.success ? parsed.data : "remmy";
  const db = ctx.db<typeof schema>();
  const taskRows = await db.select().from(schema.tasks).where(eq(schema.tasks.id, brief.taskId)).limit(1);
  const task = taskRows[0];
  // Client photo preference: a client-tagged job whose client provided
  // their own photos carries that preference into every run's media
  // policy, so downstream image steps use the client's real photos first.
  let clientPhotoBlock: string | null = null;
  if (task?.clientId) {
    const clientRows = await db.select().from(schema.clients).where(eq(schema.clients.id, task.clientId)).limit(1);
    if (clientRows[0]) clientPhotoBlock = clientPhotoPreferenceBlock(clientRows[0]);
  }
  const mediaPolicy = mediaProcessingPolicy(brief, task, clientPhotoBlock);
  const skillPool = await skillPoolSection(ctx);
  const outputContract = task?.pipeline === "x_posts"
    ? `X POST OUTPUT — DEFINITION OF DONE: the posts are drafted exactly as your instructions specify AND saved by one call to save_x_posts with this brief id, this job id, and posts as objects { text, imagePath }. Before that call, check every post against this list — the server enforces it and rejects the whole save on any single failure:
- ${X_POST_MAX_CHARS} characters or fewer INCLUDING hashtags. Count every character; an over-limit post cannot be saved.
- Scope is Pulse HQ capabilities ONLY (the AI office, the Research Department and its case files, the done-for-you social media management offer and 14-day pilot, build-in-public milestones) — never Perfectly Paranoid, Skunk Tools, or personal content.
- Facts are real events and real numbers taken from the material in your instructions only; never invent clients, testimonials, results, or metrics.
- The words Ben, Benjamin, or Skunk appear nowhere in the text or the hashtags — write as the Pulse HQ brand.
- Attraction grammar: marketing copy, not a status update — a strong opening hook, second-person address, a benefit or curiosity gap, short punchy lines, and a closing call to action before the hashtag block.
- Hashtag block, always — INCOMPLETE WITHOUT IT: every post ENDS with a hashtag block (final line, only hashtags, nothing after it) of 1–3 top topic-specific tags for that post, counted inside the 280-character limit. ${HASHTAG_RULE_X} A post missing that block, ending on prose after its tags, or carrying a filler tag (#fyp, #viral, #trending, #explore, or similar) cannot be saved and the brief cannot finish — the same standing as a post missing its link or image.
- Image or link, always: either the text includes a link (${X_SHOWCASE_LINK} or another relevant link from your instructions) and imagePath is null, OR the text has no link and imagePath is the path of an image you generated during this job, saved as-is under ~/workspace/ai-office/jobs/${brief.taskId}/ and inspected by you. A post with neither cannot be saved and the brief cannot finish.
Never log into X, use an API, or publish — the Post Queue is the deliverable.`
    : task?.pipeline === "research_case"
    ? brief.pipelineStage === "claim_check"
      ? "RESEARCH DEPT OUTPUT — CLAIM-CHECK. Done means all of these exist: (1) the claim manifest, recorded FIRST with save_claim_manifest — every claim Walter extracted, in order, with its exact text, source references, and a role tag (central / decision-critical / supporting / contextual); the server assigns stable IDs CC-001, CC-002, … and saves claim-manifest.md in this job's folder; (2) the grades, saved with save_claim_grade_chunk in deterministic chunks of at most 15 claims in manifest order as each chunk is graded — every claim ending with exactly one disposition (STRONG / SUPPORTED / SHAKY / MISFRAMED, or UNTRACEABLE for a claim the Verifier labeled NOT VERIFIED, or UNGRADED with its specific recorded reason) and a one-line reason naming the deciding test(s); on a resume, grade only the claims get_claim_grading_state shows as still missing — never try to change a recorded grade, a conflicting overwrite is a reconciliation failure; (3) a closing reconcile_claim_grades call, whose verdict is the grading's completeness: complete only when every manifest ID has exactly one non-UNGRADED disposition; (4) your result grades every claim under its CC ID — followed by the grade tallies and a demoted list naming every SHAKY and MISFRAMED claim again with its reason — and the identical grading saved as claim-check.md in this job's folder. If the reconciliation is not complete, your result and claim-check.md state GRADING INCOMPLETE in plain words and list the unaccounted claim IDs — a partial grading is never presented as complete. The grading opens with its plain human title heading, then a section headed exactly `## In plain words` holding one or two plain sentences that state the grading outcome — the tallies in plain words (how many claims were checked, and how many came out strong, supported, shaky, and misframed) and what that leaves standing. That lead carries NO byline and NO stage narration: never \"Claim-checker: Peter\", never a department name, never \"Stage 3 of 4\" — who graded it and how belongs in the working content, not the lead. This pass is independent of the Verifier's check: the Verifier's labels stand exactly as written, and any grade that turns on methodology is decided from the source itself, opened by you."
      : worker === "walter"
      ? "RESEARCH DEPT OUTPUT — READER. Done means all of these exist: (1) your result is the full claim-by-claim extraction — for each claim: the claim, the evidence offered for it, and the exact source URL; (2) the same extraction saved as reader-extraction.md in this job's folder; (3) a provenance record for EVERY gathered source, saved with save_source_provenance at gather time — publisher, document type, publication date or vintage, primary-vs-secondary, and independence — with, in tiered gathering mode, the primary-retrieval outcome recorded on each secondary source whose claim-bearing figures were sought at the primary tier. The extraction opens with its plain human title heading, then a section headed exactly `## In plain words` holding one or two plain sentences that say what the gathered claims amount to — how many claims, and what they cover — and your claim count stated on the extraction's first line after that lead. No conclusions and no verdicts anywhere in it — checking is Peter's desk, next. The plain-words lead carries NO byline and NO process narration: never \"Reader: Walter\", never a department name, never \"Stage 1 of 3\" — who gathered it and how belongs in the working content, not the lead."
      : worker === "peter"
        ? "RESEARCH DEPT OUTPUT — VERIFIER. Done means both of these exist and are identical: (1) your result lists every claim Walter extracted, each with exactly one label (DOCUMENTED / MAINSTREAM INTERPRETATION / FRINGE CLAIM / NOT VERIFIED) and one line of reasoning; (2) the same list saved as verifier-check.md in this job's folder. The check opens with its plain human title heading, then a section headed exactly `## In plain words` holding one or two plain sentences that state what held up — the tally in plain words: how many claims were DOCUMENTED, how many carried each other label, and whether anything failed checking. That lead carries NO byline and NO method line: never \"Verifier: Peter\", never a department name, never \"Pulse HQ Method:\" — your method and your name belong in the working content, not the lead. Every NOT VERIFIED claim is listed a second time at the end under a DO-NOT-PUBLISH heading. A claim whose source you could not open is NOT VERIFIED — never passed on trust."
        : "RESEARCH DEPT OUTPUT — BRIEF. Done means both of these exist and are identical: (1) your result is the complete case brief in the case-file structure from your instructions; (2) the same brief saved as research-brief.md in this job's folder. The brief opens with a section headed exactly `## SUMMARY` — genuinely short (one screen): the research question on one line, the short answer / verdict in 2–4 sentences, the top 3 verified facts as bullets, a \"Failed checking\" bullet list of headline claims that failed verification (write \"None\" if nothing failed), and the claim-check tally in plain words (how many claims were checked, and how many came out strong, supported, shaky, and misframed — with the line that the verdict rests only on the strong and supported claims) plus a plain statement of any research question the surviving claims could not answer — before the case-file sections. The SUMMARY's short answer / verdict paragraph IS this piece's plain summary: it states the answer itself, never the research question restated and never a description of the brief. GRADING COMPLETENESS GATE: check get_claim_grading_state for this job before writing — if the reconciliation is GRADING INCOMPLETE, the brief opens, before the `## SUMMARY` section, with the grading-incomplete banner the reconciliation returns (it lists the unaccounted claim IDs), the SUMMARY's tally states the incomplete count in plain words, and no ungraded or unaccounted claim carries any weight in the brief; the server stamps the same banner onto the finished brief if it is missing, so write it yourself, in place, the first time. CLAIM-CHECK GATE: the verdict and the top verified facts rest ONLY on claims the Claim-checker graded STRONG or SUPPORTED (and the Verifier labeled DOCUMENTED or MAINSTREAM INTERPRETATION); a SHAKY claim appears in body sections only, labelled shaky with its claim-check reason; a MISFRAMED claim is never used as evidence and appears only in the \"Claims that failed the claim-check — do not use\" section with the reason it failed. Every claim keeps the verification label Peter gave it; never upgrade a FRINGE CLAIM or NOT VERIFIED item into the narrative."
    : task?.pipeline === "perfectly_paranoid" && worker === "quill"
    ? `SOCIAL COPY OUTPUT — this is an exact text contract, because the office extracts the publishable copy from your output mechanically. Done means all three: (1) a Markdown file saved in this job's folder with a heading exactly named \`## PUBLICATION-READY POST COPY\`; (2) beneath that heading, only the verbatim text Ben should publish — and nothing else; (3) that section ends with a line containing only \`---\`, before any notes. In your set_brief_status result, repeat that same heading and the exact publishable copy before any work summary or file path. Copy that appears in any other shape will not reach Ben as a finished package.\n\nVOICE OVERRIDE FOR THIS PIPELINE ONLY: the general Johnny tone in your worker contract (direct, warm, playful) does NOT apply to this copy. This step uses the locked Perfectly Paranoid voice below instead. This also applies on a copy rework of a Perfectly Paranoid job: rewrite the copy in this voice, using only the verified facts already in the package.\n\n${PERFECTLY_PARANOID_VOICE}\n\n${HASHTAG_RULE_FACEBOOK}\n\nVOICE + HASHTAG CHECK BEFORE FINISHING — all five must be true or the copy is not done: (a) flat factual opening in flat sequence with a dry aside, dry tone throughout; (b) an explicit stakes paragraph beginning with the exact phrase "Why is this a big deal?"; (c) a quiet closing hook (inversion or unanswered question, never a punchline) as the last prose; (d) zero facts, numbers, or quotes beyond Tom's Verified list; (e) HASHTAG BLOCK — the copy ENDS, after that hook, with a hashtag block of 3–5 top topic-specific tags (final line(s), only hashtags, nothing after them, no filler tags). The server checks (e) mechanically and rejects this step as incomplete without it.`
    : task?.standingOrderId === SVEN_VISIONARY_ORDER_ID && worker === "ledger"
      ? `VISIONARY OUTPUT — DEFINITION OF DONE: you researched and produced exactly 2 or 3 distinct, concrete ideas AND saved them with one call to save_visionary_ideas (this brief id, this job id) before finishing. Lane rule: at least one idea is within-scope (an improvement to Ben's existing ventures — Pulse HQ / done-for-you AI offices, Perfectly Paranoid, or the AI Office itself) and at least one is outside-scope (a genuinely new market, product category, content vertical, or monetization angle). ${SVEN_RPG_MAKER_EXCLUSION} The server rejects any saved idea that is RPG Maker-related, so do not waste a run on one. An outside-scope idea counts only if it is realistic for Ben's skills (JavaScript, writing, teaching, design, content creation, and building AI offices and social-media offers) plus the crew's capabilities (web research, content writing, image generation, data organization, and trend analysis). Every saved idea carries: its scope as within or outside, a short plain title a person understands at a glance, one category, a plainSummary of one or two plain sentences (leading with the idea itself and what the reader gets from it, stated as the idea — never as a description of a document or the work behind it — this leads the card, before any reasoning), a specific rationale naming why it is worth doing in plain words, the smallest practical next step, and exact inspected HTTPS source URLs whenever external facts or trends informed it. ${SVEN_PLAIN_LANGUAGE_RULE} The server rejects any title or plain summary that uses crew jargon, so write them in everyday words the first time. A prose-only list in your result does NOT satisfy this contract — if save_visionary_ideas was not called, the run is not done.\n\n${SVEN_STORY_DUTY}\n\nFile the stories you genuinely found with one call to save_sven_stories in this same run, alongside the ideas — if a shelf honestly turns up nothing worth filing, say so in your result in plain words instead of padding it. Your result closes with the counts in plain words: how many ideas, how many stories on each shelf, and how many of the Perfectly Paranoid stories came from declassified files.`
      : "";
  // Sven-launched jobs carry the plain-language package contract for EVERY
  // crew step, whatever the worker's role: the finished package is read by
  // a person, so its documents need human titles and plain summaries even
  // though Sven himself only supplied the idea.
  const svenLaunchedRows = task ? await db.select({ id: schema.visionaryIdeas.id }).from(schema.visionaryIdeas).where(eq(schema.visionaryIdeas.launchedTaskId, task.id)).limit(1) : [];
  const packageContract = svenLaunchedRows.length > 0 ? SVEN_PACKAGE_CONTRACT : "";
  // Front Office output contracts: Maria's steps produce exact, checkable
  // artifacts — the shaped brief, the package cover note, the activity
