  // note Ben reads on the package IS Maria's result text).
  const frontOfficeContract = worker === "maria" && brief.pipelineStage === "intake"
    ? "FRONT OFFICE OUTPUT — INTAKE. Done means both of these exist and are identical: (1) your result is the complete shaped brief — the full original request with every applicable registry constraint applied and named; (2) the same shaped brief saved as client-brief.md in this job's folder. The crew steps after you work from your brief, so anything you leave out here is work they will never see."
    : worker === "maria" && task?.pipeline === "client_delivery"
      ? "FRONT OFFICE OUTPUT — DELIVERY PACKAGE. Done means: (1) your result is the package cover note itself, word for word, in plain client language — the office stores it on the package exactly as you return it; (2) delivery-package.md exists in this job's folder with the cover note and the exact names of the finished files the package contains, read from the source job's folder yourself. A cover note describing work you did not find in that folder is not done. (3) If Ben's feedback changed a finished piece itself — the words of a post, say — the complete revised piece is saved in THIS job's folder under the original file name (for a post: the full revised copy under its `## PUBLICATION-READY POST COPY` heading, ending with its hashtag block, then the `---` line). The office carries that saved revision into the package Ben reads when you finish; a cover note that merely says the change was made, without the revised piece saved here, leaves the package showing the old version."
      : worker === "maria" && task?.pipeline === "client_report"
        ? "FRONT OFFICE OUTPUT — ACTIVITY RECORD. Done means both of these exist and are identical: (1) your result is the assembled activity record; (2) the same record saved as client-activity-record.md in this job's folder. The record contains only the office facts supplied in your brief — no added job, count, date, or outcome, ever."
        : task?.pipeline === "client_report" && worker === "quill"
          ? "FRONT OFFICE OUTPUT — CLIENT SUMMARY. Done means both of these exist and are identical: (1) your result is the finished client summary; (2) the same summary saved as client-report.md in this job's folder. Every fact in it traces to Maria's activity record in the completed work above — nothing added, nothing rounded up."
          : "";
  // Escalation contract: every main-floor Tom research/verification step
  // carries the rule at run time, whatever plan produced the brief — social
  // posts, planner-written standard jobs, and reworks alike. Research cases
  // (already in the lab), X posts, and Front Office jobs never carry it.
  // Downstream steps on an escalated job also carry the do-not-publish
  // footing for lab-failed claims, so Johnny's copy consumes the lab list.
  const escalationContract = worker === "scout" && isEscalationEligibleTask(task)
    ? ESCALATION_RULE
    : task?.escalationStatus === "returned"
      ? `LAB VERIFICATION — this job was escalated to the Research Department and the lab has returned its check. Tom's step output above includes a LAB VERIFICATION section (also saved as lab-verification.md in this job's folder) with Peter's labels for the escalated claims. Treat that lab-verified list as binding: any escalated claim the lab labeled NOT VERIFIED, FRINGE CLAIM, or that failed checking is on the do-not-publish footing for this job — do not use it, quote it, or build on it. Claims the lab labeled DOCUMENTED or MAINSTREAM INTERPRETATION may be used with their labels' care.`
      : "";
  // Product pipeline output contracts (market briefing, creative package):
  // each step produces one exact, checkable artifact, and the final step's
  // artifact IS the product Ben approves — the briefing document, or the
  // concept + visual set together.
  const productContract = task?.pipeline === "market_briefing" && worker === "ledger"
    ? "MARKET BRIEFING OUTPUT — SCOUTING. Done means both of these exist and are identical: (1) your result is the full gathering — opportunities and market observations for the named business/market, kept in separate lists, each with what supports it and its exact source URL where it has one, plus a third list of anything not checked; (2) the same gathering saved as market-observations.md in this job's folder. Plain human terms throughout — no crew jargon in anything a person will read."
    : task?.pipeline === "market_briefing" && worker === "scout"
      ? "MARKET BRIEFING OUTPUT — THE BRIEFING. Done means both of these exist and are identical: (1) your result is the complete finished Market briefing in the four-part shape in your instructions (opening summary, what we found, structured recommendations, what to watch), opening with a plain human title heading and a `## In plain words` section whose first sentence states the headline finding — verdict first, never a description of the briefing itself; (2) the same briefing saved as market-briefing.md in this job's folder. Every fact traces to Sven's gathering in the completed work above — nothing added, nothing upgraded from his not-checked list."
      : task?.pipeline === "creative_package" && worker === "quill"
        ? "CREATIVE PACKAGE OUTPUT — CONCEPT AND COPY. Done means both of these exist and are identical: (1) your result is the complete campaign concept document — concept, finished copy, visual direction, and the brand-asset list with any missing asset marked exactly as a PLACEHOLDER to be supplied by the client; (2) the same document saved as campaign-concept.md in this job's folder. Never present an invented logo or brand asset as the client's real one."
        : task?.pipeline === "creative_package" && worker === "forge"
          ? "CREATIVE PACKAGE OUTPUT — VISUAL SET. Done means: every visual the concept calls for exists in this job's folder, you inspected each one, and your result names each visual's exact file path in plain words. These are designed visuals — the source-first real-photograph rule and its provenance record do not apply here. No invented client logo or brand asset anywhere: a missing asset stays a clearly marked placeholder box, labelled exactly as the concept specifies."
          : "";
  // Outcome contract override — appended LAST in the run wrapper, so for a
  // contract-bound job the contract has the final word over any general
  // worker-contract wording it conflicts with (Johnny's standing hashtag
  // rule for social posts, the office-wide image habits, a borrowed
  // template voice). Unbound jobs (created before contracts, standing
  // orders) carry no override and run exactly as they always have.
  const boundTaskContract = contractForTask(task);
  const contractOverride = boundTaskContract
    ? [
      `OUTCOME CONTRACT OVERRIDE — this job is bound to the ${boundTaskContract.label} outcome contract; the full contract text is in your brief. It OVERRIDES any conflicting wording in your general worker contract for this job, and the finished deliverable is checked against it before it can surface${boundTaskContract.strict ? " (client deliverable — strictest enforcement: a violation blocks it entirely)" : ""}:`,
      boundTaskContract.hashtagRule === "forbidden" ? "- NO hashtag finisher and no hashtag block anywhere in your output for this job — even if your general contract describes a hashtag rule for social posts, it does not apply here, because this deliverable is not a post." : boundTaskContract.hashtagRule === "required" ? "- The hashtag block IS required on this job's finished post, exactly as the contract in your brief states." : boundTaskContract.hashtagRule === "forbidden_except_posts" ? (boundTaskContract.postsRequested ? "- HASHTAG CARVE-OUT: this standard job's brief asks for finished social posts, so each post MUST end with its strongest topic hashtags (top topic-specific tags, no filler, nothing after the block) — Johnny's standing post hashtag rule DOES apply to the posts in this job. Documents, letters, and reports in this job get NO hashtag finisher." : "- HASHTAG CARVE-OUT: NO hashtag finisher in this job — its deliverable is a document, letter, or report shape, and the no-hashtag rule applies to those. (Finished social posts would carry hashtags, but this brief does not ask for posts.)") : "- Hashtags appear only inside copy items that are themselves social posts — never as a pack-level finisher block.",
      boundTaskContract.ppVoiceAllowed ? "" : "- The Perfectly Paranoid voice and template do NOT apply to this job — never use them, whatever the subject.",
      boundTaskContract.imageRule === "none" || (boundTaskContract.imageRule === "brief" && !boundTaskContract.imageAllowed) ? "- No image step runs on this job and no image is attached to the deliverable." : "",
      `- Deliverable shape: ${boundTaskContract.deliverableShape}`,
    ].filter(Boolean).join("\n")
    : "";
  const fullOutputContract = [outputContract, packageContract, frontOfficeContract, productContract, escalationContract, contractOverride].filter(Boolean).join("\n\n");
  const spawned = await ctx.agent.spawnTask(
    `${workerInstructions[worker]}

You are the visible worker executing ONE step of a job in AI Office. You start this run with no memory of earlier jobs: everything you need is in this message, and when earlier steps of this job are done, their results are included in the instructions below.

Brief id: ${brief.id}
Job id: ${brief.taskId}
Step: ${brief.title}
Instructions:
${brief.notes}

${mediaPolicy}${fullOutputContract ? `\n\n${fullOutputContract}` : ""}

${VERDICT_FIRST_RULE}

${PIECE_PLAIN_SUMMARY_RULE}

${skillPool}

HOW EVERY RUN WORKS:
- Progress: immediately call report_progress with this brief id, member id ${worker}, and one concrete line naming what you are starting. Before and after every meaningful tool call, call report_progress with a short operational line prefixed "Tool ·" (for example "Tool · Searching the web for primary sources" or "Tool · Inspecting the image"). Also report at every meaningful milestone, and at least every three minutes during a long operation. One line each, operational only — never reveal private chain-of-thought or hidden reasoning.
- Work: use your tools to do the work and to verify it — open the source, run the build, inspect the image. Do not roleplay, and never claim a check you did not actually perform.
- Files: put every final file for this job under ~/workspace/ai-office/jobs/${brief.taskId}/ (create the folder if needed), give files descriptive names, keep research notes, copy documents, and images together in that one folder, and name every final file path in your result. Do not scatter deliverables elsewhere in the workspace.
- Blocked: only a real missing decision or a real access problem counts as a blocker — inconvenience and uncertainty you can resolve with your tools do not. Call report_blocker with this brief id, job id, member id, one precise question, blockerKind, a gateKey, and, for browser_action blockers only, verificationInstructions. blockerKind is "decision" when Ben's words resolve it, and "browser_action" when Ben must click, sign in, approve consent, or clear an access wall in a browser. gateKey is a stable key built from the service and the underlying cause (for example redbubble-cloudflare-human-check); repeated failures at the same gate reuse the same gateKey, never a reworded one. verificationInstructions describes a lightweight check that confirms only whether the gate cleared — it must not redo the blocked work. After calling report_blocker, stop.
- Finishing: on success, call set_brief_status with status done and a result whose FIRST sentence states the outcome — the finding, verdict, recommendation, or finished result (verdict first, per the rule above: never a description of the document, the work, or what was produced) — and that names every final file path. The server then starts the next planned crew step automatically, or puts the final result in front of Ben — you never hand off manually. On failure, call set_brief_status with status failed and the honest error: what failed, and at what step.
- Never: call set_task_status, create another task, spawn another worker, or invent an approval checkpoint. Ben reviews once, at the end.`,
  );

  if (!spawned.ok) return { ok: false };
  const now = new Date();
  await db.update(schema.briefs).set({ runTaskId: spawned.taskId, progressText: `${memberNames[worker]} started ${brief.title}.`, lastHeartbeatAt: now, updatedAt: now }).where(eq(schema.briefs.id, brief.id));
  ctx.invalidateQueries();
  return { ok: true, taskId: spawned.taskId };
}

const STALLED_BRIEF_THRESHOLD_MS = 15 * 60 * 1000;
// Phase 5: the watchdog's recovery is BOUNDED. A brief gets at most
// STALL_MAX_ATTEMPTS working attempts; when a brief stalls after its last
// allowed attempt, the watchdog stops re-queueing it and surfaces it to
// Ben as a blocker instead of looping silently forever.
const STALL_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3;
const STALL_BLOCKER_GATE_KEY = "stall-watchdog-exhausted";
export const STALL_STUCK_REASON = "This job stalled 3 times — it kept stopping with no progress. Answer here to queue it again, send the job back for rework, or delete it.";

// READY FOR YOU MEMBERSHIP RULE (Ben, 2026-10-18): Ready for You means
// exactly one thing — "this needs Ben's decision." A job may sit in the
// approval state ONLY if it is a finished manual-job result awaiting his
// approval or a job with a genuine blocker addressed to him. A
// standing-order run is NEVER a decision: creating the order was the
// approval, and every run finishes straight to Done (the approver
// doctrine). Every finish path already routes standing-order runs to
// Done, but three finished daily-news runs were found sitting in
// approval anyway — flipped there before the doctrine was enforced on
// every path — where the client's standing-order filter hid them from
// the queue without ever re-homing them: not decisions, not Done, just
// limbo. This sweep is the structural backstop: any standing-order run
// found in approval is moved to Done and the move is written to the
// office log, so the run stays findable in Done history and activity.
// It runs inside poll_dispatch, so the queue heals itself on the
// dispatcher's regular cycle no matter which path let a run through.
async function rehomeStandingOrderApprovals(ctx: Ctx): Promise<number> {
  const db = ctx.db<typeof schema>();
  const stranded = await db.select().from(schema.tasks).where(and(isNotNull(schema.tasks.standingOrderId), eq(schema.tasks.status, "approval")));
  if (stranded.length === 0) return 0;
  const now = new Date();
  await db.batch([
    db.update(schema.tasks).set({ status: "done" }).where(and(isNotNull(schema.tasks.standingOrderId), eq(schema.tasks.status, "approval"))),
    db.insert(schema.activityLog).values({ t: now, text: `${stranded.length} standing-order ${stranded.length === 1 ? "run was" : "runs were"} sitting in Ready for You, where ${stranded.length === 1 ? "it does" : "they do"} not belong — standing-order runs are never decisions. ${stranded.length === 1 ? "It was" : "They were"} moved to Done; the results stay in History and this log.` }),
  ]);
  ctx.invalidateQueries();
  return stranded.length;
}

// COMPANION SWEEP — client jobs stranded in Ready for You. Before the
// pipeline routes were enforced at the finish gate, a finished job for
// an external client surfaced loose in Ready for You and waited for a
// job-level approval before its delivery package was even created.
// Under the routes, that job's decision item is its package: this
// sweep finds external-client jobs still sitting in approval (no open
// blocker — a blocked job is genuinely waiting on Ben's answer; not
// contract-stuck — a stuck job surfaces on purpose for rework/delete)
// and routes each one through the same gate the lifecycle now uses:
// close to Done, Maria assembles the package, Ben decides once, on
// the package in Deliverables.
async function routeStrandedClientJobs(ctx: Ctx): Promise<number> {
  const db = ctx.db<typeof schema>();
  const [candidates, openBlockers] = await Promise.all([
    db.select().from(schema.tasks).where(eq(schema.tasks.status, "approval")),
    db.select({ taskId: schema.blockers.taskId }).from(schema.blockers).where(eq(schema.blockers.status, "open")),
  ]);
  const blockedIds = new Set(openBlockers.map((blocker) => blocker.taskId));
  const stranded = candidates.filter((task) => isExternalClientJob(task) && !isStuckOnContract(task) && !blockedIds.has(task.id) && !isApprovedPostPackage(task));
  for (const task of stranded) {
    await routeFinishedClientJob(ctx, task, task.assignee);
  }
  return stranded.length;
}

async function requeueStalledBriefs(ctx: Ctx): Promise<number> {
  const db = ctx.db<typeof schema>();
  const [activeBriefs, openBlockers] = await Promise.all([
    db.select().from(schema.briefs).where(eq(schema.briefs.status, "in_progress")),
    db.select({ briefId: schema.blockers.briefId }).from(schema.blockers).where(eq(schema.blockers.status, "open")),
  ]);
  const blockedBriefIds = new Set(openBlockers.map((blocker) => blocker.briefId));
  const now = new Date();
  const cutoff = now.getTime() - STALLED_BRIEF_THRESHOLD_MS;
  let restarted = 0;
  for (const brief of activeBriefs) {
    if (blockedBriefIds.has(brief.id)) continue;
    const lastProgressAt = brief.lastHeartbeatAt ?? brief.updatedAt;
    if (lastProgressAt.getTime() > cutoff) continue;
    if (Math.max(1, brief.attempt) >= STALL_MAX_ATTEMPTS) {
      // Cap hit: fail the step loudly and surface it. Standing-order runs
      // keep their doctrine (never Ben's queue): they end as Done with
      // the stall recorded, exactly like standing-order blockers.
      const failedRows = await db.update(schema.briefs).set({
        status: "failed",
        runTaskId: null,
        result: `Needs you: ${STALL_STUCK_REASON}`,
        progressText: "Stalled 3 times — needs you",
        lastHeartbeatAt: now,
        updatedAt: now,
      }).where(and(eq(schema.briefs.id, brief.id), eq(schema.briefs.status, "in_progress"))).returning({ id: schema.briefs.id });
      if (!failedRows[0]) continue;
      const taskRows = await db.select().from(schema.tasks).where(eq(schema.tasks.id, brief.taskId)).limit(1);
      const stuckTask = taskRows[0];
      const standingOrderRun = Boolean(stuckTask?.standingOrderId);
      if (stuckTask && standingOrderRun) {
        await db.batch([
          db.update(schema.tasks).set({ status: "done" }).where(eq(schema.tasks.id, stuckTask.id)),
          db.insert(schema.activityLog).values({ t: now, text: `${memberByAssignee(brief.assignee)}'s “${brief.title}” stalled 3 times on a standing-order run. It was stopped and recorded here instead of restarting again.` }),
        ]);
      } else if (stuckTask) {
        await db.batch([
          db.update(schema.tasks).set({ status: "approval", assignee: brief.assignee }).where(eq(schema.tasks.id, stuckTask.id)),
          db.insert(schema.blockers).values({
            id: `blocker-${crypto.randomUUID()}`, briefId: brief.id, taskId: brief.taskId, memberId: brief.assignee,
            question: STALL_STUCK_REASON, kind: "decision", gateKey: STALL_BLOCKER_GATE_KEY, retryCount: STALL_MAX_ATTEMPTS,
            status: "open", answer: null, notifiedAt: null, createdAt: now, updatedAt: now, resolvedAt: null,
            verificationInstructions: null, verificationStatus: null, lastVerificationAt: null,
          }),
          db.insert(schema.activityLog).values({ t: now, text: `${memberByAssignee(brief.assignee)}'s “${brief.title}” stalled 3 times. It will not restart on its own — it is waiting on you in Ready for You.` }),
        ]);
      }
      restarted += 1;
      continue;
    }
    const nextAttempt = Math.max(1, brief.attempt + 1);
    const rows = await db.update(schema.briefs).set({
      status: "new",
      runTaskId: null,
      progressText: `Attempt ${Math.max(1, brief.attempt)} stalled — queued to restart`,
      lastHeartbeatAt: null,
      updatedAt: now,
    }).where(and(eq(schema.briefs.id, brief.id), eq(schema.briefs.status, "in_progress"))).returning({ id: schema.briefs.id });
    if (!rows[0]) continue;
    await db.insert(schema.activityLog).values({
      t: now,
      text: `${memberByAssignee(brief.assignee)}'s “${brief.title}” stalled with no progress for 15 minutes. Attempt ${Math.max(1, brief.attempt)} was marked failed; restarting as attempt ${nextAttempt}.`,
    });
    restarted += 1;
  }
  if (restarted > 0) ctx.invalidateQueries();
  return restarted;
}

async function eligibleBriefs(ctx: Ctx): Promise<Array<typeof schema.briefs.$inferSelect>> {
  const db = ctx.db<typeof schema>();
  const [tasks, briefs] = await Promise.all([db.select().from(schema.tasks), db.select().from(schema.briefs).orderBy(schema.briefs.stepIndex, schema.briefs.createdAt)]);
  const escalationWaiting = new Set(tasks.filter((task) => task.escalationStatus === "pending").map((task) => task.id));
  const activeTaskRevisions = new Map(tasks.filter((task) => task.status === "working" && !escalationWaiting.has(task.id)).map((task) => [task.id, task.revision]));
  const grouped = new Map<string, Array<typeof schema.briefs.$inferSelect>>();
  for (const brief of briefs) {
    if (activeTaskRevisions.get(brief.taskId) !== brief.revision) continue;
    const list = grouped.get(brief.taskId) ?? []; list.push(brief); grouped.set(brief.taskId, list);
  }
  const eligible: Array<typeof schema.briefs.$inferSelect> = [];
  for (const list of grouped.values()) {
    if (list.some((brief) => brief.status === "in_progress")) continue;
    const firstOpen = list.find((brief) => brief.status === "new" || brief.status === "failed");
    if (firstOpen?.status === "new") eligible.push(firstOpen);
  }
  return eligible;
}

async function claimBrief(ctx: Ctx, id: string): Promise<typeof schema.briefs.$inferSelect | null> {
  const db = ctx.db<typeof schema>(); const allowed = await eligibleBriefs(ctx);
  const selected = allowed.find((brief) => brief.id === id);
  if (!selected) return null;
  const now = new Date();
  const rows = await db.update(schema.briefs).set({ status: "in_progress", updatedAt: now, attempt: selected.attempt + 1 }).where(and(eq(schema.briefs.id, id), eq(schema.briefs.status, "new"))).returning();
  const brief = rows[0]; if (!brief) return null;
  await db.batch([
    db.update(schema.tasks).set({ status: "working", assignee: brief.assignee }).where(eq(schema.tasks.id, brief.taskId)),
    db.insert(schema.activityLog).values({ t: now, text: `${memberByAssignee(brief.assignee)} started “${brief.title}”.` }),
  ]);
  ctx.invalidateQueries(); return brief;
}

async function startNextForTask(ctx: Ctx, taskId: string): Promise<typeof schema.briefs.$inferSelect | null> {
  const eligible = await eligibleBriefs(ctx); const next = eligible.find((brief) => brief.taskId === taskId); if (!next) return null;
  const claimed = await claimBrief(ctx, next.id); if (!claimed) return null;
  const started = await spawnWorker(ctx, claimed);
  if (!started.ok) {
    const db = ctx.db<typeof schema>(); const now = new Date();
    await db.batch([
      db.update(schema.briefs).set({ status: "new", runTaskId: null, progressText: "Waiting for a worker to start", lastHeartbeatAt: null, updatedAt: now }).where(eq(schema.briefs.id, claimed.id)),
      db.insert(schema.activityLog).values({ t: now, text: `${memberByAssignee(claimed.assignee)} could not start “${claimed.title}”. It remains queued.` }),
    ]);
    ctx.invalidateQueries(); return null;
  }
  return claimed;
}

// Spawn the ONE lab sub-case for a parent job's escalated claims. The
// sub-case runs the existing Research Department pipeline (Walter → Peter
// → Tom synthesis, Tom commuting as usual) on exactly the escalated claims.
// It is internal: pipeline research_case, parentTaskId set, and its finish
// is intercepted in set_brief_status so it closes to Done and resumes the
// parent instead of ever surfacing in Ready for You.
async function spawnLabSubcase(ctx: Ctx, parent: typeof schema.tasks.$inferSelect, claims: string[], tomResult: string): Promise<{ task: typeof schema.tasks.$inferSelect; briefs: Array<typeof schema.briefs.$inferSelect> } | null> {
  const claimList = claims.map((claim) => `- ${claim}`).join("\n");
  const notes = `Internal lab sub-case — escalated claims only. This is NOT a new job from Ben and needs no approval of its own; it exists because Tom, working the main-floor job “${parent.title}” (job id ${parent.id}), sent specific claims to the Research Department for a full lab check under the escalation rule.\n\nCheck ONLY these claims — no others:\n${claimList}\n\nTom's downstairs result on the parent job, for context (the claims above are the ones to check; the rest of his result is background only):\n${tomResult.slice(0, 6000)}`;
  const title = `Lab check — ${parent.title}`.slice(0, 120);
  const parentMode = parent.gatheringMode === "tiered" ? "tiered" : "standard";
  return createPlannedWork(ctx, { title, notes, steps: researchPlan(title, notes, parentMode), pipeline: "research_case", parentTaskId: parent.id, gatheringMode: parentMode });
}

// The lab has returned (or a lab step failed): save the lab's synthesis
// into the parent job's folder as lab-verification.md, attach it to Tom's
// step output on the parent so downstream steps consume the lab-verified
// list, mark the parent's escalation returned with Peter's label counts,
// and resume the parent exactly where it waited — next crew step if one
// remains, otherwise its one trip to Ready for You.
async function resumeParentAfterLab(ctx: Ctx, parent: typeof schema.tasks.$inferSelect, labText: string, counts: { documented: number; notVerified: number }): Promise<void> {
  const db = ctx.db<typeof schema>();
  const now = new Date();
  try {
    await ctx.executePrivileged(privileged.writeLabVerification, { taskId: parent.id, text: labText });
  } catch {
    // The verification record also lives in Tom's step output below, so
    // the parent can still resume honestly if the file write fails.
  }
  const parentBriefs = await db.select().from(schema.briefs).where(and(eq(schema.briefs.taskId, parent.id), eq(schema.briefs.revision, parent.revision))).orderBy(schema.briefs.stepIndex, schema.briefs.createdAt);
  const tomBrief = [...parentBriefs].reverse().find((item) => item.assignee === "scout" && item.status === "done" && item.result && /ESCALATED TO RESEARCH DEPT/i.test(item.result))
    ?? [...parentBriefs].reverse().find((item) => item.assignee === "scout" && item.status === "done");
  const labSection = `\n\n---\nLAB VERIFICATION (Research Department) — the lab checked the escalated claims and returned: ${counts.documented} documented, ${counts.notVerified} not verified. The full lab record is saved as lab-verification.md in this job's folder. Claims the lab labeled NOT VERIFIED (and any that failed checking) are on the do-not-publish footing for this job — downstream steps must not use them.\n\n${labText}`;
  let tomResultWithLab = tomBrief?.result ?? "";
  if (tomBrief) {
    tomResultWithLab = `${tomBrief.result ?? ""}${labSection}`.slice(0, 100000);
    await db.update(schema.briefs).set({ result: tomResultWithLab, updatedAt: now }).where(eq(schema.briefs.id, tomBrief.id));
  }
  await db.update(schema.tasks).set({ escalationStatus: "returned", escalationDocumented: counts.documented, escalationNotVerified: counts.notVerified }).where(eq(schema.tasks.id, parent.id));
  await db.insert(schema.activityLog).values({ t: now, text: `Research Department returned: ${counts.documented} documented, ${counts.notVerified} not verified — “${parent.title}” resumed with the lab's labels attached to Tom's work.` });
  const refreshedBriefs = await db.select().from(schema.briefs).where(and(eq(schema.briefs.taskId, parent.id), eq(schema.briefs.revision, parent.revision))).orderBy(schema.briefs.stepIndex, schema.briefs.createdAt);
  const next = refreshedBriefs.find((item) => item.status === "new");
  if (!next) {
    // Ready for You membership rule: a standing-order run never enters
    // the decision queue, even by this lab-return path — it finishes
    // straight to Done like every other standing-order run.
    if (parent.standingOrderId) {
      await db.batch([
        db.update(schema.tasks).set({ status: "done" }).where(eq(schema.tasks.id, parent.id)),
        db.insert(schema.activityLog).values({ t: now, text: `Tom finished the final crew step of the standing-order run “${parent.title}” with the lab's check attached. It moved directly to Done.` }),
      ]);
      ctx.invalidateQueries();
      return;
    }
    // Client route, same as the final gate in set_brief_status: a
    // finished job for an external client goes to its delivery
    // package, never loose into Ready for You (a contract-stuck job
    // is the exception — it surfaces as a stuck item below).
    if (isExternalClientJob(parent) && !isStuckOnContract(parent)) {
      await routeFinishedClientJob(ctx, parent, parent.assignee);
      ctx.invalidateQueries();
      return;
    }
    await db.batch([
      db.update(schema.tasks).set(parent.pipeline === "perfectly_paranoid"
        ? { status: "approval", publicationStatus: "awaiting_approval" }
        : { status: "approval" }).where(eq(schema.tasks.id, parent.id)),
      db.insert(schema.activityLog).values({ t: now, text: `Tom finished the final crew step of “${parent.title}” with the lab's check attached. The job is waiting for your one decision.` }),
    ]);
    ctx.invalidateQueries();
    return;
  }
  const completedContext = refreshedBriefs
    .filter((item) => item.status === "done" && item.result?.trim())
    .map((item) => `${memberByAssignee(item.assignee)} — ${item.title}:\n${item.id === tomBrief?.id ? tomResultWithLab : item.result}`)
    .join("\n\n");
  const priorContext = completedContext ? `\n\nCompleted work so far:\n${completedContext}` : "";
  await db.update(schema.briefs).set({ notes: ensureContractBlock(parent, `${next.notes}${priorContext}`).slice(-20000), updatedAt: now }).where(eq(schema.briefs.id, next.id));
  const fromParsed = memberId.safeParse(tomBrief?.assignee ?? "scout");
  const toParsed = memberId.safeParse(next.assignee);
  if (fromParsed.success && toParsed.success) {
    await db.insert(schema.handoffEvents).values({ id: `handoff-${crypto.randomUUID()}`, fromMemberId: fromParsed.data, toMemberId: toParsed.data, sourceTaskId: parent.id, targetBriefId: next.id, title: next.title, createdAt: now });
  }
  await db.insert(schema.activityLog).values({ t: now, text: `Tom handed “${parent.title}” to ${memberByAssignee(next.assignee)} with the Research Department's labels attached. No approval was requested.` });
  await startNextForTask(ctx, parent.id);
  ctx.invalidateQueries();
}

async function isEscalationSubcase(ctx: Ctx, task: typeof schema.tasks.$inferSelect | undefined): Promise<typeof schema.tasks.$inferSelect | null> {
  if (!task?.parentTaskId) return null;
  const db = ctx.db<typeof schema>();
  const rows = await db.select().from(schema.tasks).where(eq(schema.tasks.id, task.parentTaskId)).limit(1);
  const parent = rows[0];
  return parent && parent.escalationSubtaskId === task.id ? parent : null;
}

// Olivia's scheduled Monday batch: ONE creation path, used by the
// scheduled evaluation below and by the on-demand run_olivia_batch_now
// action. Her brief is grounded in REAL recent office activity only — the
// actual log, finished jobs, and closed research cases — so the truth
// rules in her standing order have something true to use, and her
// drafting rules are composed from that same standing-order text
// (oliviaRulesFromOrderText at the scheduled batch count of 3), exactly
// as manual X Posts jobs compose theirs. The order's stored instruction
// also remains the job's notes (its description in the Work panel).
async function createOliviaMondayBatch(ctx: Ctx, order: typeof schema.standingOrders.$inferSelect): Promise<{ task: typeof schema.tasks.$inferSelect; briefs: Array<typeof schema.briefs.$inferSelect> } | null> {
  const db = ctx.db<typeof schema>();
  const instruction = expandStandingOrderInstruction(order.instruction);
  const [recentLog, allTasks] = await Promise.all([
    db.select().from(schema.activityLog).orderBy(desc(schema.activityLog.t), desc(schema.activityLog.id)).limit(18),
    db.select().from(schema.tasks).orderBy(desc(schema.tasks.created)).limit(30),
  ]);
  const completed = allTasks.filter((task) => task.status === "done").slice(0, 8);
  const closedCases = allTasks.filter((task) => task.pipeline === "research_case" && task.status !== "working").slice(0, 5);
  const grounding = [
    "Recent office activity (newest first):",
    ...recentLog.map((entry) => `- ${entry.text}`),
    completed.length ? `\nRecently completed jobs:\n${completed.map((task) => `- ${task.title}`).join("\n")}` : "",
    closedCases.length ? `\nResearch cases on file:\n${closedCases.map((task) => `- ${task.title}`).join("\n")}` : "",
  ].filter(Boolean).join("\n");
  const title = "Olivia: Monday X post batch";
  const instructions = `You are Olivia, the X Drafter in Pulse HQ's Research Department. This is your standing Monday batch. It follows the same drafting contract as a manual X Posts job, with one difference: your source material is the real office activity listed at the end of this brief, and it is the ONLY source you may use — every event and number in your posts must come from it.\n\n${oliviaRulesFromOrderText(order.instruction, 3)}\n\nDraft from this real office activity — these are the only events and numbers you may use:\n${grounding}`;
  return createPlannedWork(ctx, { title, notes: instruction, standingOrderId: order.id, pipeline: "x_posts", steps: [{ assignee: "olivia", title, instructions }] });
}


async function evaluateStandingOrdersNow(ctx: Ctx): Promise<{ created: number; evaluated: number }> {
  const db = ctx.db<typeof schema>(); const now = new Date(); const orders = await db.select().from(schema.standingOrders).where(eq(schema.standingOrders.enabled, true)); const tasks = await db.select().from(schema.tasks); let created = 0;
  for (const order of orders) {
    const instruction = expandStandingOrderInstruction(order.instruction);
    let scheduledDue = false;
    let recomputedNextRunAt = order.nextRunAt;
    if (order.mode === "scheduled" && order.cadence) {
      const latest = latestScheduledRun(now, order.cadence, order.weekday, order.scheduleHour, order.scheduleMinute, order.timezone);
      recomputedNextRunAt = nextScheduledRun(now, order.cadence, order.weekday, order.scheduleHour, order.scheduleMinute, order.timezone);
      scheduledDue = order.createdAt.getTime() <= latest.getTime() && (!order.lastRunAt || order.lastRunAt.getTime() < latest.getTime());
    }
    const quantity = order.mode === "scheduled"
      ? (scheduledDue ? 1 : 0)
      : Math.max(0, Math.min(10, (order.targetCount ?? 1) - tasks.filter((task) => task.standingOrderId === order.id && task.status !== "done").length));
    for (let index = 0; index < quantity; index += 1) {
      const parsedAssignee = crewMemberId.safeParse(order.assignee);
      if (order.id === OLIVIA_X_ORDER_ID) {
        const createdWork = await createOliviaMondayBatch(ctx, order);
        if (createdWork) created += 1;
        continue;
      }
      const title = `${instruction}${quantity > 1 ? ` #${index + 1}` : ""}`.slice(0, 120);
      const createdWork = await createPlannedWork(ctx, { title, notes: instruction, standingOrderId: order.id, steps: [{ assignee: parsedAssignee.success ? parsedAssignee.data : "ledger", title, instructions: instruction }] });
      if (createdWork) created += 1;
    }
    await db.update(schema.standingOrders).set({ lastRunAt: quantity ? now : order.lastRunAt, nextRunAt: recomputedNextRunAt }).where(eq(schema.standingOrders.id, order.id));
  }
  // Front Office reporting orders live on the client record, not in the
  // standing-orders table: a client whose report is due (cadence on, due
  // time reached) gets a reporting job — Maria assembles the activity
  // record from office data only, Johnny drafts the summary. The next due
  // time advances whether or not a report was created (one already open),
  // so a busy month never stacks duplicate reports.
  const reportClients = await db.select().from(schema.clients).where(or(eq(schema.clients.reportCadence, "weekly"), eq(schema.clients.reportCadence, "monthly")));
  for (const client of reportClients) {
    const cadence = client.reportCadence === "monthly" ? "monthly" as const : "weekly" as const;
    if (!client.nextReportAt) {
      await db.update(schema.clients).set({ nextReportAt: nextClientReportAt(cadence, now) }).where(eq(schema.clients.id, client.id));
      continue;
    }
    if (client.nextReportAt.getTime() > now.getTime()) continue;
    const fired = await createClientReportJob(ctx, client, "schedule");
    if (fired) created += 1;
    await db.update(schema.clients).set({ nextReportAt: nextClientReportAt(cadence, client.nextReportAt) }).where(eq(schema.clients.id, client.id));
  }
  ctx.invalidateQueries(); return { created, evaluated: orders.length };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// PRE-SURFACE FINISHER CHECK (outcome contracts).
//
// When the final step of a contract-bound job finishes, the deliverable is
// validated against the job's contract BEFORE the task may move to Ready
// for You: forbidden elements for the type (a hashtag block or an attached
// image on a document-type deliverable, Perfectly Paranoid template markers
// in a non-PP deliverable, a pack-level finisher on a creative package) and
// required elements per type (the PP stakes beat + hashtag block + image,
// the research brief's claim labels, the briefing's recommendations, the
// creative package's visuals). A violation bounces the deliverable back as
// a contract-rework step with the reasons recorded on the task and in the
// office log — Ben never sees the violating version. After two bounces the
// job surfaces WITH the violation recorded on it (so a stuck job can never
// loop workers forever), except that a client-tagged job still cannot be
// approved into a delivery package while a violation stands — client
// enforcement is strictest. Unbound jobs (job_type NULL) skip the check
// entirely: they finish under their pre-contract plans.
const CONTRACT_MAX_BOUNCES = 2;

const outcomeContractShape = z.object({
  jobType, label: z.string(), stepsSummary: z.string(), deliverableShape: z.string(), voice: z.string(),
  imageRule: z.enum(["none", "brief", "post", "image_or_link", "designed"]),
  hashtagRule: z.enum(["forbidden", "required", "inside_copy_only", "forbidden_except_posts"]),
  ppVoiceRule: z.enum(["required", "forbidden", "brief"]),
  exitRule: z.string(), requiredElements: z.array(z.string()), forbiddenElements: z.array(z.string()),
  strict: z.boolean(), imageAllowed: z.boolean(), ppVoiceAllowed: z.boolean(), postsRequested: z.boolean(),
});
const contractCheckResponse = z.object({
  taskId: z.string(), contractBound: z.boolean(), jobType: jobType.nullable(), contract: outcomeContractShape.nullable(),
  steps: z.array(z.object({ assignee: z.string(), stage: z.string().nullable(), title: z.string(), isImageStep: z.boolean(), carriesContract: z.boolean() })),
  planViolations: z.array(z.string()), deliverableViolations: z.array(z.string()),
  contractStatus: z.enum(["passed", "bounced"]).nullable(), contractViolation: z.string().nullable(), contractBounces: z.number().int().nonnegative(),
});

function trailingHashtagBlock(text: string): boolean {
  return trailingHashtagLines(text).reduce((total, line) => total + extractHashtags(line).length, 0) >= 2;
}

// A report deliverable is present when a deliverable file is a report
// document (its name says report — client-report.md is the report
// pipeline's own file) or a deliverable text IS a report document (a
// heading that names it a report). A passing mention of the word
// "report" in prose is not a report deliverable.
export function hasClientReportDeliverable(texts: string[], fileNames: string[]): boolean {
  if (fileNames.some((name) => /report/i.test(name))) return true;
  return texts.some((text) => /(^|\n)#{1,6}\s*[^\n]*\breport\b/i.test(text) || /^\s*client report\b/im.test(text));
}

export function contractViolationsFor(contract: OutcomeContract, input: { texts: string[]; finalText: string; postCopy: string | null; imageCount: number; hasImageStep: boolean; fileNames?: string[]; requiresClientReport?: boolean; hasClientReport?: boolean }): string[] {
  const violations: string[] = [];
  const joined = input.texts.join("\n\n");
  // CLIENT REPORT GUARANTEE (Ben, 2026-10-15): a client-tagged job whose
  // brief requires a report — and every client_report job — cannot
  // surface, close, or be packaged without its report document. The
  // caller computes both flags from the task and its deliverable files;
  // the plain-language reason is exactly "client report missing".
  if (input.requiresClientReport) {
    const hasReport = input.hasClientReport ?? hasClientReportDeliverable(input.texts, input.fileNames ?? []);
    if (!hasReport) violations.push("client report missing — this client job's finished work must include its client report document, and none was found in the deliverables");
  }
  if (contract.jobType === "client_report" && !(input.hasClientReport ?? hasClientReportDeliverable(input.texts, input.fileNames ?? []))) {
    if (!violations.some((violation) => violation.startsWith("client report missing"))) {
      violations.push("client report missing — a client report job must deliver its client report document (client-report.md), and none was found in the deliverables");
    }
  }
  // AUTHORED SUMMARY (Ben, 2026-10-19): every job's finishing step authors
  // the job's plain summary in its result — a "## SUMMARY" section whose
  // "Short answer / verdict" paragraph states the result, verdict first —
  // and the office stores that paragraph on the task record for the card.
  // A finish without one is held here, in plain words, instead of
  // surfacing as a clean Decide item the app would have to summarize by
  // scraping the documents.
  if (!extractAuthoredSummary(input.finalText)) {
    violations.push("the finished work carries no summary — the final step must end its result with a section headed “## SUMMARY” whose “Short answer / verdict” paragraph states the result in one or two plain sentences, verdict first");
  }
  if (contract.hashtagRule === "forbidden" && input.texts.some((text) => findHashtagBlock(text))) {
    violations.push("a hashtag block appears in the deliverable — this job type forbids hashtag finishers");
  }
  if (contract.hashtagRule === "forbidden_except_posts") {
    if (contract.postsRequested) {
      // Post side of the carve-out: finished posts MUST end with hashtags.
      const postCopy = input.postCopy ?? extractPublicationReadyPost(input.finalText);
      const candidateTexts = postCopy ? [postCopy] : input.texts;
      const anyHashtagEnding = candidateTexts.some((text) => trailingHashtagBlock(text) || findHashtagBlock(text));
      if (!anyHashtagEnding) {
        violations.push("a finished social post is missing its hashtag block — in a standard job whose brief asks for posts, every post ends with its strongest topic hashtags (documents, letters, and reports are the shapes that get no hashtags)");
      } else if (postCopy) {
        const hashtagError = hashtagBlockError(postCopy, "facebook");
        if (hashtagError) violations.push(`a finished social post's hashtag ending fails the contract — ${hashtagError}`);
      }
    } else if (input.texts.some((text) => findHashtagBlock(text))) {
      violations.push("a hashtag block appears in the deliverable — documents, letters, and reports get no hashtag finisher (the hashtag carve-out covers finished social posts only, and this job's brief does not ask for posts)");
    }
  }
  if (contract.hashtagRule === "inside_copy_only") {
    const packLevel = input.texts.some((text) => hasHashtagHeading(text) || (trailingHashtagBlock(text) && !/PUBLICATION-READY POST COPY|social post copy/i.test(text)));
    if (packLevel) violations.push("a hashtag block appears as a pack-level finisher — in a creative package, hashtags live only inside copy items that are themselves social posts");
  }
  if (!contract.ppVoiceAllowed && input.texts.some((text) => findPpTemplateMarkers(text))) {
    violations.push("Perfectly Paranoid template markers (its stakes-beat structure / post-copy format) appear in a deliverable whose contract forbids the Perfectly Paranoid template and voice");
  }
  const imageForbidden = contract.imageRule === "none" || (contract.imageRule === "brief" && !contract.imageAllowed);
  if (imageForbidden && input.imageCount > 0) {
    violations.push(`an image is attached to the deliverable (${input.imageCount} image file${input.imageCount === 1 ? "" : "s"} in the job folder) — this job type forbids image steps and attached images`);
  }
  if (contract.jobType === "perfectly_paranoid") {
    if (!input.hasImageStep) violations.push("the finished package has no image step — the Perfectly Paranoid pipeline always runs Tom → Johnny → Nik");
    if (input.imageCount === 0) violations.push("no image is attached to the finished post package — the contract requires exactly one image");
    const copy = input.postCopy ?? extractPublicationReadyPost(input.finalText) ?? "";
    if (!copy) {
      violations.push("no publication-ready post copy was found in the finished package");
    } else {
      if (!/why is this a big deal\?/i.test(copy)) violations.push("the copy is missing its stakes beat — the paragraph beginning “Why is this a big deal?”");
      const hashtagError = hashtagBlockError(copy, "facebook");
      if (hashtagError) violations.push(`the copy's hashtag ending fails the contract — ${hashtagError}`);
    }
  }
  if (contract.jobType === "research") {
    const labelSource = /\b(?:DOCUMENTED|MAINSTREAM INTERPRETATION|FRINGE CLAIM|NOT VERIFIED)\b/.test(input.finalText) ? input.finalText : joined;
    if (!/\b(?:DOCUMENTED|MAINSTREAM INTERPRETATION|FRINGE CLAIM|NOT VERIFIED)\b/.test(labelSource)) {
      violations.push("the case brief carries none of the contract's claim labels (documented / mainstream interpretation / fringe claim / not verified)");
    }
  }
  if (contract.jobType === "market_briefing") {
    if (!/recommendation/i.test(input.finalText) && !/recommendation/i.test(joined)) {
      violations.push("the briefing has no recommendations — the contract requires structured recommendations in plain human terms");
    }
  }
  if (contract.jobType === "creative_package" && input.imageCount === 0) {
    violations.push("no designed visual was delivered — a creative package's visuals are its product");
  }
  return violations;
}

// Phase 5 fail-loud rule: a deliverable file that EXISTS (it was found by
// the folder scan) but cannot be read is a contract violation, never a
// silent exclusion — a corrupt deliverable must not pass by absence.
export const UNREADABLE_DELIVERABLE_VIOLATION = "a deliverable file could not be read for checking";

async function collectDeliverableCorpus(ctx: Ctx, task: typeof schema.tasks.$inferSelect, currentResultText: string): Promise<{ texts: string[]; imagePaths: string[]; fileNames: string[]; unreadableFileCount: number }> {
  const texts = [currentResultText];
  if (task.postCopy) texts.push(task.postCopy);
  let imagePaths: string[] = [];
  try { imagePaths = await taskImagePaths(ctx, task); } catch { imagePaths = []; }
  const fileNames: string[] = [];
  let unreadableFileCount = 0;
  try {
    const folder = taskDeliverableFolder(task.id);
    const scanned = await ctx.executePrivileged(privileged.scanDeliverables, { relativeHints: [folder] });
    for (const file of scanned.files) {
      if (file.relativePath.startsWith(`${folder}/`) && !file.relativePath.includes("/.superseded/")) fileNames.push(file.fileName);
    }
    const files = scanned.files
      .filter((file) => file.relativePath.startsWith(`${folder}/`) && !file.relativePath.includes("/.superseded/") && (file.kind === "markdown" || file.kind === "text") && !/^image-provenance\.(?:md|txt)$/i.test(file.fileName) && !/^lab-verification\.(?:md|txt)$/i.test(file.fileName))
      .slice(0, 12);
    for (const file of files) {
      try {
        const content = await ctx.executePrivileged(privileged.readDeliverable, { relativePath: file.relativePath });
        if (content.text) texts.push(content.text);
      } catch { unreadableFileCount += 1; }
    }
  } catch { /* The result text and stored copy still give the check a corpus. */ }
  return { texts, imagePaths, fileNames, unreadableFileCount };
}

async function validateDeliverableAgainstContract(ctx: Ctx, task: typeof schema.tasks.$inferSelect, currentResultText: string, briefs: Array<typeof schema.briefs.$inferSelect>): Promise<string[]> {
  const contract = contractForTask(task);
  if (!contract) return [];
  // Olivia's contract is enforced at the save gate (save_x_posts) — the
  // Post Queue is her surface, and her drafts never pass through here.
  if (contract.jobType === "x_posts") return [];
  const corpus = await collectDeliverableCorpus(ctx, task, currentResultText);
  const hasImageStep = briefs.some((brief) => brief.assignee === "forge" && isImageProductionStep({ assignee: brief.assignee, title: brief.title, instructions: brief.notes }));
  const requiresClientReport = Boolean(task.clientId) && (task.jobType === "client_report" || task.pipeline === "client_report" || briefIncludesReport(task.title, task.notes));
  const hasClientReport = hasClientReportDeliverable(corpus.texts, corpus.fileNames);
  const violations = contractViolationsFor(contract, { texts: corpus.texts, finalText: currentResultText, postCopy: task.postCopy ?? null, imageCount: corpus.imagePaths.length, hasImageStep, fileNames: corpus.fileNames, requiresClientReport, hasClientReport });
  if (corpus.unreadableFileCount > 0) violations.unshift(UNREADABLE_DELIVERABLE_VIOLATION);
  // Claim completeness gate (Change 1): a research case whose grading
  // reconciles incomplete may still surface — synthesis is allowed to
  // draft — but ONLY carrying the grading-incomplete banner, so no
  // surface can represent it as fully checked. A job with no manifest and
  // no persisted gate verdict predates the gate and is never bounced by
  // it (existing jobs and their files are untouched).
  if (contract.jobType === "research" && isResearchGateTask(task) && task.gradingStatus !== null) {
    const gateRows = await loadClaimGate(ctx, task.id);
    const recon = computeReconciliation(gateRows.manifest, gateRows.grades);
    if (recon.status === "incomplete" && !currentResultText.includes("GRADING INCOMPLETE")) {
      violations.push(`the claim-check grading is incomplete — ${recon.incompleteIds.length} of ${recon.manifestCount} claims unaccounted for (${recon.incompleteIds.join(", ") || "none recorded"}) — but the brief carries no grading-incomplete banner listing those claim IDs with the incomplete count stated in plain words`);
    }
  }
  return violations;
}

// Plan-shape receipts: how a bound job's planned steps measure against its
// contract — which steps exist, which are image steps, whether any brief
// carries the PP voice template it should not, and whether every brief
// carries the contract text. Used by check_outcome_contract.
const CONTRACT_EXPECTED_STEPS: Partial<Record<JobTypeValue, string[]>> = {
  research: ["walter", "peter", "peter", "scout"],
  x_posts: ["olivia"],
  perfectly_paranoid: ["scout", "quill", "forge"],
  market_briefing: ["ledger", "scout"],
  creative_package: ["quill", "forge"],
  client_report: ["maria", "quill"],
};

function planCheckForTask(task: typeof schema.tasks.$inferSelect, briefs: Array<typeof schema.briefs.$inferSelect>): { steps: Array<{ assignee: string; stage: string | null; title: string; isImageStep: boolean; carriesContract: boolean }>; violations: string[] } {
  const contract = contractForTask(task);
  const current = briefs.filter((brief) => brief.revision === task.revision).sort((a, b) => a.stepIndex - b.stepIndex || a.createdAt.getTime() - b.createdAt.getTime());
  const steps = current.map((brief) => ({
    assignee: brief.assignee,
    stage: brief.pipelineStage ?? null,
    title: brief.title,
    isImageStep: isImageProductionStep({ assignee: brief.assignee, title: brief.title, instructions: brief.notes }),
    carriesContract: brief.notes.includes("OUTCOME CONTRACT —"),
  }));
  const violations: string[] = [];
  if (!contract) return { steps, violations };
  const imageForbidden = contract.imageRule === "none" || (contract.imageRule === "brief" && !contract.imageAllowed);
  for (const step of steps) {
    if (imageForbidden && step.isImageStep) violations.push(`an image step is planned (“${step.title}”) — this job's contract forbids image steps`);
    if (contract.hashtagRule !== "required" && isFinisherStep({ title: step.title })) violations.push(`a finisher step is planned (“${step.title}”) — this job's contract forbids finisher steps`);
    if (!step.carriesContract) violations.push(`a brief (“${step.title}”) does not carry the outcome contract text`);
  }
  if (!contract.ppVoiceAllowed && current.some((brief) => /PERFECTLY PARANOID VOICE — LOCKED/.test(brief.notes) || brief.notes.includes("NASA would like to send people to Mars"))) {
    violations.push("a brief carries the Perfectly Paranoid voice template — a non-PP job's briefs must not contain it");
  }
  if (contract.jobType === "perfectly_paranoid" && !steps.some((step) => step.isImageStep)) {
    violations.push("the Perfectly Paranoid pipeline has no image step — Tom → Johnny → Nik always ends with Nik's image");
  }
  const expected = CONTRACT_EXPECTED_STEPS[contract.jobType];
  if (expected) {
    const actual = current.filter((brief) => !(brief.pipelineStage === "intake" && brief.assignee === "maria")).map((brief) => brief.assignee);
    if (actual.join(",") !== expected.join(",")) violations.push(`the planned steps (${actual.join(" → ") || "none"}) do not match this contract's steps (${expected.join(" → ")})`);
  }
  return { steps, violations };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// CLAIM COMPLETENESS GATE (Lab Efficiency Programme Change 1, 2026-10-23 —
// Alex's ruling: CLEAR WITH CONDITIONS; closes the benchmark's partial-pass
// hole mechanically, at the claim-check → synthesis boundary).
//
// The failure this fixes: the claim-check stage could quietly stop halfway
// (the benchmark found 20 claims ungraded across five passes) and nothing
// downstream could tell — synthesis drafted over a partial grading and the
// brief read as fully checked. The gate makes completeness a mechanical
// property, not a model's promise:
//
// 1. MANIFEST FIRST. When claim-check begins, every extracted claim is
//    recorded (save_claim_manifest) with a stable ID — CC-001, CC-002, …
//    in extraction order — its exact text, its source references, and a
//    role tag (central / decision-critical / supporting / contextual).
//    The manifest is written to claim-manifest.md in the job folder and is
//    immutable per job: re-saving the identical manifest is a no-op, a
//    different one is a reconciliation failure.
// 2. CHUNKED GRADING, SAFE RESUME. Grades are saved in deterministic
//    chunks of at most 15 claims (chunk N covers manifest positions
//    N*15+1 … N*15+15 in order) via save_claim_grade_chunk, persisted as
//    each chunk completes into claim-grades.md. Re-saving a chunk's grades
//    with the same dispositions is an idempotent no-op (resume never
//    duplicates); a different disposition for an ID that already has one
//    is a conflicting overwrite — rejected as a reconciliation failure.
// 3. ONE TERMINAL DISPOSITION PER CLAIM: STRONG, SUPPORTED, SHAKY,
//    MISFRAMED (the four-test grades — definitions unchanged),
//    UNTRACEABLE (no traceable source to grade: a claim the Verifier
//    labeled NOT VERIFIED), or UNGRADED (accounted-for, never a pass;
//    it always carries a specific recorded reason).
// 4. RECONCILIATION GATE. reconcileClaimGate mechanically compares the
//    manifest against the grade records: duplicate IDs, unknown IDs,
//    missing IDs, malformed records (an UNGRADED with no reason), and
//    conflicting grades are hard errors. On any failure — or any UNGRADED
>>>>> HEADLINE: CLAIM-GATE IMPLEMENTATION — original actions.ts lines 4200-4600 begin here (gate schemas, reconciliation, manifest/grade/provenance writes, measurement refresh, gate application, artifact writes) <<<<<
//    claim — the job is marked GRADING INCOMPLETE on the task record
//    (gradingStatus), shown on the job page and its Breakdown. Synthesis
//    may still draft, but set_brief_status stamps the grading-incomplete
//    banner (listing the unaccounted IDs, with the incomplete count in
//    plain words) onto the finished brief, and the outcome-contract check
//    bounces any research brief that claims completeness without it.
//
// Scope: research_case jobs only. Jobs created before this gate carry no
// manifest and no grading status — they are never reconciled, bannered,
// or bounced by it (their files and records are untouched).
export const CLAIM_CHUNK_SIZE = 15;
const claimRole = z.enum(["central", "decision-critical", "supporting", "contextual"]);
const claimDisposition = z.enum(["STRONG", "SUPPORTED", "SHAKY", "MISFRAMED", "UNTRACEABLE", "UNGRADED"]);
type ClaimDispositionValue = z.infer<typeof claimDisposition>;
const claimManifestEntryShape = z.object({
  claimId: z.string(), claimText: z.string(), sources: z.array(z.string()), role: claimRole,
});
const claimGradeEntryShape = z.object({
  claimId: z.string(), disposition: claimDisposition, reason: z.string(), chunkIndex: z.number().int().nonnegative(),
});
const claimReconciliationShape = z.object({
  status: z.enum(["complete", "incomplete", "none"]),
  manifestCount: z.number().int().nonnegative(), gradedCount: z.number().int().nonnegative(), chunkCount: z.number().int().nonnegative(),
  counts: z.object({
    STRONG: z.number().int().nonnegative(), SUPPORTED: z.number().int().nonnegative(), SHAKY: z.number().int().nonnegative(),
    MISFRAMED: z.number().int().nonnegative(), UNTRACEABLE: z.number().int().nonnegative(), UNGRADED: z.number().int().nonnegative(),
  }),
  missingIds: z.array(z.string()), ungradedIds: z.array(z.string()), unknownIds: z.array(z.string()), incompleteIds: z.array(z.string()),
  errors: z.array(z.string()), banner: z.string().nullable(), checkedAt: z.string().nullable(),
});
type ClaimReconciliation = z.infer<typeof claimReconciliationShape>;
const claimGradingStateShape = z.object({
  taskId: z.string(), manifest: z.array(claimManifestEntryShape), grades: z.array(claimGradeEntryShape), reconciliation: claimReconciliationShape,
  // Change 2: the gathering mode, every source's provenance record, and
  // the measurement block ride with the gate state — the manifest's
  // source references resolve to these provenance records, so a reader
  // can see what kind of source stands behind any claim.
  gatheringMode: gatheringMode, provenance: z.array(sourceProvenanceShape), measurements: labMeasurementsShape,
});
type ClaimGradingState = z.infer<typeof claimGradingStateShape>;
const claimManifestResult = z.discriminatedUnion("ok", [
  z.object({ ok: z.literal(true), manifest: z.array(claimManifestEntryShape), reconciliation: claimReconciliationShape }),
  z.object({ ok: z.literal(false), error: z.string(), reconciliation: claimReconciliationShape.nullable() }),
]);
const claimGradeChunkResult = z.discriminatedUnion("ok", [
  z.object({ ok: z.literal(true), saved: z.number().int().nonnegative(), alreadyRecorded: z.number().int().nonnegative(), reconciliation: claimReconciliationShape }),
  z.object({ ok: z.literal(false), error: z.string(), reconciliation: claimReconciliationShape.nullable() }),
]);
const sourceProvenanceResult = z.discriminatedUnion("ok", [
  z.object({ ok: z.literal(true), provenance: z.array(sourceProvenanceShape), measurements: labMeasurementsShape }),
  z.object({ ok: z.literal(false), error: z.string() }),
]);

export function claimIdForPosition(position: number): string {
  return `CC-${String(position + 1).padStart(3, "0")}`;
}

function parseSourceRefs(raw: string): string[] {
  try {
    const parsed = JSON.parse(raw) as unknown;
    return Array.isArray(parsed) ? parsed.filter((value): value is string => typeof value === "string") : [];
  } catch { return []; }
}

type ManifestRow = typeof schema.claimManifestEntries.$inferSelect;
type GradeRow = typeof schema.claimGrades.$inferSelect;
type ProvenanceRow = typeof schema.sourceProvenance.$inferSelect;
type LabMeasurements = z.infer<typeof labMeasurementsShape>;

async function loadClaimGate(ctx: Ctx, taskId: string): Promise<{ manifest: ManifestRow[]; grades: GradeRow[] }> {
  const db = ctx.db<typeof schema>();
  const [manifest, grades] = await Promise.all([
    db.select().from(schema.claimManifestEntries).where(eq(schema.claimManifestEntries.taskId, taskId)).orderBy(schema.claimManifestEntries.position),
    db.select().from(schema.claimGrades).where(eq(schema.claimGrades.taskId, taskId)),
  ]);
  grades.sort((a, b) => a.claimId.localeCompare(b.claimId));
  return { manifest, grades };
}

async function loadProvenance(ctx: Ctx, taskId: string): Promise<ProvenanceRow[]> {
  const db = ctx.db<typeof schema>();
  const rows = await db.select().from(schema.sourceProvenance).where(eq(schema.sourceProvenance.taskId, taskId));
  rows.sort((a, b) => a.sourceRef.localeCompare(b.sourceRef));
  return rows;
}

function provenanceDto(row: ProvenanceRow): z.infer<typeof sourceProvenanceShape> {
  const docType = sourceDocType.safeParse(row.docType);
  const tier = sourceTier.safeParse(row.tier);
  const independence = sourceIndependence.safeParse(row.independence);
  return {
    sourceRef: row.sourceRef, publisher: row.publisher,
    docType: docType.success ? docType.data : "other",
    vintage: row.vintage, tier: tier.success ? tier.data : "secondary",
    independence: independence.success ? independence.data : "independent",
    independenceNote: row.independenceNote, primaryRef: row.primaryRef ?? null, primaryAttempt: row.primaryAttempt,
    createdAt: row.createdAt.toISOString(), updatedAt: row.updatedAt.toISOString(),
  };
}

// The measurement block (Change 2) — a pure computation over the stored
// manifest, grade, and provenance records, so the Breakdown, the stored
// record, and the A/B comparison all report the identical numbers.
// Rates are fractions of the total claim count (null when there are no
// claims). Weak-source share: of the claims that resolve to at least one
// provenance record, the share whose best available source is secondary
// (no primary-tier record among the claim's sources). A claim with no
// provenance record at all is not counted either way — the share never
// guesses at a source nobody recorded.
export function computeLabMeasurements(manifest: ManifestRow[], grades: GradeRow[], provenance: ProvenanceRow[], mode: "standard" | "tiered", computedAt: string | null): LabMeasurements {
  const totalClaims = manifest.length;
  const manifestIds = new Set(manifest.map((entry) => entry.claimId));
  const gradedById = new Map<string, GradeRow>();
  for (const grade of grades) if (manifestIds.has(grade.claimId)) gradedById.set(grade.claimId, grade);
  const counts: Record<z.infer<typeof dispositionValue>, number> = { STRONG: 0, SUPPORTED: 0, SHAKY: 0, MISFRAMED: 0, UNTRACEABLE: 0, UNGRADED: 0 };
  let gradedCount = 0;
  for (const grade of gradedById.values()) {
    counts[grade.disposition] += 1;
    if (grade.disposition !== "UNGRADED") gradedCount += 1;
  }
  const rate = (count: number): number | null => (totalClaims > 0 ? count / totalClaims : null);
  const byRef = new Map(provenance.map((record) => [record.sourceRef, record]));
  let claimsWithProvenance = 0;
  let weakSourceClaims = 0;
  let weakSourceEligible = 0;
  for (const entry of manifest) {
    const records = parseSourceRefs(entry.sourceRefs).map((ref) => byRef.get(ref)).filter((record): record is ProvenanceRow => record !== undefined);
    if (records.length > 0) claimsWithProvenance += 1;
    if (records.length === 0) continue;
    weakSourceEligible += 1;
    if (!records.some((record) => record.tier === "primary")) weakSourceClaims += 1;
  }
  return {
    gatheringMode: mode,
    totalClaims, gradedCount,
    completenessRate: rate(gradedCount),
    dispositions: (Object.keys(counts) as Array<z.infer<typeof dispositionValue>>).map((disposition) => ({ disposition, count: counts[disposition], rate: rate(counts[disposition]) })),
    unaccountedCount: totalClaims - gradedById.size,
    provenanceRecords: provenance.length, claimsWithProvenance,
    weakSourceClaims, weakSourceEligible,
    weakSourceShare: weakSourceEligible > 0 ? weakSourceClaims / weakSourceEligible : null,
    computedAt,
  };
}

// Persist the measurement block onto the job's stored record. Called
// whenever the manifest, the grades, or the provenance records change;
// it writes ONLY the lab_measurements column — grading state, the gate,
// and every other record are untouched.
async function refreshLabMeasurements(ctx: Ctx, taskId: string): Promise<LabMeasurements | null> {
  const db = ctx.db<typeof schema>();
  const taskRows = await db.select().from(schema.tasks).where(eq(schema.tasks.id, taskId)).limit(1);
  const task = taskRows[0];
  if (!task || !isResearchGateTask(task)) return null;
  const [{ manifest, grades }, provenance] = await Promise.all([loadClaimGate(ctx, taskId), loadProvenance(ctx, taskId)]);
  const measurements = computeLabMeasurements(manifest, grades, provenance, task.gatheringMode === "tiered" ? "tiered" : "standard", new Date().toISOString());
  await db.update(schema.tasks).set({ labMeasurements: JSON.stringify(measurements) }).where(eq(schema.tasks.id, taskId));
  return measurements;
}

function sourceProvenanceMarkdown(task: typeof schema.tasks.$inferSelect, provenance: ProvenanceRow[]): string {
  const docTypeLabels: Record<string, string> = {
    primary_document: "Primary document", official_statistics: "Official statistics", vendor_page: "Vendor page",
    compilation_roundup: "Compilation or roundup", news_report: "News report", other: "Other",
  };
  const independenceLabels: Record<string, string> = {
    independent: "Independent source", same_owner_family: "Same-owner family as another gathered source", syndicated_copy: "Syndicated or copied version of another source",
  };
  const lines = [
    `# Source provenance — ${task.title}`,
    "",
    "## In plain words",
    `Every source gathered for this job carries a provenance record: who published it, what kind of document it is, its date or vintage, whether it is primary or secondary material, and how independent it is of the other sources. Provenance is recorded and reported only — it never changes how a claim is graded.`,
    "",
    ...provenance.flatMap((record) => [
      `### ${record.sourceRef}`,
      `Publisher: ${record.publisher} · Type: ${docTypeLabels[record.docType] ?? record.docType} · Vintage: ${record.vintage || "not recorded"} · Tier: ${record.tier === "primary" ? "Primary" : "Secondary"}`,
      `Independence: ${independenceLabels[record.independence] ?? record.independence}${record.independenceNote ? ` — ${record.independenceNote}` : ""}`,
      ...(record.primaryRef ? [`Primary source it derives from: ${record.primaryRef}`] : []),
      ...(record.primaryAttempt ? [`Primary retrieval (tiered gathering): ${record.primaryAttempt}`] : []),
      "",
    ]),
  ];
  return lines.join("\n");
}

// The banner every grading-incomplete brief must carry, word for word the
// same wherever the server stamps or checks it: prominent, it names every
// unaccounted claim ID, and its tally sentence states the incomplete count
// in plain words.
export function gradingIncompleteBanner(recon: ClaimReconciliation): string {
  if (recon.manifestCount === 0) {
    return [
      `> ⚠ **GRADING INCOMPLETE — this brief is NOT fully checked.** No claim manifest was recorded for this job, so none of its claims could be accounted for in the claim-check.`,
      `> Grading tally (incomplete): no claims were graded under the claim completeness gate — the grading for this brief is incomplete in full, and its verdict rests only on claims the Claim-checker graded STRONG or SUPPORTED in the claim-check record.`,
    ].join("\n");
  }
  if (recon.incompleteIds.length === 0) {
    return [
      `> ⚠ **GRADING INCOMPLETE — this brief is NOT fully checked.** Every claim has a grade, but the grading records could not be reconciled (${recon.errors[0] ?? "a reconciliation error was recorded"}), so the grading cannot be trusted as complete.`,
      `> Grading tally (incomplete): ${recon.counts.STRONG} strong, ${recon.counts.SUPPORTED} supported, ${recon.counts.SHAKY} shaky, ${recon.counts.MISFRAMED} misframed, ${recon.counts.UNTRACEABLE} untraceable, ${recon.counts.UNGRADED} ungraded — recorded, but not reconciled. The verdict below rests only on the strong and supported claims that were graded.`,
    ].join("\n");
  }
  const ids = recon.incompleteIds.join(", ");
  const unaccounted = recon.incompleteIds.length;
  return [
    `> ⚠ **GRADING INCOMPLETE — this brief is NOT fully checked.** ${unaccounted} of ${recon.manifestCount} claims could not be accounted for in the claim-check: ${ids}.`,
    `> Grading tally (incomplete): ${recon.counts.STRONG} strong, ${recon.counts.SUPPORTED} supported, ${recon.counts.SHAKY} shaky, ${recon.counts.MISFRAMED} misframed, ${recon.counts.UNTRACEABLE} untraceable, ${recon.counts.UNGRADED} ungraded — and ${unaccounted} ${unaccounted === 1 ? "claim is" : "claims are"} unaccounted for, so this tally does not cover every claim in the case. The verdict below rests only on the strong and supported claims that were graded.`,
  ].join("\n");
}

// The mechanical reconciliation itself — pure over the stored records, so
// the read path (Breakdown), the worker-facing actions, and the
// set_brief_status gate all run the identical check.
export function computeReconciliation(manifest: ManifestRow[], grades: GradeRow[], extraErrors: string[] = []): ClaimReconciliation {
  const errors = [...extraErrors];
  const manifestIds = manifest.map((entry) => entry.claimId);
  const manifestSet = new Set(manifestIds);
  if (manifestSet.size !== manifestIds.length) errors.push("The claim manifest itself contains duplicate claim IDs.");
  const counts: Record<ClaimDispositionValue, number> = { STRONG: 0, SUPPORTED: 0, SHAKY: 0, MISFRAMED: 0, UNTRACEABLE: 0, UNGRADED: 0 };
  const gradedIds = new Set<string>();
  const unknownIds: string[] = [];
  const ungradedIds: string[] = [];
  for (const grade of grades) {
    if (gradedIds.has(grade.claimId)) errors.push(`Duplicate grade record for ${grade.claimId} — a claim must end with exactly one disposition.`);
    gradedIds.add(grade.claimId);
    if (!manifestSet.has(grade.claimId)) { unknownIds.push(grade.claimId); continue; }
    counts[grade.disposition] += 1;
    if (grade.disposition === "UNGRADED") {
      ungradedIds.push(grade.claimId);
      if (!grade.reason.trim()) errors.push(`${grade.claimId} is UNGRADED with no recorded reason — an UNGRADED disposition requires a specific reason (malformed grade record).`);
    }
  }
  if (unknownIds.length > 0) errors.push(`Grade records name claims that are not in the manifest: ${unknownIds.join(", ")} (unknown IDs).`);
  const missingIds = manifestIds.filter((id) => !gradedIds.has(id));
  const order = new Map(manifestIds.map((id, index) => [id, index]));
  const byManifestOrder = (a: string, b: string) => (order.get(a) ?? 9999) - (order.get(b) ?? 9999);
  const incompleteIds = [...missingIds, ...ungradedIds].sort(byManifestOrder);
  const chunkCount = grades.length > 0 ? Math.max(...grades.map((grade) => grade.chunkIndex)) + 1 : 0;
  const base: ClaimReconciliation = {
    status: "none", manifestCount: manifest.length, gradedCount: grades.length, chunkCount, counts,
    missingIds, ungradedIds, unknownIds, incompleteIds, errors, banner: null, checkedAt: null,
  };
  if (manifest.length === 0) {
    if (errors.length > 0) base.status = "incomplete";
    return base;
  }
  base.status = errors.length === 0 && missingIds.length === 0 && ungradedIds.length === 0 && unknownIds.length === 0 ? "complete" : "incomplete";
  if (base.status === "incomplete") base.banner = gradingIncompleteBanner(base);
  return base;
}

function claimGradingState(taskId: string, manifest: ManifestRow[], grades: GradeRow[], reconciliation: ClaimReconciliation, lab?: { provenance: ProvenanceRow[]; mode: "standard" | "tiered" }): ClaimGradingState {
  const gradeById = new Map(grades.map((grade) => [grade.claimId, grade]));
  const provenance = lab?.provenance ?? [];
  const mode = lab?.mode ?? "standard";
  return {
    taskId,
    manifest: manifest.map((entry) => ({ claimId: entry.claimId, claimText: entry.claimText, sources: parseSourceRefs(entry.sourceRefs), role: (claimRole.safeParse(entry.role).success ? entry.role : "contextual") as z.infer<typeof claimRole> })),
    grades: manifest.filter((entry) => gradeById.has(entry.claimId)).map((entry) => {
      const grade = gradeById.get(entry.claimId) as GradeRow;
      return { claimId: grade.claimId, disposition: grade.disposition, reason: grade.reason, chunkIndex: grade.chunkIndex };
    }),
    reconciliation,
    gatheringMode: mode,
    provenance: provenance.map(provenanceDto),
    measurements: computeLabMeasurements(manifest, grades, provenance, mode, null),
  };
}

// Load everything a full grading-state response needs — manifest,
// grades, provenance records, and the job's gathering mode — in one go.
async function loadLabExtras(ctx: Ctx, taskId: string): Promise<{ provenance: ProvenanceRow[]; mode: "standard" | "tiered" }> {
  const db = ctx.db<typeof schema>();
  const [provenance, taskRows] = await Promise.all([
    loadProvenance(ctx, taskId),
    db.select().from(schema.tasks).where(eq(schema.tasks.id, taskId)).limit(1),
  ]);
  return { provenance, mode: taskRows[0]?.gatheringMode === "tiered" ? "tiered" : "standard" };
}

function emptyClaimGradingState(taskId: string): ClaimGradingState {
  return claimGradingState(taskId, [], [], computeReconciliation([], []));
}

function claimManifestMarkdown(task: typeof schema.tasks.$inferSelect, manifest: ManifestRow[]): string {
  const lines = [
    `# Claim manifest — ${task.title}`,
    "",
    "## In plain words",
    `This is the fixed list of every claim the claim-check must grade on this job: ${manifest.length} claims, each with a stable ID that never changes across retries. The claim-check is complete only when every ID below has exactly one grade.`,
    "",
    ...manifest.flatMap((entry) => [
      `### ${entry.claimId} — ${entry.role}`,
      entry.claimText,
      `Sources: ${parseSourceRefs(entry.sourceRefs).join(" · ") || "none recorded"}`,
      "",
    ]),
  ];
  return lines.join("\n");
}

function claimGradesMarkdown(task: typeof schema.tasks.$inferSelect, manifest: ManifestRow[], grades: GradeRow[], recon: ClaimReconciliation): string {
  const chunks = new Map<number, GradeRow[]>();
  for (const grade of grades) {
    const list = chunks.get(grade.chunkIndex) ?? [];
    list.push(grade);
    chunks.set(grade.chunkIndex, list);
  }
  const lines = [
    `# Claim grades — ${task.title}`,
    "",
    "## In plain words",
    recon.status === "complete"
      ? `Every one of the ${recon.manifestCount} claims in the manifest has exactly one grade: ${recon.counts.STRONG} strong, ${recon.counts.SUPPORTED} supported, ${recon.counts.SHAKY} shaky, ${recon.counts.MISFRAMED} misframed, ${recon.counts.UNTRACEABLE} untraceable. The grading reconciles — nothing is missing, duplicated, or unknown.`
      : `GRADING INCOMPLETE — ${recon.incompleteIds.length} of ${recon.manifestCount} claims are unaccounted for (${recon.incompleteIds.join(", ") || "none recorded"}). This job must not be represented as fully checked.`,
    "",
    ...[...chunks.entries()].sort((a, b) => a[0] - b[0]).flatMap(([chunkIndex, chunkGrades]) => [
      `## Chunk ${chunkIndex + 1} (${chunkGrades.length} claims)`,
      ...chunkGrades.sort((a, b) => a.claimId.localeCompare(b.claimId)).map((grade) => `- ${grade.claimId} — ${grade.disposition} — ${grade.reason}`),
      "",
    ]),
    ...(recon.missingIds.length > 0 ? [`## Not yet graded`, ...recon.missingIds.map((id) => `- ${id} — no grade recorded`), ""] : []),
    `Manifest claims: ${recon.manifestCount} · Grades recorded: ${recon.gradedCount} · Chunks completed: ${recon.chunkCount}`,
    ...(manifest.length > 0 && recon.manifestCount !== manifest.length ? [`Manifest rows read back: ${manifest.length}`] : []),
  ];
  return lines.join("\n");
}

// Run the gate and persist its verdict on the job record. Fail-closed: a
// job whose grading state cannot be reconciled — including a research job
// that reaches a gate point with no manifest at all — is marked
// GRADING INCOMPLETE, never passed on trust.
async function applyClaimGate(ctx: Ctx, taskId: string, extraErrors: string[] = []): Promise<ClaimReconciliation> {
  const db = ctx.db<typeof schema>();
  const { manifest, grades } = await loadClaimGate(ctx, taskId);
  const errors = [...extraErrors];
  if (manifest.length === 0) errors.push("No claim manifest was recorded for this job — the claim-check cannot be reconciled without one.");
  const recon = computeReconciliation(manifest, grades, errors);
  if (recon.status === "none") recon.status = "incomplete";
  if (recon.status === "incomplete" && !recon.banner) recon.banner = gradingIncompleteBanner(recon);
  recon.checkedAt = new Date().toISOString();
  await db.update(schema.tasks).set({ gradingStatus: recon.status, gradingDetail: JSON.stringify(recon), gradingUpdatedAt: new Date() }).where(eq(schema.tasks.id, taskId));
  // Change 2: the measurement block is refreshed alongside the gate
  // verdict — an additive write to lab_measurements only; the gate's own
  // behaviour is exactly as Change 1 left it.
  await refreshLabMeasurements(ctx, taskId);
  return recon;
}

async function writeClaimGateFiles(ctx: Ctx, task: typeof schema.tasks.$inferSelect): Promise<void> {
  try {
    const { manifest, grades } = await loadClaimGate(ctx, task.id);
    if (manifest.length > 0) {
      await ctx.executePrivileged(privileged.writeClaimGateFile, { taskId: task.id, fileName: "claim-manifest.md", text: claimManifestMarkdown(task, manifest) });
    }
    if (grades.length > 0 || manifest.length > 0) {
      const recon = computeReconciliation(manifest, grades);
      await ctx.executePrivileged(privileged.writeClaimGateFile, { taskId: task.id, fileName: "claim-grades.md", text: claimGradesMarkdown(task, manifest, grades, recon) });
    }
  } catch { /* The structured records are the gate's authority; the files are their artifact copy. */ }
}

function isResearchGateTask(task: typeof schema.tasks.$inferSelect | null | undefined): boolean {
  return Boolean(task && (task.pipeline === "research_case" || task.jobType === "research"));
}

      const plan = planCheckForTask(task, briefs);
      const contract = contractForTask(task);
